articles.title: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Bank measures can only limit damage from ‘digital arrest’ scams

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation, during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams, that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.

Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.
Editorial Context: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Suboptimal outcomes: On social security boards for unorganised, gig, platform workers
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Social security concerns of unorganised sector workers remain

One year after the implementation of the Code on Social Security , the Union Labour Ministry has constituted the National Social Security Boards for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers. The constitution of the boards, though delayed, is a welcome step. However, the highly centralised nature of this mechanism may hinder its optimal outcomes. By design, the Union Government controls both the Boards: they will be chaired by Union Minister for Labour Mansukh Mandaviya. The Board for Unorganised Sector Workers will have 40 members, nominated by the Union Government. They include seven members representing unorganised sector workers and seven members representing employers of the unorganised sector. Similarly, the Board for the welfare of gig and platform workers will have 22 members with five representatives each from the aggregators and the workers. But they have no significant representation of Central Trade Unions from the Opposition side or from the State Governments ruled by the Opposition. Labour is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and both the States and the Union must work together to improve the living standards of workers.

The International Labour Organization defines social security as the ‘protection that a society provides to individuals and households to ensure access to health care and to guarantee income security, particularly in cases of old age, unemployment, sickness, invalidity, work injury, maternity or loss of a breadwinner’. The Union Government claims that the country’s social security coverage has increased from 19% in 2015 to 64.3% in 2025, which is around 94 crore citizens. However, it is apparent that the unorganised and gig and platform workers, who make up more than 92% of the country’s total workforce, are far from enjoying any social security under this definition. Almost two decades ago, the National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector, headed by economist Arjun Sengupta, recommended a slew of measures to improve the social security of workers in the informal sector. The issues raised by the panel still remain unaddressed. A report prepared by Justice V. Gopala Gowda for the Keralam Government in March this year flagged certain anti-federal and anti-worker characteristics in the Social Security Code and suggested amendments. The Union Government should take the trade unions and the State Governments on board while creating new systems and mechanisms to address the social security concerns of the vast majority of workers.

Editorial Context: Suboptimal outcomes: On social security boards for unorganised, gig, platform workers. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Open to investigation: On the challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Public functionaries must not use privacy to seek exemption from scrutiny

The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases.

The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutory protection for their work, freedom of the press is constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a). The Court has also shielded newspapers from arbitrary state restrictions. However, growing mistrust of legacy media and the rise of independent content creators have made it difficult to determine who receives such protection. The Centre has also flagged this concern. Yet, carving out distinct categories is no easy task — a 2026 Reuters Institute report shows that the proportion of 18- to 24-year-olds identifying social media as their primary source of news rose from 21% in 2015 to 39% in 2025. A purely legalistic determination of these competing concerns may perhaps prove too onerous. Stakeholders must build consensus on a mutually acceptable framework where public functionaries and those handling public funds are not insulated from scrutiny under the guise of privacy. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw’s indication that he would meet editors is a welcome step towards consensus.

The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases.
• The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutory protection for their work, freedom of the press is constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a). The Court has also shielded newspapers from arbitrary state restrictions. However, growing mistrust of legacy media and the rise of independent content creators have made it difficult to determine who receives such protection. The Centre has also flagged this concern. Yet, carving out distinct categories is no easy task — a 2026 Reuters Institute report shows that the proportion of 18- to 24-year-olds identifying social media as their primary source of news rose from 21% in 2015 to 39% in 2025. A purely legalistic determination of these competing concerns may perhaps prove too onerous. Stakeholders must build consensus on a mutually acceptable framework where public functionaries and those handling public funds are not insulated from scrutiny under the guise of privacy. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw’s indication that he would meet editors is a welcome step towards consensus.

articles.title: Deemed ineligible: On the Supreme Court and SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court has pointed to the SIR’s flaws by design

At Wednesday’s hearing of a petition on the Delhi SIR in the Supreme Court, Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked questions that cut to the heart of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s SIR of electoral rolls . If an existing voter was “lax, inert or did not respond” to enumeration forms, was that a ground for the ECI to “forfeit his or her right to vote forever”? The Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the ECI was in “error” to force such voters, struck off for not returning enumeration forms, to reapply on Form 6 as if they were new voters. It asked why voters who had shifted residences could not just disclose details and why deleted voters could not fill enumeration forms belatedly. This is the central design flaw of the SIR as it shifts the burden of enrolment from the state to the elector, including those who have voted before, and treats a mere change of address as ground for deletion. The share of draft deletions recorded as “shifted” or “absent” rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in States/Union Territories in Phase 3. In Karnataka, about 84 lakh electors were deleted, marked as “shifted” or “absent” during enumeration. But only a net of 8.2 lakh, including new electors, were added during the claims phase, with the final roll being 64.5 lakh short of the projected adult population. Requiring moved voters to re-register as fresh applicants defeats the ECI’s historic mandate of widening the franchise, which was inherent in the 2002-03 intensive revision, where enumerators enrolled shifted voters at their new homes and the Chief Electoral Officer reconciled the old entries.

Justice Bagchi also mentioned that the Bihar judgment was not a “binding precedent” and that the legality of “logical discrepancy” checks, allowed only as an “interim arrangement” in West Bengal, had not been finally adjudicated. No statute or rule provides for judging a voter’s eligibility on the basis of family size or the age gap between voters and parents, which were two of the ECI’s ludicrous and algorithm-driven “logical discrepancy” checks. In West Bengal these checks resulted in massive disenfranchisement and The Hindu’s analysis found that in Delhi, Muslims were disproportionately flagged. But the Court should not merely issue managerial fixes such as extended deadlines or displaying printed lists in blocks, as it has in the past. The final SIR rolls are erroneous as deletions flowed from a flawed design rather than just lapses by the ECI. The dead and duplicate entries that the SIR identified should be removed and newly eligible electors added. Voters wrongly removed from draft rolls must be included again. The larger questions over the Commission’s SIR conduct and how its members are appointed must also be settled.

articles.title: Clinging on: On Netanyahu and the Israel elections
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Netanyahu’s continuance will be bad news for Israel and the region

Benjamin Netanyahu was at the centre of Israel’s October 27 elections. For Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw a genocidal war in Gaza following Hamas’s October 7 attack , the election was the biggest test of his political career. For the Opposition, which promised to hold him accountable for the failures of October 7 and end the country’s “forever wars”, the election offered an opportunity to oust him from power. The results, however, sent a mixed message. With 85.6% of the votes counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has lost its majority but is still the largest bloc . His Likud party is projected to win 26 seats, while its main rival Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to secure 21. Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, the far-right extremist parties in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, demonstrated their continued strength, winning 13 seats between them. The dark horse, however, could be the Arab parties — the Joint List is projected to win 12 seats while the United Arab List (Ra’am) could secure seven seats. With neither bloc commanding a majority, the Arab parties could propel the opposition coalition to power. But the big question is whether the anti-Netanyahu coalition is ready to join hands with the Arab parties, which have historically been kept on the margins of Israel’ s power politics.

Mr. Netanyahu’s central promise has been that only he can guarantee Israel’s security. Yet, the October 7 attack took place on his watch and he has refused to take responsibility for the failures that led to it. A wanted man by the International Criminal Court, he has repeated, before and after October 7, that a Palestine state would not be formed while he is in power. His war on Gaza has killed over 70,000 Palestinians, including 20,000 children, and displaced the region’s population. Israel’s brutal occupation machinery has also expanded and tightened its control of the West Bank, while settler terrorists have unleashed violence on Palestinian households. His war on Iran has been a disaster, with global economic consequences. Mr. Netanyahu has sought to portray his wars as bold, necessary moves to protect Israel, while exploiting Israelis’ security concerns for political gain. He may not be voted out immediately, but his failure to secure a majority and the decline in his party’s popularity are significant. The Opposition should take its cue from the results and form a broad coalition with the Arab parties. It should restore accountability in governance, revisit his unchecked militarism and rebuild ties with the world. If Mr. Netanyahu continues to cling to power, it would be bad news for Israel and the region.

articles.title: Hunker down: On Cyclone Arnab, its landfall
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Proactive governance kept the casualties low after Cyclone Arnab

Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.

Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

articles.title: Uttam wants Tummidihatti alignments keeping in mind eco issues, asks for realistic solutions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: At the proposed FRL of 152 metres, storage capacity would increase to 5.697 tmc ft from 2.182 tmc ft at 148 metres, more than doubling the storage potential, the Minister said

Minister for Irrigation and Civil Supplies N. Uttam Kumar Reddy on Saturday instructed officials to work out technically-sound and pragmatic solutions to the concerns being raised by Maharashtra over the proposed barrage at Tummidihatti across the Pranahita river with 152 metres height (full reservoir level), particularly on the submergence and environmental issues involved.

As a follow up to the recent talks with Maharashtra government on the barrage proposal, the Minister reviewed the project’s technical aspects and alignments, emphasising the need for a comprehensive assessment of the land likely to be affected or submerged at different reservoir levels.

He asked the officials to prepare detailed maps identifying the riverbed areas, forest and eco-sensitive zones, protected core areas, revenue lands and human habitations to establish the actual extent of submergence. He highlighted that engineering modifications should be examined to minimise environmental impact and address Maharashtra’s concerns without compromising the project’s irrigation objectives.

He pointed out that Telangana was seeking to raise the barrage’s FRL from 148 metres, as agreed between the two States in 2016, to 152 metres to improve water storage and utilisation. The proposal was discussed during the October 26 meeting between Chief Ministers A. Revanth Reddy and Devendra Fadnavis, along with the Irrigation and Water Resources Ministers and officials of the two States in Mumbai.

The barrage was being proposed to divert 77 tmc ft of water and was expected to support irrigating over 5.85 lakh acres across seven districts of Telangana through an integrated system involving Sundilla Barrage and Sripada Yellampalli Project.
At the proposed FRL of 152 metres, storage capacity would increase to 5.697 tmc ft from 2.182 tmc ft at 148 metres, more than doubling the storage potential.

articles.title: Fuel surcharge of 4 paise per unit for bi-monthly billed consumers and 5 paise for monthly billed consumers in November
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The surcharge is meant to recover additional spending in power purchases in September this year
The Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) will collect 4 paise per unit from bi-monthly billed consumers and 5 paise per unit from monthly billed consumers as fuel surcharge in November.

The surcharge is meant to recover additional spending on power purchases in September this year. The surcharge will be applicable to all consumers except domestic consumers with connected load of and below 1,000 watts and monthly consumption of and below 40 units. Green tariff consumers also are exempted from this levy.
The levy is aimed at recouping the additional spending on power purchases from 12 central generating stations and six independent power producers (IPP) across the country.

The Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions for determination of Tariff) (First Amendment) Regulations allow a distribution business/ licensee to adjust, by recovery or refund, the fuel surcharge on a monthly basis.

articles.title: 'Chalo Dilli' protests: Rahul Gandhi assures 'legal action against PM Modi'; Kharge says 'we're not afraid to fight' | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ICC General Secretary KC Venugopal said the INDIA bloc’s mega rally was a strong response to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. He accused the BJP leadership of undermining democracy by misusing the office of the Chief Election Commissioner.
Nadda decries the INDIA rally as foolish drama, predicting it seals Congress's political downfall amid accusations of anti-democracy plots.

Addressing the INDIA bloc’s mega rally, Rahul Gandhi accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of “stealing votes” and said legal action would follow. He asserted that the Opposition would ensure accountability and justice.

Addressing the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, Rahul Gandhi said he harboured no personal enmity towards Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Amit Shah or CEC Gyanesh Kumar. He vowed that the Opposition would reject violence and hatred while continuing its fight to protect the Constitution.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah said Delhi traders had repeatedly urged the Congress to postpone its November 1 rally until after Diwali, citing concerns over festival-season business.

Union Minister JP Nadda accused Rahul Gandhi of attempting to incite unrest and destabilise the elected government through the rally at Ramlila Maidan. He also invoked the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, accusing the Congress of having a dark record on the issue.

AISA president Neha Bora said that removing people’s names from electoral rolls denied them equal status and made them “second-class citizens”. She alleged that Muslims, women, Dalits, Adivasis and poor labourers were repeatedly asked to prove their citizenship.

Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi claimed that 15% of India’s voters were removed from electoral rolls after the 2024 elections, alleging that this made the election “illegal” and “stolen”. He said the Election Commission had made the claim. ANI/Congress

Rahul Gandhi alleged that votes had been stolen in Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Karnataka, as well as in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. He accused the BJP of using EVMs and manipulating voter lists by deleting and adding names. ANI/Congress
TMC chief Mamata Banerjee accused the BJP of “looting” Bengal and said her party would fight the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
“We will save democracy and bring it back,” she said at the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi. Banerjee added that the fight would continue through politics and democracy.

Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde criticised the INDIA bloc’s rally at Ramlila Maidan, alleging that its leaders were spreading a “fake narrative” and defaming Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

articles.title: UDP chief Metbah Lyngdoh resigns as Meghalaya Minister after all other MLAs joined BJP, NPP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The development followed a series of defections that saw eight of the UDP MLAs merge with the BJP in September and three others with the NPP, the Chief Minister's party, earlier this month

United Democratic Party president Metbah Lyngdoh resigned as a Minister in the Meghalaya Cabinet on Saturday (October 31, 2026), days after 11 of the party's 12 MLAs joined the BJP and the NPP, leaving him as the UDP's sole legislator in the State Assembly.
Mr. Lyngdoh said that he had submitted his resignation letter to Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma after assessing the prevailing political situation and recent developments within the party.

The development followed a series of defections that saw eight of the UDP MLAs merge with the BJP in September and three others with the NPP, the Chief Minister's party, earlier this month. The Speaker recognised both mergers, reducing the UDP's strength from 12 to one. Both BJP and UDP are constituents of the NPP-led Meghalaya Democratic Alliance.
Mr. Lyngdoh said the UDP's Central Executive Committee would deliberate on the developments and decide on the future course of action in consultation with party leaders and office-bearers.
Rejecting speculation that he was forced to resign, the UDP president maintained that the decision was voluntary.
He was in charge of the departments of power, textiles, water resources and taxation.

The political upheaval in the UDP came amid reported discontent within the party over leadership and organisational issues. The developments also followed a cabinet reshuffle in September 2025, when Metbah Lyngdoh and Lahkmen Rymbui replaced senior UDP leaders Paul Lyngdoh and Kyrmen Shylla as the party's representatives in the state cabinet.

The eight legislators who joined the BJP were Lahkmen Rymbui, Kyrmen Shylla, Pius Marwein, Mayralborn Syiem, Matthew Beyondstar Kurbah, Ollan Singh Suin, Balajied Kupar Synrem and Synshar Kupar Roy Lyngdoh Thabah.
The three who merged with the NPP were Paul Lyngdoh, Renikton Lyngdoh Tongkhar and Nujorki Sungoh.
The moves took the NPP's strength in the 60-member Assembly to 36, while the BJP's tally rose to 10.
The UDP had emerged as the second-largest party in the 2023 Meghalaya Assembly elections with 12 seats.

articles.title: Postponement of college exam for CM’s visit in Pudukottai triggers row
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: With Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay scheduled to visit Pudukottai on November 2, to inaugurate the new bus stand and distribute welfare measure, semester examinations scheduled for the day at the Kalaignar Karunanidhi Government Arts College for Women, an autonomous institution in the town, has been postponed, triggering a row.

The examinations in the college started on October 30 and are to conclude on November 19. However, the examinations scheduled on November 2 have been postponed apparently “keeping in mind the difficulty the students of the college may face in reaching the institution from the bus stand,” said the college authorities.

The exam scheduled on November 2 would be held on a later day. The college office would work as usual on November 2, the college authorities said. Several students of the college hail from the rural areas of the district.

Information about the postponement of the examination on November 2 was conveyed to the faculty members in the college group on a mobile messaging platform a couple of days ago and communicated to the students.
The Tamizhaga Vazhvurimai Katchi leader, T. Velmurugan, in a social media post expressed shock over the postponement of the examination at the college in view of the Chief Minister’s visit.

He condemned the postponement and wondered whether the Chief Minister’s visit was more important than the future of students. “It was the government’s responsibility to make arrangements for security and transportation for the official function. But, action affecting the education and examination of students could not be accepted,” he said.
Meanwhile, arrangements are under way for the Chief Minister’s programme in Pudukottai.

Minister for Labour Welfare and Skill Development J. Mohamed Farvas on Saturday said that the Chief Minister would inaugurate the new bus stand in Pudukottai and distribute welfare assistance to the beneficiaries. The function is to be held at the District Armed Reserve ground during which welfare assistance would be provided to 2,000 beneficiaries. Welfare assistance to the tune of Rs. 100 crore is to be given to 14,000 beneficiaries of Pudukottai district on that day, the Minister told reporters in Pudukottai.

articles.title: ‘You can break a stick, not a bundle’: From an IT couple to a hospital patient, citizens turn up for INDIA bloc rally
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Citizens, youth groups, farmers and political party workers gather ahead of the Ramlila Maidan rally, saying a united movement is needed to fight alleged vote theft and electoral roll irregularities

Thousands of protesters from across the country, representing political parties, youth organisations, women’s groups and farmers’ bodies, gathered at Minto Road in Delhi on Sunday (November 1, 2026) ahead of the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, seeking to strengthen the campaign against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Chalo Dilli protests: Follow LIVE updates from the Opposition rally on November 1, 2026

Ahead of the arrival of Opposition leaders, including Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, protesters raised slogans of “vote chori” and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the rollback of the SIR exercise.

Among those assembling at Minto Road were members of the Indian Youth Congress, Samajwadi Party, Rashtriya Janata Dal, National Students’ Union of India, Krantikari Yuva Sangathan and the All India Students’ Federation, among other groups.

The gathering also drew citizens (independent of parties) who said the coming together of various parties and the public had given the protests greater strength after several demonstrations against the SIR in recent weeks.

“You can break one stick easily, but if you bundle 10 sticks together, they cannot be broken. Today’s protest symbolises that bundle of sticks,” said Tejender, an IT employee who had arrived with his wife from Gurugram.

When asked why he had joined the demonstration on a Sunday afternoon, he said, “We are doing this for a better future for our children. The education system is in a bad state, healthcare facilities are lacking, and there are concerns over the misappropriation of votes. Our country has so many problems that need to be addressed. It is high time we all came together,” he said.
Mr. Tejender said the SIR exercise has disproportionately affected people who lacked the resources or awareness to navigate the documentation process.

“I am educated and was able to produce all the required documents, but a large section of the population is either uneducated or unaware of the process and is being targeted by the SIR of electoral rolls. Who will fight for them?” he asked.
Participants also said that the past protests ensured that fear of demonstrations was gradually receding.

“The earlier protests were a struggle by the youth and they have helped remove the fear of the police from people’s minds. I was scared earlier, many political parties were scared too. But after a series of consistent protests, that fear is no longer there,” said Anil S. Raj, an advocate who had attended previous demonstrations against the SIR.

Participants said earlier demonstrations had largely taken place in silos, with different groups raising concerns over the SIR separately. The INDIA bloc rally, they said, offered an opportunity to bring these voices together and build a broader movement.

articles.title: GST mop-up grows 23% to over ₹2.31 lakh cr. in October
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore

Gross GST collections increased 23% to over ₹2.31 lakh crore in October, driven by strong mop-up from domestic activities and imports, according to government data released on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore.
The ₹2.31 lakh crore collection includes Central GST mop-up of ₹42,935 crore, State GST of ₹51,340 crore and Integrated GST of over ₹1.37 lakh crore, data showed.
Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds increased 6.5% year-on-year to ₹27,934 crore in October.
After adjusting for refunds, net GST collections rose 26% to over ₹2.03 lakh crore in October.
During April-October, gross GST collection grew 13.2% to over ₹14.77 lakh crore. Net collections rose 13% to over ₹12.69 lakh crore.

articles.title: IOC says crude Q2 price volatile as procurement swings between discounts and premiums
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Anuj Jain, Director (Finance) at Indian Oil also stated under-recoveries on LPG is projected at ₹309/cylinder in November and ₹370/cylinder in December.

Crude oil procurement remained volatile during the September quarter, with Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) sourcing supplies at discounts of up to $5 per barrel and premiums of as much as $12, Anuj Jain, Director (Finance), told investors during a post-results call on Saturday.

The Delhi-headquartered refiner’s net profit more than doubled year-on-year to ₹21,630 crore in the second quarter, supported by improved refining margins and a brief decline in benchmark crude oil prices.
Mr. Jain said LPG under-recoveries stood at ₹184 per cylinder in September before rising to ₹229 in October. These are projected to increase further to ₹309 in November and ₹370 in December.

Explaining the volatility in procurement costs, he said crude purchases during the quarter ranged from a discount of $5 per barrel to a premium of $12 against prevailing benchmark prices. In the first quarter, the range was from zero discount or premium to a premium of $18 per barrel.
Effective procurement prices depend on several factors, including whether supplies are contracted on a free-on-board (FOB) or delivered-at-place (DAP) basis, freight costs and the grade of crude.

Russian crude accounted for around 55% of IOC’s crude basket during the first half of the fiscal, followed by supplies from the Middle East, primarily Saudi Arabia and Dubai, at 24%. Africa, including Angola and Nigeria, contributed about 10%, while Brazil accounted for 7%. Supplies from the U.S. and Venezuela made up the remaining 2-5% and 3-4%, respectively.
Around 87% of the company’s crude procurement during the period came through spot sourcing. Mr. Jain said.
Responding to a question on whether spot purchases entailed higher costs, he said such sourcing did not necessarily mean paying a premium, as prices varied across region/geography.
“Now, within spot you have Russian crude. Sometimes, we are getting a high discount, sometimes we are paying a premium as well,” Mr. Jain said.

“In the few months, we have seen huge, discounted crude coming in from Iraq. So, the moment it is available, we are buying huge quantities from Iraq also. That used to be our staple diet before the [West Asia] crisis as well.”
He added that procurement economics were also influenced by effective negotiations, which played an important role in determining the final price.

articles.title: Towards recognising women farmers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Maharashtra’s passage of the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, brings into focus the structural bias against the female agricultural workforce, highlights the need for a database of women farmers and using it to ensure access to welfare schemes

Picture a farmer. The image that comes to mind is of a man. But when one looks at who is actually farming, she is increasingly likely to be a woman. This perception-reality mismatch is caused by age-old practices of collecting data, designing policies and defining who a farmer is. It makes millions of women who work on farms, make agricultural decisions and contribute to production nearly invisible. That may, however, finally be beginning to change.

In July 2026, Maharashtra passed the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, through a Woman Farmer Certificate. This is the first Indian State legislation to give enforceable legal form to the activity-based, land-delinked definition of ‘farmer’ that the National Policy for Farmers set out in 2007 but never operationalised. The Bill arrives nearly two decades after that policy, and 15 years after a comparable law was first proposed at the national level (a lapsed bill introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 2011). It is, in effect, the culmination of three decades of women farmers’ movements backed by civil society organisations.
Macroeconomic & Financial Update: Towards recognising women farmers. This development reflects key trends in India's fiscal roadmap, monetary policy transmission, and financial sector resilience.

RBI & Fiscal Dynamics: In the context of inflation targeting by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), credit growth, capital expenditure (Capex), and external balance of payments remain vital indicators for economic stability.

📈 Economy & Finance 📅 31 Oct 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Towards recognising women farmers

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates

Maharashtra’s passage of the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, brings into focus the structural bias against the female agricultural workforce, highlights the need for a database of women farmers and using it to ensure access to welfare schemes

Picture a farmer. The image that comes to mind is of a man. But when one looks at who is actually farming, she is increasingly likely to be a woman. This perception-reality mismatch is caused by age-old practices of collecting data, designing policies and defining who a farmer is. It makes millions of women who work on farms, make agricultural decisions and contribute to production nearly invisible. That may, however, finally be beginning to change.

In July 2026, Maharashtra passed the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, through a Woman Farmer Certificate. This is the first Indian State legislation to give enforceable legal form to the activity-based, land-delinked definition of ‘farmer’ that the National Policy for Farmers set out in 2007 but never operationalised. The Bill arrives nearly two decades after that policy, and 15 years after a comparable law was first proposed at the national level (a lapsed bill introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 2011). It is, in effect, the culmination of three decades of women farmers’ movements backed by civil society organisations.

articles.title: Petrol export duty cut to nil, diesel levy raised by ₹3 a litre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The government’s fortnightly review raised the export levy on diesel to ₹11.5 per litre from ₹8.5 and on aviation turbine fuel to ₹11 per litre from ₹10.5, while India’s diesel exports touched 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025, according to Kpler

The government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) slashed the export duty on petrol to nil while hiking the levy on export of diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹3 per litre and 50 paise per litre respectively for the next 15-day period.
There was no change in the existing excise duty rates for petrol and diesel for domestic consumption.
Diesel exports would now draw a levy of ₹11.5 for every litre against ₹8.5 per litre it drew in the previous fortnight.
ATF would be subject to an export levy of ₹11 for every litre against ₹10.5 for every litre as mandated for the previous fortnight.
The revised levy on diesel assumes significance as India spiked its exports of the liquid vehicular fuel amid a global supply crunch, particularly in Europe.
According to data from real-time analytics provider Kpler, India’s diesel exports stood at 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025.

Sumit Ritolia, Manager for Modelling and Refining at Kpler, in a social media post on Friday (October 30, 2026) further observed, “India’s diesel exports are expected to ease to 500-550 kbd in Nov–Dec as seasonal domestic demand peaks before recovering to 550–600 kbd in Q1 2027. Higher maintenance in Q2-27 will constrain export, with new capacity contributing meaningfully only later in 2027.”

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

articles.title: Disinvestment as key economic strategy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Given the fact that privatisation of several PSEs is a long journey, calibrated disinvestment could serve as an interim measure

S even months into 2026-27, the fiscal year has been shaped by global uncertainty, high energy prices and worries over a deficient monsoon. Against this backdrop, disinvestment and asset monetisation have helped in navigating a challenging fiscal year. While receipts were already on course to meet the budget target, the government’s approval of the sale of its share in the IDBI Bank on October 14 makes it likely that the target will be exceeded. For the industry and investors, the receipts are a signal of the government’s continued commitment to reforms and a larger role for the private sector. This year so far, the disinvestment trajectory has progressed well, even before the IDBI stake sale. According to DIPAM data, the Centre mobilised ₹62,124 crore in April-September 2026 through disinvestment and asset monetisation, of which ₹55,757 crore came from disinvestment. These collections had already reached 78% of the full-year budget target of ₹80,000 crore. With the IDBI proceeds, the collections are to head past the target.

This comes at a time when the government looks to diversify its revenue sources amid rising expenditure commitments. Net tax revenue rose by a modest 3.4% in April-August 2026 and non-tax revenue by 3.2%, while capital expenditure was up by over 18%. Overall, the fiscal deficit has already reached 42% of the budgeted levels which implies a tight balance between revenue shortfalls and spending risks.

articles.title: Coal India profit jumps 57% as higher offtake, prices weigh over costs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Cost of input materials increased 20% during the quarter.
Coal India’s net profit surged 57% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹6,547 crore in the second quarter, driven by higher offtake and improved price realisations that offset an increase in input costs.
The state-owned coal miner declared a second interim dividend of ₹10.25 per equity share.

Offtake during the quarter ended September increased 12% YoY to 186.34 million tonnes (MT), primarily driven by higher power demand. Average price realisation, covering fuel supply agreements, e-auctions, washed coal and other categories, rose 7% YoY to ₹2,346.21 per tonne.
The Kolkata-headquartered company’s overall production grew 4% YoY to 151.37 MT in the reported quarter, falling short of its target of 157.83 MT.
Revenue from the sale of products increased 21% YoY to ₹43,724 crore. Overall revenue also rose 21% to ₹44,179 crore.

The company’s cost of materials -- which primarily includes expenditure on explosives, oil and lubricants, heavy earth-moving machinery, spares and timber, among other items -- increased 20% YoY to ₹2,752 crore during the quarter.

articles.title: Six Indian tourists stranded in Nepal, rescue efforts underway
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Indian tourists had ventured into the area despite warnings from security personnel and the Nepali guide accompanying them, says an official

Security personnel are making efforts to rescue six Indian tourists, including two women, stranded due to heavy snowfall in the Shey-Phoksundo National Park area of Nepal since Saturday afternoon (October 31, 2026), officials said on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
The tourists had gone to the Dho area in Shey Phoksundo Rural Municipality’s Ward No. 8, which was covered in heavy snow, according to Dolpa Chief District Officer Junu Dhakal.
Shey Phoksundo Lake, located in the rural municipality, is Nepal’s deepest lake. It is situated at an altitude of 3,600 metres and has an estimated depth of 145 metres.
“We have located the area where they are stranded, and an Army helicopter is arriving to rescue them. We hope to rescue them soon,” Ms. Dhakal told PTI .
The Indian tourists had ventured into the area despite warnings from security personnel and the Nepali guide accompanying them, she said.
Ms. Dhakal said the tourists left the guide and proceeded towards the lake area despite heavy snowfall. Communication with them was disrupted on Saturday night (October 31, 2026).

The guide contacted the District Administration Office in Dolpa on Saturday evening (October 31, 2026), saying the tourists might have been stranded due to heavy snowfall, she said. However, communication was completely disrupted on Sunday morning (November 1, 2026).
“We cannot say they are missing, as we have located the area,” Ms. Dhakal clarified.

The tourists have been identified as Moumita Halder, Piyali Koley, Jajla Trivedi Kumar, Aditya Singha, Diplina Bishwas and Rajesh De, according to a press release issued by the District Administration Office, Dolpa.
Security personnel are being mobilised, and a rescue helicopter is expected to arrive soon, the press release said.

articles.title: Terrorism is 'red line': Pakistan tells Afghanistan as it warns of action against cross-border threats
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting of Pakistan, on Saturday, accused the Afghan Taliban leadership of refusing to address militancy emanating from Afghan soil and instead shifting blame on Islamabad for the deterioration in bilateral ties

Pakistan has warned Afghanistan that it reserves the right to take all necessary measures to eliminate cross-border terror threats , asserting that terrorism remains a "red line" and its national security cannot be held hostage to the Taliban regime's "inaction".

In a strongly worded statement issued Saturday (October 31, 2026) night, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting accused the Afghan Taliban leadership of refusing to address militancy emanating from Afghan soil and instead shifting blame on Islamabad for the deterioration in bilateral ties.
The latest remarks by the Afghan Taliban spokesperson exposed the regime's “deeply misguided approach and unwillingness to confront the root cause of deteriorating relations with Pakistan”, it said.
"Pakistan’s position is unequivocal: Terrorism is a red line and the security of its citizens is non-negotiable,” the Ministry said.
The statement came in response to remarks made by Afghan Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, who accused Pakistan of being unwilling to resolve tensions with Afghanistan through dialogue.

In an interview to Hurriyat Radio on Saturday (October 31, 2026), the spokesperson said Islamabad lacked the necessary readiness for a peaceful resolution of differences and its “wrong policies” were preventing a resolution of the conflict.
Afghanistan was not responsible for the counter-terrorism issues cited by Pakistan, he said.

Pakistan said the Afghan Taliban regime must understand that Islamabad will "not tolerate terrorist sanctuaries across its borders that impact its security nor allow its people to remain targets of terrorism emanating from Afghanistan”.

The Taliban leadership continues to blame Islamabad’s policies while conveniently ignoring the single most important issue poisoning bilateral relations, which is its persistent failure to address terrorism emanating from Afghan soil, the statement said.

"The Taliban regime's persistent refusal to address terrorism remains the principal obstacle to normal relations. Shifting blame, making hollow assurances and questioning Pakistan’s policies will neither resolve the crisis nor absolve Kabul of its responsibilities,” it said.

articles.title: Israeli protesters demand opposition ally with Arab parties to oust Netanyahu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Arab-majority parties made major gains in elections, fuelled by anger over rhetoric targeting the community from Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right government, but opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition with them

Hundreds of Israelis took to the streets on Saturday (October 31, 2026) to urge the opposition to ally with Arab parties to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu , who has gone on the offensive against the minority group's leaders.

Arab-majority parties made major gains in Tuesday’s election, fuelled by anger over rhetoric targeting the community from Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right government, but opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition with them.
Joining a rally in Tel Aviv, Ayelet Raz said that the Arab community, which accounts for around 20% of Israel's population, had a right to political participation.
"It's the last chance for real change," the 60-year-old psychologist said, warning that Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, was a "great manipulator".
"We need to give peace a chance," she said. "Otherwise we'll have this bloodshed forever."
Tuesday’s election was inconclusive, with neither bloc reaching a majority in Israel's 120-seat parliament.
Jewish-majority parties opposed to Mr. Netanyahu, known by his nickname Bibi, won 48 seats, while two Arab-majority parties, Raam and the Joint List, secured a combined 19 seats.
An alliance between the two camps would potentially give the anti-Netanyahu bloc a comfortable majority of 67 seats, but the idea is opposed by some parties in the opposition bloc.
"Arabs and Jews will only win together" and "There is a majority for change" read some of the signs held by around 500 protesters in Tel Aviv.
"67 — United we stand, divided we get Bibi" and "Why not, really — unless we are racist?" read some of the placards at the 100-strong rally in Jerusalem.

Arab parties have only once formally sat in an Israeli government, when Raam leader Mansour Abbas joined a short-lived coalition that lasted from 2021 to 2022. He has voiced a willingness to do so again.
The Joint List's Yousef Jabareen, meanwhile, has told AFP he is willing to support Mr. Eisenkot in parliament without joining his government, citing, among other concerns, the war in Gaza.

articles.title: President Trump says U.S. still has ‘one or two targets’ in Iran
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The President said the United States is not in a hurry to take offensive action because it had already decimated Iran’s military and nuclear programme

President Donald Trump said on Saturday (October 31, 2026) that the United States has knocked out much of Iran’s military but still has to “take care of” one or two targets, as Tehran warned of reprisals if attacked.
Mr. Trump maintained that negotiations with Iran to end the war, which was started by the United States and Israel in February, were “going fine but you know they’re not very reliable.”
The President said the United States is not in a hurry to take offensive action because it had already decimated Iran’s military and nuclear programme.
“We’ve knocked out their nuclear. We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes,” Mr. Trump told reporters at his Florida residence.
“You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly,” he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex.
The Iranian government denied any nuclear work is carried out there.

Earlier Saturday (October 31, 2026), U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Mr. Trump has not made a decision about fresh strikes on Iran and that the United States would be open to a diplomatic solution.

Iran’s supreme leader on Saturday (October 31, 2026) warned the United States and Israel against launching a new offensive, following threats they could resume strikes after crucial elections in both countries.

Mr. Trump had previously warned an attack could come after the U.S. midterms this week, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke of a “historic, one-time opportunity” to topple the Iranian government.
The elections in both countries could determine the direction of the conflict, with Israel having voted in a general election on Tuesday but yet to form a new government.

“Any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response,” Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei told top military commanders, according to a statement.
Mr. Khamenei also ordered commanders to update Iran’s target list to include “all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy”.

articles.title: Donald Trump says Flavio Bolsonaro can stay in U.S. as long as he wants amid Brazilian probes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Flavio Bolsonaro’s decision to go to the U.S. followed a ruling by a Brazilian Supreme Court Justice to revoke his passport shortly after his loss, as the candidate faces a pair of federal money-laundering probes in Brazil and police there considered him a flight risk
President Donald Trump said on ⁠Saturday (October 31, 2026) evening that defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro can stay in the United States indefinitely.

"He can stay here as long as he wants," ‌Mr. Trump ⁠said of Mr. Bolsonaro, who left Brazil after losing the election to leftist incumbent ⁠Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, despite leading in most opinion polls. "In my opinion, the election was a disgrace," he added. Outside observers described the election as ​free and fair.
The Brazilian embassy in Washington did not immediately return a request for comment.

Mr. Bolsonaro's decision to go ‌to the U.S. followed a ruling by a Brazilian Supreme Court Justice to revoke his passport shortly after his loss, as the candidate faces a pair of federal money-laundering probes in Brazil and police there considered him a flight risk.
Flavio Bolsonaro says he left Brazil because he is the victim of 'persecution'
Flavio Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil’s true leader after fleeing to U.S.
He was admitted ‌to the United States under humanitarian parole, Reuters has previously reported, a status ​that typically only lasts for one year.

Mr. Rubio had said earlier on Saturday (October 31, 2026) that he spoke with Brazilian Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira at at the G20 Foreign Ministers’ meeting in Atlanta, and that they would see each other again in a few weeks.

A U.S. official and a person familiar with the matter have told Reuters that Mr. Trump has no current plans to support the political ambitions of Mr. Bolsonaro — who has described himself as Brazil's rightful leader — despite allowing the Brazilian politician into the ‌U.S. Mr. Trump, on Saturday (October 31, 2026), said he has no plans to meet with Mr. Bolsonaro.

Mr. Rubio said on Saturday (October 31, 2026) that ​the U.S. Government "was not involved directly in any of the moves" that led to Mr. Bolsonaro's departure from Brazil earlier this week. However, Reuters and several ⁠other media outlets have reported that Jason Miller, a White House official, helped arrange Mr. Bolsonaro's ⁠journey.

Mr. Bolsonaro's father, far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro, is imprisoned in Brazil for plotting a coup after losing his own re-election bid in 2022. Mr. Lula himself spent ‌17 months in jail in 2018 and 2019 on corruption charges that were later annulled.

articles.title: ‘Epstein Files’: U.S. Judge dismisses Trump lawsuit against Wall Street Journal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Donald Trump had sued for $10 billion after the newspaper’s story was published in July 2025 detailing the President’s alleged 2003 letter to Epstein, which apparently featured a drawing of a naked woman

A U.S. Judge on Saturday (October 31, 2026) dismissed President Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and media magnate Rupert Murdoch over a report that Mr. Trump sent a bawdy birthday letter to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Mr. Trump had sued for $10 billion after the newspaper's story was published in July 2025 detailing the President's alleged 2003 letter to Epstein, which apparently featured a drawing of a naked woman.
Mr. Murdoch is the founder of News Corp. which owns the Wall Street Journal.

The report piled scrutiny on Mr. Trump from both Democrats and his own Republican party, who rejected the President's attempts to downplay the saga as a hoax and called for a full release of legal files on Epstein.

In Saturday's (October 31, 2026) ruling, Judge Darrin Gayles dismissed Mr. Trump's lawsuit with prejudice, meaning Mr. Trump cannot file an amended version of the suit, as he did when Mr. Gayles turned down an initial version of it back in April.
The Judge wrote that in bringing his defamation claim, Mr. Trump had both times failed to establish that the defendants "acted with actual malice."
The House Oversight Committee last year published a copy of Mr. Trump's alleged birthday note to Epstein, which consists of a short dialogue between "Donald" and "Jeffrey."
"We have certain things in common," says Mr. Trump, to which Epstein responds: "Yes, we do, come to think of it."
"Enigmas never age, have you noticed that?" asks Mr. Trump.
"As a matter of fact, it was clear to me the last time I saw you," says Epstein.

"A pal is a wonderful thing. Happy Birthday — and may every day be another wonderful secret," the note ends, followed by Mr. Trump's signature, which takes the place of pubic hair on the nude outline.

Mr. Trump's supporters have been obsessed with the Epstein case for years and held as an article of faith that "deep state" elites were protecting a sex ring of Epstein associates, particularly in the Democratic Party and Hollywood.

A U.S. Judge on Saturday (October 31, 2026) dismissed President Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and media magnate Rupert Murdoch over a report that Mr. Trump sent a bawdy birthday letter to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Mr. Trump had sued for $10 billion after the newspaper's story was published in July 2025 detailing the President's alleged 2003 letter to Epstein, which apparently featured a drawing of a naked woman.

Mr. Murdoch is the founder of News Corp. which owns the Wall Street Journal.

The report piled scrutiny on Mr. Trump from both Democrats and his own Republican party, who rejected the President's attempts to downplay the saga as a hoax and called for a full release of legal files on Epstein.

In Saturday's (October 31, 2026) ruling, Judge Darrin Gayles dismissed Mr. Trump's lawsuit with prejudice, meaning Mr. Trump cannot file an amended version of the suit, as he did when Mr. Gayles turned down an initial version of it back in April.

The Judge wrote that in bringing his defamation claim, Mr. Trump had both times failed to establish that the defendants "acted with actual malice."

The House Oversight Committee last year published a copy of Mr. Trump's alleged birthday note to Epstein, which consists of a short dialogue between "Donald" and "Jeffrey."

"We have certain things in common," says Mr. Trump, to which Epstein responds: "Yes, we do, come to think of it."

"Enigmas never age, have you noticed that?" asks Mr. Trump.

"As a matter of fact, it was clear to me the last time I saw you," says Epstein.

"A pal is a wonderful thing. Happy Birthday — and may every day be another wonderful secret," the note ends, followed by Mr. Trump's signature, which takes the place of pubic hair on the nude outline.

Mr. Trump's supporters have been obsessed with the Epstein case for years and held as an article of faith that "deep state" elites were protecting a sex ring of Epstein associates, particularly in the Democratic Party and Hollywood.

articles.title: Swimmer’s ear doesn’t just affect swimmers – two ear doctors explain what you need to know about this painful condition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Swimmer’s ear is an infection in the external ear canal, the tube leading from the ear opening to the eardrum. Typically, swimmer’s ear occurs only in one ear, and sometimes the eardrum itself is affected
Many forms of ear infections strike children and adults alike, but among the most common is acute otitis externa , also known as swimmer’s ear.
About 10% of Americans will experience swimmer’s ear during their lifetimes . Adults are affected more commonly , and children only rarely, generally ages 5 to 12.

But you don’t have to be swimming to get swimmer’s ear. Go out jogging or walking, or do yardwork on a hot day, and moisture from perspiration can drip in your ear. However, the occurrence increases fivefold in swimmers – thus the reason the condition came to be called “swimmer’s ear.” It also occurs more frequently in tropical climates because of humidity and higher temperatures.

As doctors who specialise in ear problems, we are actively involved in research and clinical treatment for children and adults struggling with ear, nose and throat problems. Practicing in the state of Florida, we’ve certainly seen our share of patients with swimmer’s ear.

Swimmer’s ear is an infection in the external ear canal, the tube leading from the ear opening to the eardrum. Typically, swimmer’s ear occurs only in one ear, and sometimes the eardrum itself is affected. Moisture trapped in the canal leads to a break in the skin barrier and creates an opening for certain bacteria types to enter or existing ones to overgrow.

One of these culprits is the bacterium Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which is present in soil and water throughout the world. These bacteria favor moist areas, such as sinks, toilets, inadequately chlorinated swimming pools and hot tubs, as well as outdated or inactivated antiseptic solutions.

If you have the infection, you’ll know it. Symptoms generally appear a few days after infection. The main symptom of swimmer’s ear is severe pain and discomfort. It’s particularly noticeable when the outer ear is tugged, or by touching the tragus – that’s the small bump at the front of your ear. Other symptoms include itchiness inside the ear, redness, swelling and drainage. A feeling of fullness, or the perception of a plugged ear, may also occur, along with disturbed balance and temporary hearing loss.

Numerous factors can predispose someone to swimmer’s ear . They include a narrow ear canal, and skin diseases such as eczema or psoriasis. In addition, individuals wearing ear plugs, ear buds or hearing aids may be at an increased risk. Diabetics may also be more prone to the infection .
Swimmer’s ear can also come from something getting stuck inside the ear, excessive ear cleaning or contact with chemicals in hair dye or hairspray.

Swimmer’s ear is diagnosed after a health care provider has gathered a thorough history and examined the inside of the ear. The ear canal will typically look red, swollen and moist. There is also a possibility of fluid drainage or the appearance of scaly, shedding skin. Depending on the degree of swelling, the eardrum may be hard to see. A sample of fluid may be removed from the ear and sent to a lab to look for bacteria or fungus.
Eardrops are commonly used to treat swimmer’s ear . These drops often contain antibiotics to kill the infection and steroids to stop the swelling.

One such eardrop is Ciprodex . It contains ciprofloxacin, an antibiotic, and dexamethasone, a powerful steroid. Patients will need to place about four to five drops in the infected ear canal twice a day for seven to 10 days.

articles.title: There’s new guidance on menopause symptoms like hot flashes. What women need to know
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: For the first time in a dozen years, a leading OB-GYN group has updated its guidance on managing hot flashes, night sweats, sleep changes and other disruptive symptoms that often come along with menopause
For the first time in a dozen years, a leading OB-GYN group has updated its guidance on managing hot flashes, night sweats, sleep changes and other disruptive symptoms that often come with menopause.

Doctors stressed the importance of hormone therapies, which many women are considering again after the removal of federal safety warnings. On Friday, federal officials said the Food and Drug Administration has been taking steps to ensure there's an adequate supply.
Doctors also described various nonhormonal options in the new advice released this month by the American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists, or ACOG.
“We would love our patients to go to their OB-GYNs regarding questions about menopause and really advocate for getting the treatment that they need,” said Camille Clare, the group’s president.

Menopause occurs when a woman has gone 12 consecutive months without a menstrual period. In the U.S., it usually happens around age 50. The time leading up to it is called perimenopause, during which the body’s production of the hormones estrogen and progesterone declines sharply.

Problems commonly arise. More than half of women in menopause report having “vasomotor” issues such as hot flashes and night sweats, said ACOG. As many as two-thirds report menopause-related sleep disruption. And more than a third of perimenopausal and postmenopausal women worldwide report depressive symptoms.
In the past, doctors said, many women quietly suffered.

There's growing consensus that "these symptoms should be treated,” said JoAnn Manson, a professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School. “This should help to empower women to discuss their symptoms with their healthcare provider.”
Manson said ACOG’s new guidelines are similar to those put out by other medical organizations.

"Moderate to severe or bothersome menopausal symptoms should be treated with hormone therapy as the first line of treatment,” she said. While it's not appropriate for all women, she added, it’s a good option for many.

In 2002, a landmark study in women taking a pill-based combination of estrogen and progestin was stopped early because of links to breast cancer, blood clots and other serious issues. Concerns lingered even though later studies showed the benefits of today’s hormone therapies outweigh the risks for many women. For more than 22 years, all hormone-based menopause treatments carried a government warning, which Manson said discouraged patients and doctors from using them.

But last year, the FDA announced it would remove the boxed warning from more than 20 pills, patches and creams containing the hormones estrogen and progestin. On Friday, the FDA approved updated labeling for three additional estrogen-based patches.

articles.title: Health Wrap Episode 57 discusses mapping the human brain, potential of brain atlases and more
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The episode discusses a new technology developed at IIT Madras to create detailed three-dimensional maps of the human brain, the recently released C-STROKE atlas and plans to map more than 100 brains
The 57th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu explores how researchers are using advanced imaging and reconstruction techniques to create detailed, three-dimensional maps of the human brain.

Zubeda Hamid, senior assistant editor, The Hindu, speaks to Mohanasankar Sivaprakasam, Head of the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras, about the technology, how the maps are created and what they could reveal about the human brain.

The episode looks at C-STROKE, a recently released three-dimensional atlas of a stroke-affected brain. Unlike conventional MRI scans, which provide images of the brain at a particular resolution, the new approach allows researchers to examine brain structures in greater detail and build comprehensive 3D maps.

The discussion explains how researchers prepare brain tissue, use imaging techniques and reconstruct the data to create these maps. It also looks at the different scientific and technological disciplines involved in the process and how detailed mapping could help researchers study the brain’s structure and changes associated with neurological conditions.

Another focus is the Centre’s plan to map more than 100 human brains across different stages of life. The project aims to build a larger collection of brain maps that could help researchers understand variations in brain structure, study neurological conditions and expand the available resources for brain research.

The episode also examines the potential applications of these atlases in clinical research and healthcare, including how they could contribute to a better understanding of stroke and other brain conditions. It discusses the possibilities as well as the work needed before such maps can be translated into clinical applications.
The episode can also be viewed on The Hindu health page along with the full playlist of The Health Wrap

articles.title: How infant deaths in Keralam’s Attappady expose a deep-rooted health, social crisis
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: 12 infants, including 10 tribals, have died in Attappady this year, sparking a political row as the State government orders an expert probe. Tribal activists say the crisis demands action beyond healthcare, addressing malnutrition, anaemia and deep-rooted social issues

The deaths of 12 infants, 10 of them from tribal communities, in Attappady in Keralam in recent months have once again cast a spotlight on a child health crisis that has defied solutions for over a decade. While the State government has set an expert assessment in motion, tribal organisations maintain that the roots of the crisis run deeper than healthcare, demanding sustained action on nutrition, maternal health, landlessness and the wider socio-economic conditions of the community.

Figures cited by tribal activists show that 124 infants have died in the region since 2011. Since 2012, Attappady has also recorded around 300 abortions, 90 intrauterine deaths and two dozen stillbirths. The region came under particular scrutiny in 2013, when 47 tribal infants died. Tribal observers estimate that around 10 children have died annually over the years.

articles.title: Gene therapy offers to beat hepatitis B virus by muting its DNA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: An experimental therapy called CRMA-1001 is a remarkable development because, instead of targeting the virus directly, it silences the viral DNA; this is promising because current treatments rarely eliminate the DNA, which allows the virus to rebound
In 1904, two scientists, Henry Wheeler and Treat Johnson, synthesised a variant of cytosine, one of the building blocks of DNA, in the laboratory.

The variant they synthesised contained a chemical tag called a methyl group (-CH 3 ) attached to cytosine, so they called it 5-methylcytosine. Their motivation for doing so was based on the observation that two other building blocks of DNA and its chemical cousin RNA, called thymine and uracil, differed only by the presence of a methyl group.
