articles.title: Israeli protesters demand opposition ally with Arab parties to oust Netanyahu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Arab-majority parties made major gains in elections, fuelled by anger over rhetoric targeting the community from Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right government, but opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition with them

Hundreds of Israelis took to the streets on Saturday (October 31, 2026) to urge the opposition to ally with Arab parties to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu , who has gone on the offensive against the minority group's leaders.

Arab-majority parties made major gains in Tuesday’s election, fuelled by anger over rhetoric targeting the community from Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right government, but opposition chief Gadi Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition with them.
Joining a rally in Tel Aviv, Ayelet Raz said that the Arab community, which accounts for around 20% of Israel's population, had a right to political participation.
"It's the last chance for real change," the 60-year-old psychologist said, warning that Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, was a "great manipulator".
"We need to give peace a chance," she said. "Otherwise we'll have this bloodshed forever."
Tuesday’s election was inconclusive, with neither bloc reaching a majority in Israel's 120-seat parliament.
Jewish-majority parties opposed to Mr. Netanyahu, known by his nickname Bibi, won 48 seats, while two Arab-majority parties, Raam and the Joint List, secured a combined 19 seats.
An alliance between the two camps would potentially give the anti-Netanyahu bloc a comfortable majority of 67 seats, but the idea is opposed by some parties in the opposition bloc.
"Arabs and Jews will only win together" and "There is a majority for change" read some of the signs held by around 500 protesters in Tel Aviv.
"67 — United we stand, divided we get Bibi" and "Why not, really — unless we are racist?" read some of the placards at the 100-strong rally in Jerusalem.

Arab parties have only once formally sat in an Israeli government, when Raam leader Mansour Abbas joined a short-lived coalition that lasted from 2021 to 2022. He has voiced a willingness to do so again.
The Joint List's Yousef Jabareen, meanwhile, has told AFP he is willing to support Mr. Eisenkot in parliament without joining his government, citing, among other concerns, the war in Gaza.

articles.title: Health Wrap Episode 57 discusses mapping the human brain, potential of brain atlases and more
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The episode discusses a new technology developed at IIT Madras to create detailed three-dimensional maps of the human brain, the recently released C-STROKE atlas and plans to map more than 100 brains
The 57th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu explores how researchers are using advanced imaging and reconstruction techniques to create detailed, three-dimensional maps of the human brain.

Zubeda Hamid, senior assistant editor, The Hindu, speaks to Mohanasankar Sivaprakasam, Head of the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras, about the technology, how the maps are created and what they could reveal about the human brain.

The episode looks at C-STROKE, a recently released three-dimensional atlas of a stroke-affected brain. Unlike conventional MRI scans, which provide images of the brain at a particular resolution, the new approach allows researchers to examine brain structures in greater detail and build comprehensive 3D maps.

The discussion explains how researchers prepare brain tissue, use imaging techniques and reconstruct the data to create these maps. It also looks at the different scientific and technological disciplines involved in the process and how detailed mapping could help researchers study the brain’s structure and changes associated with neurological conditions.

Another focus is the Centre’s plan to map more than 100 human brains across different stages of life. The project aims to build a larger collection of brain maps that could help researchers understand variations in brain structure, study neurological conditions and expand the available resources for brain research.

The episode also examines the potential applications of these atlases in clinical research and healthcare, including how they could contribute to a better understanding of stroke and other brain conditions. It discusses the possibilities as well as the work needed before such maps can be translated into clinical applications.
The episode can also be viewed on The Hindu health page along with the full playlist of The Health Wrap

articles.title: How infant deaths in Keralam’s Attappady expose a deep-rooted health, social crisis
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: 12 infants, including 10 tribals, have died in Attappady this year, sparking a political row as the State government orders an expert probe. Tribal activists say the crisis demands action beyond healthcare, addressing malnutrition, anaemia and deep-rooted social issues

The deaths of 12 infants, 10 of them from tribal communities, in Attappady in Keralam in recent months have once again cast a spotlight on a child health crisis that has defied solutions for over a decade. While the State government has set an expert assessment in motion, tribal organisations maintain that the roots of the crisis run deeper than healthcare, demanding sustained action on nutrition, maternal health, landlessness and the wider socio-economic conditions of the community.

Figures cited by tribal activists show that 124 infants have died in the region since 2011. Since 2012, Attappady has also recorded around 300 abortions, 90 intrauterine deaths and two dozen stillbirths. The region came under particular scrutiny in 2013, when 47 tribal infants died. Tribal observers estimate that around 10 children have died annually over the years.

articles.title: Captain Chowta opposes proposal to revise timings of Gomateshwara Express
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Railway Ministry’s plan to postpone Mangaluru Junction-Yeshwantpur tri-weekly and weekly express departure timing from 7 am to 11.40 am severely affects passengers

Dakshina Kannada Member of Parliament Captain Brijesh Chowta has taken strong exceptions to Railway Ministry’s proposal to revise the departure timing of Mangaluru Junction – Yeshwantpur tri-weekly and weekly expresses from Mangaluru.

In a letter to Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Saturday, October 31, Capt. Chowta said he understood the Ministry was proposing to shift the departure timing from the present 7:00 a.m. to 11:40 a.m. for Train No. 16576, Mangaluru Junction-Yeshwantpur tri-weekly Gomateshwara Express, and Train No. 16540, Mangaluru Junction-Yeshwantpur weekly Express, as a consequence of which their arrival time at Yeshwantpur would be postponed from 4:30 p.m. to 10:15 p.m. Such a substantial change would affect the convenience and accessibility of this important daytime connection.

He said the existing daytime train service between Bengaluru and Mangaluru is an important and widely utilised rail connection for people travelling between the two regions. Its current schedule has been particularly convenient for daily and frequent passengers, including students, working professionals, business travellers, patients and families.

The MP said the present schedule allows passengers to undertake their journey during the day and reach Bengaluru at a reasonable hour. Shifting the departure to late morning and arrival to late evening would cause considerable inconvenience, particularly to passengers who depend on this service for work, education, medical appointments and onward travel.

“Given the importance of the Bengaluru-Mangaluru rail corridor and the considerable passenger dependence on this service, I request the Ministry of Railways and South Western Railway to kindly reconsider the proposed changes and retain the existing timings of the Yesvantpur-Mangaluru Express and its return service,” he said.

“Any changes to the schedules of established passenger services should be undertaken after due consideration of passenger requirements and consultations with relevant stakeholders,” the MP told the Ministry.

Railway Ministry’s plan to postpone Mangaluru Junction-Yeshwantpur tri-weekly and weekly express departure timing from 7 am to 11.40 am severely affects passengers

Dakshina Kannada Member of Parliament Captain Brijesh Chowta has taken strong exceptions to Railway Ministry’s proposal to revise the departure timing of Mangaluru Junction – Yeshwantpur tri-weekly and weekly expresses from Mangaluru.

In a letter to Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Saturday, October 31, Capt. Chowta said he understood the Ministry was proposing to shift the departure timing from the present 7:00 a.m. to 11:40 a.m. for Train No. 16576, Mangaluru Junction-Yeshwantpur tri-weekly Gomateshwara Express, and Train No. 16540, Mangaluru Junction-Yeshwantpur weekly Express, as a consequence of which their arrival time at Yeshwantpur would be postponed from 4:30 p.m. to 10:15 p.m. Such a substantial change would affect the convenience and accessibility of this important daytime connection.

He said the existing daytime train service between Bengaluru and Mangaluru is an important and widely utilised rail connection for people travelling between the two regions. Its current schedule has been particularly convenient for daily and frequent passengers, including students, working professionals, business travellers, patients and families.

The MP said the present schedule allows passengers to undertake their journey during the day and reach Bengaluru at a reasonable hour. Shifting the departure to late morning and arrival to late evening would cause considerable inconvenience, particularly to passengers who depend on this service for work, education, medical appointments and onward travel.

“Given the importance of the Bengaluru-Mangaluru rail corridor and the considerable passenger dependence on this service, I request the Ministry of Railways and South Western Railway to kindly reconsider the proposed changes and retain the existing timings of the Yesvantpur-Mangaluru Express and its return service,” he said.

“Any changes to the schedules of established passenger services should be undertaken after due consideration of passenger requirements and consultations with relevant stakeholders,” the MP told the Ministry.

articles.title: Karnataka thinking of officially recognising Kannada flag: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State Government will also issue order to enable private institutions to fly Kannada flag and it is thinking of making flying of the Kannada flag mandatory in institutions supported by government

The Karnataka Government is thinking of officially recognising the Kannada flag, and that the issue would be discussed in the ensuing Winter legislature session at Belagavi scheduled to commence from November 30, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said on Sunday (November 1, 2026).

The State Government will also issue order to enable private institutions to fly Kannada flag and it is thinking of making flying of the Kannada flag mandatory in institutions supported by the government.

“I have hoisted the Kannada flag along with the national flag. We are eager to officially recognise the Kannada flag. This will help take the footprint of Karnataka to greater heights in India’s federal structure,” he said. He spoke to reporters near his residence and Vidhan Soudha, as well as in his address at the 71st Rajyothsava celebrations at Kanteerava Stadium.

“In the past, the Cabinet had cleared the proposal to officially recognise the Kannada flag and the proposal had been submitted to the Centre, which is yet to accord approval. Recently, the issue has been discussed with legal experts and another round of discussion will be held. Legal options will be explored to officially recognise the Kannada flag without dishonouring the national flag or in violation of rules pertaining to the national flag,” the Chief Minister said.

In 2018, the State Government, then headed by Mr. Siddaramaiah, had approved a horizontal tricolour flag with yellow, white and red, with the insignia of Gandaberunda (a mythical bird and the State’s emblem) in the Centre after an expert committee set up by the Kannada and Culture Department recommended the design. The proposal was sent to the Centre since it requires an amendment to the Flag Code that governs national flag-related issues, and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) turned it down. Mr. Shivakumar, however, said, “There will be no addition. This [pointing at Kannada and yellow] will be our flag. This is what has been accepted by people and us.”

Further, Mr. Shivakumar said that the issue of according official status to the State flag would be discussed again in the Cabinet. “Our Government is committed to bringing legislation to ensure hoisting the state flag along with the national flag. The issue is open for discussion in public and among the legislators, and it will be given a new life in the winter session. Our Government is committed for a resolution seeking official status for the State flag and ensuring legal protection. This is not our government, this is your government. The Kannada flag is the beacon of emotions of Kannadigas, and it will be respected. We are taking steps to officially recognise the Kannada flag that symbolises Kannada knowledge, culture, heritage, a culture of equality for all religions and peace.”

Mr. Shivakumar also announced that the State Government has made preparations to organise various programmes to create awareness about the eminence of Kannada for the next one year. “The Kannada flag will be hoisted in all Government offices, and the government is thinking of making flying Kannada flags compulsory in institutions supported by the State Government. The government will issue an order this month to enable private institutions to fly the Kannada flag.”

Asking the Kannada activists not to indulge in ‘moral policing’ in IT and other companies, the Chief Minister told presspersons, “Marathi-speaking people should also have to accept the Rajyothsava since they are living here. Those who are here [non-Kannada-speaking population] should live here restpectfully. When we are trying to withdraw all cases against Kannada activists, they should not indulge in moral policing. The Government is there to protect the interest of the State.”

articles.title: Lady Goshen stands first among district government hospitals for zero maternal mortality after abortion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A survey conducted by the Health and Family Welfare Department in collaboration with Ipas Development Foundation among district hospitals in the State has recognised the Lady Goschen to this distinction, said a release

The District Government Lady Goschen Hospital has secured the first place in the State for maintaining 100% maternal health and bringing maternal mortality to zero in legal abortion and post-abortion care performed during 2025-26.

A survey conducted by the Health and Family Welfare Department in collaboration with Ipas Development Foundation among district hospitals in the State has recognised the Lady Goschen to this distinction, said a release. The hospital could reduce maternal and infant mortality rates to a minimum by adopting many innovative programs and methods.

The release said Lady Goschen has handled 304 legal abortions during the year under the survey, and each case has followed all the rules under the quality comprehensive abortion care program, recording a zero mortality rate.
It conducted 191 abortions before nine weeks of pregnancy, 31 between 10-12 weeks, 52 between 12-20 weeks, 20 between 20-24 weeks and five abortions post-24 weeks.

Hospital Medical Superintendent M. R. Durgaprasad congratulated the experts of the Obstetrics and Gynecology Department, Anesthesia Department, Radiodiagnosis Department, and Neonatal Department of KMC Hospital for their cooperation in achieving the feat.

He also said the service of the nursing staff, paramedical staff, and technical staff of the hospital was unique. Dr. Durgaprasad said the newly implemented WhatsApp High Risk Pregnancy Tracking System, Maternity Intensive Care Unit, Maternity Critical Care Unit, and High Risk Pregnancy Delivery Unit have played a major role in reducing the maternal mortality rate to zero.

The Medical Superintendent said the state-of-the-art life-saving equipment, which has been procured through corporate social responsibility grants from various organisations, has been helpful in providing quality service facilities. He appreciated the cooperation of the Health Minister, people’s representatives, senior officers of the district administration, departmental officers and social organisations in hospital’s functioning.

articles.title: Petrol export duty cut to nil, diesel levy raised by ₹3 a litre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The government’s fortnightly review raised the export levy on diesel to ₹11.5 per litre from ₹8.5 and on aviation turbine fuel to ₹11 per litre from ₹10.5, while India’s diesel exports touched 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025, according to Kpler

The government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) slashed the export duty on petrol to nil while hiking the levy on export of diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹3 per litre and 50 paise per litre respectively for the next 15-day period.
There was no change in the existing excise duty rates for petrol and diesel for domestic consumption.
Diesel exports would now draw a levy of ₹11.5 for every litre against ₹8.5 per litre it drew in the previous fortnight.
ATF would be subject to an export levy of ₹11 for every litre against ₹10.5 for every litre as mandated for the previous fortnight.
The revised levy on diesel assumes significance as India spiked its exports of the liquid vehicular fuel amid a global supply crunch, particularly in Europe.
According to data from real-time analytics provider Kpler, India’s diesel exports stood at 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025.

Sumit Ritolia, Manager for Modelling and Refining at Kpler, in a social media post on Friday (October 30, 2026) further observed, “India’s diesel exports are expected to ease to 500-550 kbd in Nov–Dec as seasonal domestic demand peaks before recovering to 550–600 kbd in Q1 2027. Higher maintenance in Q2-27 will constrain export, with new capacity contributing meaningfully only later in 2027.”

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 01 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Petrol export duty cut to nil, diesel levy raised by ₹3 a litre

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

The government’s fortnightly review raised the export levy on diesel to ₹11.5 per litre from ₹8.5 and on aviation turbine fuel to ₹11 per litre from ₹10.5, while India’s diesel exports touched 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025, according to Kpler

The government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) slashed the export duty on petrol to nil while hiking the levy on export of diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹3 per litre and 50 paise per litre respectively for the next 15-day period.

There was no change in the existing excise duty rates for petrol and diesel for domestic consumption.

Diesel exports would now draw a levy of ₹11.5 for every litre against ₹8.5 per litre it drew in the previous fortnight.

ATF would be subject to an export levy of ₹11 for every litre against ₹10.5 for every litre as mandated for the previous fortnight.

The revised levy on diesel assumes significance as India spiked its exports of the liquid vehicular fuel amid a global supply crunch, particularly in Europe.

According to data from real-time analytics provider Kpler, India’s diesel exports stood at 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025.

Sumit Ritolia, Manager for Modelling and Refining at Kpler, in a social media post on Friday (October 30, 2026) further observed, “India’s diesel exports are expected to ease to 500-550 kbd in Nov–Dec as seasonal domestic demand peaks before recovering to 550–600 kbd in Q1 2027. Higher maintenance in Q2-27 will constrain export, with new capacity contributing meaningfully only later in 2027.”

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.

This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

articles.title: Kannada is a confluence of history, culture and diverse literary traditions: Priyank Kharge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Emphasising the importance of preserving the State’s cultural heritage, Mr. Kharge said the present generation must protect its literature, history and traditions and pass them on to future generations

Kannada is not merely a language but a confluence of emotions, history, ideas, and traditions, said Home Minister and Kalaburagi in-charge Priyank Kharge, highlighting Karnataka’s rich literary and cultural heritage on the occasion of the 71st Karnataka Rajyotsava celebrations on Sunday (November 1, 2026).

After unfurling the national flag at the Nagareshwara High School premises in the Gunj area of Kalaburagi, Mr. Kharge addressed the gathering and said Kannada has a history spanning nearly 2,000 years and an exceptionally rich and diverse literary tradition.

He recalled that more than 40 foreign ambassadors had recently been invited by the State government to participate in the Dasara celebrations. During his interaction with them, the ambassadors had expressed admiration for Karnataka’s art, literature, food and culture. They were particularly surprised to learn about the antiquity of the Kannada language and its literary heritage, he said.

Kannada literature encompasses a rich diversity of traditions, ranging from folk and Dasa Sahitya to Jain and the Bandaya literary movements. Such a wide-ranging literary spectrum is rarely found in any other language, he observed.

Explaining Karnataka’s cultural diversity, Mr. Kharge said the State represented different identities and aspirations for different regions and communities. While Malnad was known for its lush greenery, Kalyana Karnataka was celebrated as the land of tur dal and Sufi saints, and the Mandya region as the land of silk and milk. The coastal region represented a distinctive cultural identity.

He described Karnataka as a land of art and culture for writers, a land that propagated the message of equality for followers of Basavanna, a centre of knowledge for the world, a land of opportunities for the youth, and a hub of human resources for foreigners.
He added that Karnataka’s diversity and human resources had made a significant contribution to the country’s economic progress.

Emphasising the importance of preserving the State’s cultural heritage, Mr. Kharge said the present generation must protect its literature, history and traditions and pass them on to future generations.

Celebrating Rajyotsava once a year should not be the sole expression of pride in Karnataka’s heritage. There should be sustained efforts to familiarise younger generations with the State’s cultural and literary legacy, he said.
Creating an environment conducive to preserving this heritage was the responsibility of elected representatives, while citizens also had an important role to play, he added.

The Minister joined the procession and enthusiastically played the drums. Students from various educational institutions, officials from different departments and people from various walks of life participated in the celebrations.

articles.title: Swimmer’s ear doesn’t just affect swimmers – two ear doctors explain what you need to know about this painful condition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Swimmer’s ear is an infection in the external ear canal, the tube leading from the ear opening to the eardrum. Typically, swimmer’s ear occurs only in one ear, and sometimes the eardrum itself is affected
Many forms of ear infections strike children and adults alike, but among the most common is acute otitis externa , also known as swimmer’s ear.
About 10% of Americans will experience swimmer’s ear during their lifetimes . Adults are affected more commonly , and children only rarely, generally ages 5 to 12.

But you don’t have to be swimming to get swimmer’s ear. Go out jogging or walking, or do yardwork on a hot day, and moisture from perspiration can drip in your ear. However, the occurrence increases fivefold in swimmers – thus the reason the condition came to be called “swimmer’s ear.” It also occurs more frequently in tropical climates because of humidity and higher temperatures.

As doctors who specialise in ear problems, we are actively involved in research and clinical treatment for children and adults struggling with ear, nose and throat problems. Practicing in the state of Florida, we’ve certainly seen our share of patients with swimmer’s ear.

Swimmer’s ear is an infection in the external ear canal, the tube leading from the ear opening to the eardrum. Typically, swimmer’s ear occurs only in one ear, and sometimes the eardrum itself is affected. Moisture trapped in the canal leads to a break in the skin barrier and creates an opening for certain bacteria types to enter or existing ones to overgrow.

One of these culprits is the bacterium Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which is present in soil and water throughout the world. These bacteria favor moist areas, such as sinks, toilets, inadequately chlorinated swimming pools and hot tubs, as well as outdated or inactivated antiseptic solutions.

If you have the infection, you’ll know it. Symptoms generally appear a few days after infection. The main symptom of swimmer’s ear is severe pain and discomfort. It’s particularly noticeable when the outer ear is tugged, or by touching the tragus – that’s the small bump at the front of your ear. Other symptoms include itchiness inside the ear, redness, swelling and drainage. A feeling of fullness, or the perception of a plugged ear, may also occur, along with disturbed balance and temporary hearing loss.

Numerous factors can predispose someone to swimmer’s ear . They include a narrow ear canal, and skin diseases such as eczema or psoriasis. In addition, individuals wearing ear plugs, ear buds or hearing aids may be at an increased risk. Diabetics may also be more prone to the infection .
Swimmer’s ear can also come from something getting stuck inside the ear, excessive ear cleaning or contact with chemicals in hair dye or hairspray.

Swimmer’s ear is diagnosed after a health care provider has gathered a thorough history and examined the inside of the ear. The ear canal will typically look red, swollen and moist. There is also a possibility of fluid drainage or the appearance of scaly, shedding skin. Depending on the degree of swelling, the eardrum may be hard to see. A sample of fluid may be removed from the ear and sent to a lab to look for bacteria or fungus.
Eardrops are commonly used to treat swimmer’s ear . These drops often contain antibiotics to kill the infection and steroids to stop the swelling.

One such eardrop is Ciprodex . It contains ciprofloxacin, an antibiotic, and dexamethasone, a powerful steroid. Patients will need to place about four to five drops in the infected ear canal twice a day for seven to 10 days.

articles.title: There’s new guidance on menopause symptoms like hot flashes. What women need to know
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: For the first time in a dozen years, a leading OB-GYN group has updated its guidance on managing hot flashes, night sweats, sleep changes and other disruptive symptoms that often come along with menopause
For the first time in a dozen years, a leading OB-GYN group has updated its guidance on managing hot flashes, night sweats, sleep changes and other disruptive symptoms that often come with menopause.

Doctors stressed the importance of hormone therapies, which many women are considering again after the removal of federal safety warnings. On Friday, federal officials said the Food and Drug Administration has been taking steps to ensure there's an adequate supply.
Doctors also described various nonhormonal options in the new advice released this month by the American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists, or ACOG.
“We would love our patients to go to their OB-GYNs regarding questions about menopause and really advocate for getting the treatment that they need,” said Camille Clare, the group’s president.

Menopause occurs when a woman has gone 12 consecutive months without a menstrual period. In the U.S., it usually happens around age 50. The time leading up to it is called perimenopause, during which the body’s production of the hormones estrogen and progesterone declines sharply.

Problems commonly arise. More than half of women in menopause report having “vasomotor” issues such as hot flashes and night sweats, said ACOG. As many as two-thirds report menopause-related sleep disruption. And more than a third of perimenopausal and postmenopausal women worldwide report depressive symptoms.
In the past, doctors said, many women quietly suffered.

There's growing consensus that "these symptoms should be treated,” said JoAnn Manson, a professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School. “This should help to empower women to discuss their symptoms with their healthcare provider.”
Manson said ACOG’s new guidelines are similar to those put out by other medical organizations.

"Moderate to severe or bothersome menopausal symptoms should be treated with hormone therapy as the first line of treatment,” she said. While it's not appropriate for all women, she added, it’s a good option for many.

In 2002, a landmark study in women taking a pill-based combination of estrogen and progestin was stopped early because of links to breast cancer, blood clots and other serious issues. Concerns lingered even though later studies showed the benefits of today’s hormone therapies outweigh the risks for many women. For more than 22 years, all hormone-based menopause treatments carried a government warning, which Manson said discouraged patients and doctors from using them.

But last year, the FDA announced it would remove the boxed warning from more than 20 pills, patches and creams containing the hormones estrogen and progestin. On Friday, the FDA approved updated labeling for three additional estrogen-based patches.

articles.title: Uttam wants Tummidihatti alignments keeping in mind eco issues, asks for realistic solutions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: At the proposed FRL of 152 metres, storage capacity would increase to 5.697 tmc ft from 2.182 tmc ft at 148 metres, more than doubling the storage potential, the Minister said

Minister for Irrigation and Civil Supplies N. Uttam Kumar Reddy on Saturday instructed officials to work out technically-sound and pragmatic solutions to the concerns being raised by Maharashtra over the proposed barrage at Tummidihatti across the Pranahita river with 152 metres height (full reservoir level), particularly on the submergence and environmental issues involved.

As a follow up to the recent talks with Maharashtra government on the barrage proposal, the Minister reviewed the project’s technical aspects and alignments, emphasising the need for a comprehensive assessment of the land likely to be affected or submerged at different reservoir levels.

He asked the officials to prepare detailed maps identifying the riverbed areas, forest and eco-sensitive zones, protected core areas, revenue lands and human habitations to establish the actual extent of submergence. He highlighted that engineering modifications should be examined to minimise environmental impact and address Maharashtra’s concerns without compromising the project’s irrigation objectives.

articles.title: Fuel surcharge of 4 paise per unit for bi-monthly billed consumers and 5 paise for monthly billed consumers in November
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The surcharge is meant to recover additional spending in power purchases in September this year
The Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) will collect 4 paise per unit from bi-monthly billed consumers and 5 paise per unit from monthly billed consumers as fuel surcharge in November.

The surcharge is meant to recover additional spending on power purchases in September this year. The surcharge will be applicable to all consumers except domestic consumers with connected load of and below 1,000 watts and monthly consumption of and below 40 units. Green tariff consumers also are exempted from this levy.
The levy is aimed at recouping the additional spending on power purchases from 12 central generating stations and six independent power producers (IPP) across the country.

The Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions for determination of Tariff) (First Amendment) Regulations allow a distribution business/ licensee to adjust, by recovery or refund, the fuel surcharge on a monthly basis.

articles.title: 'Chalo Dilli' protests: Rahul Gandhi assures 'legal action against PM Modi'; Kharge says 'we're not afraid to fight' | LIVE

Nadda decries the INDIA rally as foolish drama, predicting it seals Congress's political downfall amid accusations of anti-democracy plots.

Addressing the INDIA bloc’s mega rally, Rahul Gandhi accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of “stealing votes” and said legal action would follow. He asserted that the Opposition would ensure accountability and justice.

Addressing the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, Rahul Gandhi said he harboured no personal enmity towards Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Amit Shah or CEC Gyanesh Kumar. He vowed that the Opposition would reject violence and hatred while continuing its fight to protect the Constitution.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah said Delhi traders had repeatedly urged the Congress to postpone its November 1 rally until after Diwali, citing concerns over festival-season business.

Union Minister JP Nadda accused Rahul Gandhi of attempting to incite unrest and destabilise the elected government through the rally at Ramlila Maidan. He also invoked the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, accusing the Congress of having a dark record on the issue.

AISA president Neha Bora said that removing people’s names from electoral rolls denied them equal status and made them “second-class citizens”. She alleged that Muslims, women, Dalits, Adivasis and poor labourers were repeatedly asked to prove their citizenship.

Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi claimed that 15% of India’s voters were removed from electoral rolls after the 2024 elections, alleging that this made the election “illegal” and “stolen”. He said the Election Commission had made the claim. ANI/Congress

TMC chief Mamata Banerjee accused the BJP of “looting” Bengal and said her party would fight the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
“We will save democracy and bring it back,” she said at the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi. Banerjee added that the fight would continue through politics and democracy.

Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde criticised the INDIA bloc’s rally at Ramlila Maidan, alleging that its leaders were spreading a “fake narrative” and defaming Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

articles.title: UDP chief Metbah Lyngdoh resigns as Meghalaya Minister after all other MLAs joined BJP, NPP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The development followed a series of defections that saw eight of the UDP MLAs merge with the BJP in September and three others with the NPP, the Chief Minister's party, earlier this month

United Democratic Party president Metbah Lyngdoh resigned as a Minister in the Meghalaya Cabinet on Saturday (October 31, 2026), days after 11 of the party's 12 MLAs joined the BJP and the NPP, leaving him as the UDP's sole legislator in the State Assembly.
Mr. Lyngdoh said that he had submitted his resignation letter to Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma after assessing the prevailing political situation and recent developments within the party.

The development followed a series of defections that saw eight of the UDP MLAs merge with the BJP in September and three others with the NPP, the Chief Minister's party, earlier this month. The Speaker recognised both mergers, reducing the UDP's strength from 12 to one. Both BJP and UDP are constituents of the NPP-led Meghalaya Democratic Alliance.
Mr. Lyngdoh said the UDP's Central Executive Committee would deliberate on the developments and decide on the future course of action in consultation with party leaders and office-bearers.
Rejecting speculation that he was forced to resign, the UDP president maintained that the decision was voluntary.
He was in charge of the departments of power, textiles, water resources and taxation.

The political upheaval in the UDP came amid reported discontent within the party over leadership and organisational issues. The developments also followed a cabinet reshuffle in September 2025, when Metbah Lyngdoh and Lahkmen Rymbui replaced senior UDP leaders Paul Lyngdoh and Kyrmen Shylla as the party's representatives in the state cabinet.

The eight legislators who joined the BJP were Lahkmen Rymbui, Kyrmen Shylla, Pius Marwein, Mayralborn Syiem, Matthew Beyondstar Kurbah, Ollan Singh Suin, Balajied Kupar Synrem and Synshar Kupar Roy Lyngdoh Thabah.
The three who merged with the NPP were Paul Lyngdoh, Renikton Lyngdoh Tongkhar and Nujorki Sungoh.
The moves took the NPP's strength in the 60-member Assembly to 36, while the BJP's tally rose to 10.
The UDP had emerged as the second-largest party in the 2023 Meghalaya Assembly elections with 12 seats.

articles.title: Postponement of college exam for CM’s visit in Pudukottai triggers row
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: With Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay scheduled to visit Pudukottai on November 2, to inaugurate the new bus stand and distribute welfare measure, semester examinations scheduled for the day at the Kalaignar Karunanidhi Government Arts College for Women, an autonomous institution in the town, has been postponed, triggering a row.

The examinations in the college started on October 30 and are to conclude on November 19. However, the examinations scheduled on November 2 have been postponed apparently “keeping in mind the difficulty the students of the college may face in reaching the institution from the bus stand,” said the college authorities.

The exam scheduled on November 2 would be held on a later day. The college office would work as usual on November 2, the college authorities said. Several students of the college hail from the rural areas of the district.

Information about the postponement of the examination on November 2 was conveyed to the faculty members in the college group on a mobile messaging platform a couple of days ago and communicated to the students.
The Tamizhaga Vazhvurimai Katchi leader, T. Velmurugan, in a social media post expressed shock over the postponement of the examination at the college in view of the Chief Minister’s visit.

He condemned the postponement and wondered whether the Chief Minister’s visit was more important than the future of students. “It was the government’s responsibility to make arrangements for security and transportation for the official function. But, action affecting the education and examination of students could not be accepted,” he said.
Meanwhile, arrangements are under way for the Chief Minister’s programme in Pudukottai.

Minister for Labour Welfare and Skill Development J. Mohamed Farvas on Saturday said that the Chief Minister would inaugurate the new bus stand in Pudukottai and distribute welfare assistance to the beneficiaries. The function is to be held at the District Armed Reserve ground during which welfare assistance would be provided to 2,000 beneficiaries. Welfare assistance to the tune of Rs. 100 crore is to be given to 14,000 beneficiaries of Pudukottai district on that day, the Minister told reporters in Pudukottai.

articles.title: ‘You can break a stick, not a bundle’: From an IT couple to a hospital patient, citizens turn up for INDIA bloc rally
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Citizens, youth groups, farmers and political party workers gather ahead of the Ramlila Maidan rally, saying a united movement is needed to fight alleged vote theft and electoral roll irregularities

Thousands of protesters from across the country, representing political parties, youth organisations, women’s groups and farmers’ bodies, gathered at Minto Road in Delhi on Sunday (November 1, 2026) ahead of the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan, seeking to strengthen the campaign against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Chalo Dilli protests: Follow LIVE updates from the Opposition rally on November 1, 2026

Ahead of the arrival of Opposition leaders, including Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, protesters raised slogans of “vote chori” and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the rollback of the SIR exercise.

Among those assembling at Minto Road were members of the Indian Youth Congress, Samajwadi Party, Rashtriya Janata Dal, National Students’ Union of India, Krantikari Yuva Sangathan and the All India Students’ Federation, among other groups.

The gathering also drew citizens (independent of parties) who said the coming together of various parties and the public had given the protests greater strength after several demonstrations against the SIR in recent weeks.

“You can break one stick easily, but if you bundle 10 sticks together, they cannot be broken. Today’s protest symbolises that bundle of sticks,” said Tejender, an IT employee who had arrived with his wife from Gurugram.

When asked why he had joined the demonstration on a Sunday afternoon, he said, “We are doing this for a better future for our children. The education system is in a bad state, healthcare facilities are lacking, and there are concerns over the misappropriation of votes. Our country has so many problems that need to be addressed. It is high time we all came together,” he said.
Mr. Tejender said the SIR exercise has disproportionately affected people who lacked the resources or awareness to navigate the documentation process.

“I am educated and was able to produce all the required documents, but a large section of the population is either uneducated or unaware of the process and is being targeted by the SIR of electoral rolls. Who will fight for them?” he asked.
Participants also said that the past protests ensured that fear of demonstrations was gradually receding.

“The earlier protests were a struggle by the youth and they have helped remove the fear of the police from people’s minds. I was scared earlier, many political parties were scared too. But after a series of consistent protests, that fear is no longer there,” said Anil S. Raj, an advocate who had attended previous demonstrations against the SIR.

Participants said earlier demonstrations had largely taken place in silos, with different groups raising concerns over the SIR separately. The INDIA bloc rally, they said, offered an opportunity to bring these voices together and build a broader movement.

articles.title: Small fish: On Operation Trident
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: While carriers of narcotics are caught in the net, big sharks operate freely

Operation Trident , a multi-agency crackdown on an international syndicate operating across the India-Myanmar-Bangladesh corridor, marks a significant step-up in the government’s campaign against drug trafficking. The Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has set December 31, 2029, as the deadline to eradicate drug networks across the country. The October 23 raids, which led to 18 people being arrested , were based on NCB investigations following the arrest of an alleged Myanmar-based kingpin in Delhi this May. However, the dismantling of the entire network would require identification of all suppliers in Myanmar and their successful prosecution. The government’s strategy, involving States and Union Territories, over 40 Ministries, central agencies and the pharmaceutical sector, is outlined in the Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029), launched by Mr. Shah at the Narco-Coordination Centre meeting on June 26, 2026. It envisages dismantling 100 major cartels and improving prosecution outcomes. The broad strategy reflects the complexity of the problem and signals a more focused approach. Data for 2025 also show an increase of over 50% in arrests and a nearly 53% rise in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act compared with 2024.

However, the government’s action-plan will depend on consistent implementation and efficient coordination among agencies, and striking at the real brains behind it all. In several cases, foreign-based key operatives still remain at large and big sharks often do not fall in the net. The 2021 Mundra port case in Gujarat, involving the seizure of about 3,000 kg of heroin, is a case in point wherein the principal Afghanistan-based suppliers have yet to be brought to book. Also, the quantity of drugs seized does not, by itself, indicate whether drug availability or consumption has declined. Punjab remains a prominent example of the continuing public health challenges associated with drug abuse. The alleged drug-related killings of anti-drug activists in Mansa and Gurdaspur, along with the alleged death by suicide of a father in Sangrur who had raised concerns about the easy availability of synthetic drugs in his locality, underscore the human cost of the problem. These incidents also raise questions about the protection of those who speak out against drug trafficking and networks. These concerns lend urgency to the objective of dismantling entire networks and apprehending the “big sharks”, rather than concentrating disproportionately on individual carriers. The key is to identify the ultimate beneficiaries by meticulously following the money trail and ensuring their conviction.

articles.title: Fouled waters: On Rajasthan’s river pollution
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: River pollution from industrial effluents indicates state failure

The Supreme Court has pulled up, once again, the Rajasthan government over industrial effluents flowing into the Jojari river and the deadly risk it poses for the people depending on it. The problem is decades old — public interest litigation in the Rajasthan High Court alerted State machinery to the problem in 2011 — indicating an oversight by the State bordering on the systematic. The Jojari, the Luni, and the Bandi are seasonal rivers in the State’s arid western region, flowing through Jodhpur, Balotra, and Pali districts. This region has also evolved as a textile-dyeing and steelworking hub, and untreated or insufficiently treated effluents from these factories have run directly into the rivers and soil, endangering the health of around 20 lakh local residents. The region also suffers rampant illegal sand mining in riverbeds. The sewage treatment plants have been able to accommodate only around half of the sewage generated in the three urban centres, according to the State’s submissions to the Court in 2025, even as the Court recorded substantial underutilisation at common effluent treatment plants. The combination is suggestive of industrial sources bypassing treatment facilities, poor connections between the sources and the facilities, and/or insufficient capacity at particular sites or in specific periods.

The Court initiated a suo motu writ petition in 2025 and constituted a High-level Ecosystem Oversight Committee chaired by Justice Sangeet Lodha to audit the plants and draft a plan to restore the rivers. Based on the committee’s scathing status reports, Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta banned construction within 100 metres of the rivers’ edges and hazardous industries within 500 m of the present path, or of the flood lines where available. The Court has also upbraided local authorities for failing to enforce pollution norms by citing the Court’s own stay of a 2022 National Green Tribunal order imposing a compensation on the Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation and the local administration in Jodhpur and Barmer. The State regulatory apparatus has been dysfunctional: officials were aware of illegal mining operations in some areas, yet they regularised leases in those areas. Given the dereliction in play, the Court is correct to treat the possibility of collusion between State officials and industrial mafias seriously. Justice Mehta’s observation that the State could be held liable under the ‘polluter pays’ principle is also a significant indictment of state failure, through negligence. Now, importantly, the State still has to restore the Jojari and attend to its wellbeing, which is relevant to a recent tendency by the Court to substitute itself for regulators rather than disciplining them into discharging their functions. This needs to change.

ISRO’s live coverage of the GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission will begin at 11:20 pm IST on October 30, ahead of the scheduled 11:51 pm launch from Sriharikota.

ISRO’s NVS satellite launch programme has seen considerable gaps between missions. NVS-01 was launched in May 2023, followed by NVS-02 in January 2025, a gap of 19 months. The next satellite, NVS-03, is scheduled for launch in October 2026, nearly 20 months after its predecessor.

The pace of launches has also been affected by setbacks in ISRO’s broader mission programme. The space agency recorded three failures in six missions launched from Indian soil between January 2025 and January 2026, adding to the challenges of maintaining a steady launch schedule.

The United States operates the Global Positioning System (GPS), a satellite network that underpins a vast range of civilian, commercial and military activities across the world. While 24 satellites are considered sufficient to provide global coverage and optimal performance, the US maintains a larger constellation of at least 30 satellites. This additional capacity acts as a safety net, ensuring uninterrupted and reliable services even if some satellites malfunction or go out of service.

China, meanwhile, runs its own satellite-based navigation network, BeiDou, as an alternative to GPS and to meet its domestic and global positioning requirements. BeiDou’s global navigation services are designed around a constellation of 30 satellites, with estimates suggesting that approximately 35 satellites are currently in orbit.

Restoring NavIC to its minimum operational capacity would require ISRO to launch at least two more NVS-series satellites, NVS-04 and NVS-05, in addition to the existing NVS-01 and the upcoming NVS-03. These four satellites would form the minimum constellation needed to resume the system’s core navigation services. The launches would need to be carried out within a relatively short timeframe to ensure continuity.

However, four satellites would only meet the basic requirement. For greater reliability, stronger coverage and uninterrupted services, India would need additional backup satellites in orbit. This would mean building and maintaining a constellation of around six to seven NVS-series satellites to ensure the long-term stability of a regional navigation system like NavIC.

For NavIC’s core services to function effectively, at least four satellites are theoretically required. However, information shared by the Indian government indicates that only three of the constellation’s 11 satellites are currently capable of performing their primary functions.

These include first-generation satellites IRNSS-1B and IRNSS-1I, along with second-generation satellite NVS-01. IRNSS-1B has already exceeded its designed 10-year lifespan, making its continued operation uncertain, while IRNSS-1I could remain functional until around 2028. NVS-01, if it performs as intended, has at least another decade of service ahead. Meanwhile, NVS-02, launched in January 2025, was unable to raise its orbit after its onboard engines failed to fire, severely limiting its utility. As a result, NVS-01 is currently the only satellite that can be considered reliably operational over the long term.
ISRO’s NVS-03 launch could restore NavIC’s functionality, upgrading indigenous clocks and improving regional navigation amid recent launch setbacks.

articles.title: Man held for possession of 22 country-made explosives in Ranipet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: He was lodged in Central Prison in Vellore
A 20-year-old tribal, who belongs to the Irula community, was arrested by the Forest Department in Ranipet on Friday for possession of 22 country-made explosives.

Forest officials identified the arrested person as V. Devak Kumar, a resident of Irular colony near Arcot town. Initial inquiry revealed that a team of forest officials were on patrol in Pakkiri reserve forests near Kaveripakkam village, when they intercepted Kumar.
Upon inquiry, Kumar took the team to a hideout spot where he had stored country-made explosives for allegedly hunting small wild animals.
Based on a complaint by forest officials, a case was registered by Kaveripakkam police. Later, Kumar was lodged in Central Prison in Vellore. A probe is under way.

articles.title: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Bank measures can only limit damage from ‘digital arrest’ scams

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation , during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams , that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.

Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.
Editorial Context: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Suboptimal outcomes: On social security boards for unorganised, gig, platform workers
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Social security concerns of unorganised sector workers remain

One year after the implementation of the Code on Social Security , the Union Labour Ministry has constituted the National Social Security Boards for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers. The constitution of the boards, though delayed, is a welcome step. However, the highly centralised nature of this mechanism may hinder its optimal outcomes. By design, the Union Government controls both the Boards: they will be chaired by Union Minister for Labour Mansukh Mandaviya. The Board for Unorganised Sector Workers will have 40 members, nominated by the Union Government. They include seven members representing unorganised sector workers and seven members representing employers of the unorganised sector. Similarly, the Board for the welfare of gig and platform workers will have 22 members with five representatives each from the aggregators and the workers. But they have no significant representation of Central Trade Unions from the Opposition side or from the State Governments ruled by the Opposition. Labour is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and both the States and the Union must work together to improve the living standards of workers.

The International Labour Organization defines social security as the ‘protection that a society provides to individuals and households to ensure access to health care and to guarantee income security, particularly in cases of old age, unemployment, sickness, invalidity, work injury, maternity or loss of a breadwinner’. The Union Government claims that the country’s social security coverage has increased from 19% in 2015 to 64.3% in 2025, which is around 94 crore citizens. However, it is apparent that the unorganised and gig and platform workers, who make up more than 92% of the country’s total workforce, are far from enjoying any social security under this definition. articles.title: Bihar’s interests must be considered in the Ganga Water Treaty: Samrat Choudhary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The CM mentioned that Bihar’s rivers hold immense potential for the State, and through the proper management of their water and silt, new opportunities can be created in agriculture, industry, infrastructure, and employment

Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Friday (October 30, 2026) said that Bihar’s interests must be given top priority in matters concerning the Ganga Water and the Farakka Treaty. He said this during a one-day seminar organised by the State Water Resources Department titled ‘Ganga Water Treaty: Water Security of Bihar’.
He asserted that the availability of sufficient water is crucial for the holistic development of Bihar, the expansion of agriculture, and industrial progress.

“The State requires water for drinking, irrigation of farmlands, and the operation of industries. Bihar’s interests must be given top priority in matters concerning the Ganga water and the Farakka Treaty. The 25-year-old dispute between Bihar and Jharkhand over the sharing of Sone River water has been resolved with the assistance of the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, ensuring that Bihar receives three-fourths (3/4) of the water,”Mr. Choudhary said.

He added that it is a major achievement toward the better management of the State’s water resources. The Chief Minister also said that the State government has formulated a State-level policy for ‘Silt Management ', and a scientific approach will be adopted for the removal and utilisation of silt extracted from the Ganga and other rivers.

“Efforts will be made to make the silt and soil from the Ganga available for public use, as well as for construction projects such as roads and other infrastructure. An agreement will be signed between the Government of Bihar and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) in the near future. There is also a need to develop a silt management policy at the national level,”Mr. Choudhary said.

Emphasising the construction and strengthening of embankments along the Ganga, the Chief Minister called for the necessity of scientific understanding of the river’s flow and management, and acting accordingly.

He suggested that experts participating in the seminar should conduct an aerial survey of the Ganga to gain a direct assessment of the river’s current state, flow, and silt accumulation, enabling them to provide effective recommendations.

Mr. Choudhary mentioned that Bihar’s rivers hold immense potential for the State, and through the proper management of their water and silt, new opportunities can be created in agriculture, industry, infrastructure, and employment.
“The State government aims to generate employment and job opportunities for one crore people, a goal in which the optimal use of water resources will play a crucial role,”Mr. Choudhary said.

He reiterated the commitment to transform Bihar’s rivers into the foundation of the State’s economic prosperity. He suggested that through the scientific management of water resources, expert guidance, and the support of the Central Government, Bihar will be steered toward new heights of development.

articles.title: TNUHDB identifies 20 sites for reconstruction across State; appeals to residents of dilapidated tenements to vacate
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Tamil Nadu Urban Habitat Development Board (TNUHDB) has identified 20 locations across the State for reconstruction of ageing tenements during 2026-27 and plans to build greenfield resettlement sites in Perambur and Madurantakam.

TNUHDB Chairperson Ku. Pa. Krishnan, in an interaction with journalists on Friday, said that the reconstruction projects involve demolishing existing ageing tenements and constructing new housing units at the same locations. Residents can return after the work is completed. The Board has identified a total of 70 sites for reconstruction across the State, which will be taken up in phases, he said.

The TNUHDB also appealed to residents of 23 dilapidated sites to temporarily vacate their houses in view of the ongoing northeast monsoon. Of the 23 tenements identified in its safety advisory, 14 fell within the locations proposed for reconstruction this year, for which a Government Order is to be issued in the coming week. The remaining nine have been additionally prioritised for safety during the monsoon in view of their dilapidated condition.

The 23 tenements include Srinivasapuram, V.O.C. Nagar, Old Block Vyasarpadi, Nagooran Thottam, Annathai Kuppam, Nallankuppam (Old), N.V.N. Nagar (Phase-II), West Cemetery Road, Pallakumaniyam and Kabali Thottam, and Rukmani Nagar.

Mr. Krishnan said the Board was willing to undertake reconstruction of structurally weak buildings but residents’ cooperation in vacating the premises was essential. Citing Srinivasapuram, where tenements constructed in the 1970s had deteriorated over the years, he said the Board was ready to rebuild the houses and hand them back to the residents.

Two new settlement sites will come up in Perambur and Madurantakam, with Mullai Nagar identified as the location for the Perambur project. Both projects are expected to have over 450 housing units. A G.O. will be issued in the coming weeks, said Ramana Saraswathi, Managing Director, TNUHDB.

The constructions are proposed as ground-plus-six-floor buildings and are intended for eligible families living on vulnerable and objectionable poromboke land, including flood-prone areas lacking basic infrastructure.

Mr. Krishnan also spoke about the infrastructure challenges at two housing projects taken up during the previous DMK government in Dindigul district. At Oddanchatram, 480 housing units were constructed at a cost of ₹66.23 crore. “The Board is now spending an additional ₹7.14 crore to provide drinking water connectivity to the site. Nearly 90% of the work is over. But the site has poor road connectivity. We will have to look at the other amenities required to make such locations liveable,” he said.

He said a similar situation prevails at Keeranur in Dindigul district, where 432 houses were constructed at a cost of ₹57.04 crore. “Such housing projects across the State would be reviewed to assess their location, infrastructure facilities and suitability for habitation. Action will be initiated if any irregularities are found,” he said.

articles.title: Bengaluru needs long-term master plan for water, roads and sewerage: KBG
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda has directed officials to prepare a comprehensive, long-term master plan to provide drinking water, road connectivity, and underground drainage infrastructure across the Bengaluru Urban district, including areas beyond the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) limits.

Mr. Gowda chaired the fourth Executive Committee meeting of the Bengaluru Development Authority at Vikas Soudha on Friday. He said infrastructure projects must be taken up in phases with clearly defined timelines, keeping pace with the city’s rapid expansion.
The Minister said a uniform policy would hold agencies excavating roads accountable for restoration, with clear standards, cost recovery and penalties for violations.

He also stressed the need to prioritise scientific treatment and reuse of sewage to improve water security. He cited the KC Valley, HN Valley, and Vrishabhavathi Valley projects, which supply treated wastewater to lakes across neighbouring districts.

Further, he directed the BMTC to introduce GPS-enabled feeder buses within a 2 to 3 km radius of Metro stations, with fixed routes. Plans are also under way to integrate private auto-rickshaw and taxi services with the BMTC 2.0 app, which already facilitates combined ticket bookings for Metro and BMTC services.
The government has also approved nine additional fire stations across the five municipal corporations under the GBA, taking the proposed network beyond the existing 20, he said.

articles.title: Seven packaged drinking water units closed for violations in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: 102 units inspected in two days; 69 water samples collected for laboratory analysis

Karnataka’s Food Safety and Drug Administration has closed seven packaged drinking water units across Karnataka for major violations, including severe unhygienic conditions, operating without mandatory licences and non-cooperation with inspection teams, as part of a Statewide special inspection drive.

Officials also seized 82 cases of one-litre packaged drinking water bottles, valued at ₹7,380, from M.S. Food and Beverages in Devanahalli taluk of Bengaluru Rural district after detecting labelling defects.

As many as 102 packaged drinking water units were inspected between October 29 and 30, 69 water samples collected for laboratory analysis and issued notices to 53 food business operators (FBOs) for various violations.

On the second day of the drive, officials inspected 57 units and collected 37 samples for testing. Notices were issued to 29 units for violations, including unhygienic conditions, absence of medical certificates for food handlers, labelling defects, non-availability of water analysis reports and lack of mandatory pest control certificates.
Among the units closed were S.P. Food and Beverages in Hassan district, Avanti Industries in Bengaluru Urban district and Sai Ram Food Beverages in Bidar district for severe unhygienic conditions.

Om Shakthi Minerals in Bengaluru Urban, Nandi Food and Beverages in Kalaburagi and Dalia Beverages in Mysuru Rural were shut down for operating without the mandatory Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) licence. Nandi Food and Beverages was also found to be maintaining unhygienic conditions.
Aqua Refresh Packaged Drinking Water Unit in Kalaburagi district was closed following non-cooperation during inspection and investigation.
The samples collected during the inspections have been sent to government food laboratories to assess their quality and compliance with prescribed food safety standards.

The department said the special inspection drive would continue across the State and warned that stringent legal action would be initiated against packaged drinking water units found violating the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the rules framed under it.

articles.title: Karnataka High Court to nominate new head for SIT to probe KPSC irregularities on Monday
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: State government issues notification declaring SIT as police station

The State government on Friday issued a notification declaring the Special Investigation Team (SIT), which has been constituted by the High Court of Karnataka to probe cases related to alleged irregularity and corruption in recruitment process in the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC), to be a police station under Section 2(1)(u) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).

The notification was issued as the High Court on October 28 questioned the inaction on the part of the State government in not declaring the SIT as a police station in terms of High Court’s September 21 direction even 15 days after the Supreme Court on October 13 upheld the order of the High Court in constituting a SIT by the High Court.

The investigation officers appointed to the SIT are authorised under Section 193 of the BNSS to file police reports before the competent courts after investigation into the two cases related to the KPSC irregularities, it has been stated in the notification, a copy of which has been submitted to the High Court on Friday.

Justice M. Nagaprasanna, who took on record the notification, said that the court would pass orders on head of the SIT by considering the names of four senior officers suggested by the State government in terms of the order passed by the apex court on an appeal filed by the government.

The government had filed appeal before the apex court against the High Court’s September 21 order of constituting the SIT, appointing Director-General of Police Alok Kumar as its head, along with four other IPS officers, and directing the SIT to conduct investigation afresh.

However, as the apex court had observed that “...having regard to the seriousness of the allegations and possibility of the involvement of functionaries in the KPSC, the case requires investigation by a SIT comprising high ranking officers, therefore, we do not find a good reason to interfere with the impugned order (of the High Court) insofar as it directs for investigation by an SIT.”

As the apex court found the SIT a necessity, the government had confined its challenge “only to the composition of the SIT and the direction to conduct investigation afresh by pointing out certain reservation about Mr. Kumar heading it.
Besides, the government had pointed out possible conflict of interest in the inclusion of IPS officer Divya Gopinath, Director of Forensic Sciences Laboratory, in the SIT.

Though the apex court set aside the High Court’s order for conducting probe afresh, it left it to the High Court to appoint/substitute the head/member in the SIT constituted earlier, while giving liberty to the State government to suggest names of senior police officers to the SIT.

Now, the State government has suggested Additional Directors General of Police, R. Hitendra, B.K. Singh, S. Murugan, and Soumendu Mukherjee to head the SIT, and the advocates for the petitioners, Basanagouda R. Patil Yatnal, MLA, All Karnataka State Students’ Association, and Manjunath, who had sought probe by independent investigation for the KPSC irregularities, have filed their objections/responses for nominating among these officers to the SIT.

articles.title: Japan’s Omron Healthcare opens first India manufacturing facility near Chennai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Japan’s Omron Healthcare on Friday formally inaugurated its first India production facility in Gummidipoondi near Chennai. The new unit, spread over an area of 258,333 square feet at Origins by Mahindra industrial estate in Puduvoyal, has been built within three years of the Japanese firm signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Tamil Nadu government in 2023.

Designed to produce about 300,000 blood pressure monitors annually, the company plans to increase its production capacity tenfold to make 30 lakh units annually in the next two years. Omron will manufacture three models of blood pressure monitors at the new facility. The firm is also looking at exporting blood pressure monitors manufactured at the new factory to the European market by next year. “We plan to make Chennai a base not just for the Indian market but also develop it as a base for exports,” Ayumu Okada, president and CEO, Omron Healthcare Company Limited, said.

Muneo Takahashi, Consul General of Japan in Chennai said: “Tamil Nadu has become an important destination for Japanese investment, supported by its strong industrial base, skilled human resources and excellent infrastructure.”

Deepak Jacob, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Guidance said: “In 1972, Omron‘s founder joined hands with Dr. Yutaka Nakamura — a doctor known as the father of Japan’s Paralympic movement — to open Omron Taiyo in Beppu. It was Japan’s first welfare factory run and staffed by people with disabilities. People called it “the factory with wheelchairs.” And a second such factory followed in Kyoto in 1985.” Omron‘s commitment to employing persons with disabilities in this plant (Chennai) reflects exactly that value. It will inspire industries across our State to see ability first, he added.

Approximately 300 million people nationwide are estimated to be living with hypertension, while the World Health Organization (WHO) identifies cardiovascular diseases like stroke and heart failure among the country’s leading causes of death. As India’s economy continues to grow at approximately 7% annually, lifestyle changes mean that the prevalence of hypertension is expected to rise further, adding to such challenges and increasing the need for preventive healthcare. Yet fewer than 5% of households have a home blood pressure monitor in regular use, while access to healthcare services also remains limited in many regions. By strengthening the domestic supply of blood pressure monitors, Omron Healthcare aims to support more widespread home monitoring, earlier identification of cardiovascular risks, and improved hypertension management, the company said.
