articles.title: NVS-03 launched successfully; satellite placed in intended orbit | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: NVS-03 satellite is equipped with an indigenous atomic clock alongside procured atomic clocks

The GSLV rocket carrying the next-gen navigation satellite NVS-03 lifts off from Sriharikota Spaceport. 18.46 minutes later, the GSLV-F18 is expected to place the NVS-03 satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit. Cryo-stage performance of GSLV rocket normal
ISRO’s live coverage of the GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission will begin at 11:20 pm IST on October 30, ahead of the scheduled 11:51 pm launch from Sriharikota.

ISRO’s NVS satellite launch programme has seen considerable gaps between missions. NVS-01 was launched in May 2023, followed by NVS-02 in January 2025, a gap of 19 months. The next satellite, NVS-03, is scheduled for launch in October 2026, nearly 20 months after its predecessor.

The pace of launches has also been affected by setbacks in ISRO’s broader mission programme. The space agency recorded three failures in six missions launched from Indian soil between January 2025 and January 2026, adding to the challenges of maintaining a steady launch schedule.

Sriharikota [Andhra Pradesh], Oct 29 (ANI): A view of the NVS-03 satellite, which will enter the Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit in the 20th GSLV-F18 flight from Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR), in Sriharikota on Thursday. The launch is scheduled for October 30. (@isro X/ANI Photo)

The United States operates the Global Positioning System (GPS), a satellite network that underpins a vast range of civilian, commercial and military activities across the world. While 24 satellites are considered sufficient to provide global coverage and optimal performance, the US maintains a larger constellation of at least 30 satellites. This additional capacity acts as a safety net, ensuring uninterrupted and reliable services even if some satellites malfunction or go out of service.

China, meanwhile, runs its own satellite-based navigation network, BeiDou, as an alternative to GPS and to meet its domestic and global positioning requirements. BeiDou’s global navigation services are designed around a constellation of 30 satellites, with estimates suggesting that approximately 35 satellites are currently in orbit.

Restoring NavIC to its minimum operational capacity would require ISRO to launch at least two more NVS-series satellites, NVS-04 and NVS-05, in addition to the existing NVS-01 and the upcoming NVS-03. These four satellites would form the minimum constellation needed to resume the system’s core navigation services. The launches would need to be carried out within a relatively short timeframe to ensure continuity.

However, four satellites would only meet the basic requirement. For greater reliability, stronger coverage and uninterrupted services, India would need additional backup satellites in orbit. This would mean building and maintaining a constellation of around six to seven NVS-series satellites to ensure the long-term stability of a regional navigation system like NavIC.

For NavIC’s core services to function effectively, at least four satellites are theoretically required. However, information shared by the Indian government indicates that only three of the constellation’s 11 satellites are currently capable of performing their primary functions.

These include first-generation satellites IRNSS-1B and IRNSS-1I, along with second-generation satellite NVS-01. IRNSS-1B has already exceeded its designed 10-year lifespan, making its continued operation uncertain, while IRNSS-1I could remain functional until around 2028. NVS-01, if it performs as intended, has at least another decade of service ahead. Meanwhile, NVS-02, launched in January 2025, was unable to raise its orbit after its onboard engines failed to fire, severely limiting its utility. As a result, NVS-01 is currently the only satellite that can be considered reliably operational over the long term.
ISRO’s NVS-03 launch could restore NavIC’s functionality, upgrading indigenous clocks and improving regional navigation amid recent launch setbacks.

Sriharikota [Andhra Pradesh], Oct 29 (ANI): A view of the NVS-03 satellite, which will enter the Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit in the 20th GSLV-F18 flight from Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR), in Sriharikota on Thursday. The launch is scheduled for October 30. (@isro X/ANI Photo)

The United States operates the Global Positioning System (GPS), a satellite network that underpins a vast range of civilian, commercial and military activities across the world. While 24 satellites are considered sufficient to provide global coverage and optimal performance, the US maintains a larger constellation of at least 30 satellites. This additional capacity acts as a safety net, ensuring uninterrupted and reliable services even if some satellites malfunction or go out of service.

China, meanwhile, runs its own satellite-based navigation network, BeiDou, as an alternative to GPS and to meet its domestic and global positioning requirements. BeiDou’s global navigation services are designed around a constellation of 30 satellites, with estimates suggesting that approximately 35 satellites are currently in orbit.

Restoring NavIC to its minimum operational capacity would require ISRO to launch at least two more NVS-series satellites, NVS-04 and NVS-05, in addition to the existing NVS-01 and the upcoming NVS-03. These four satellites would form the minimum constellation needed to resume the system’s core navigation services. The launches would need to be carried out within a relatively short timeframe to ensure continuity.

However, four satellites would only meet the basic requirement. For greater reliability, stronger coverage and uninterrupted services, India would need additional backup satellites in orbit. This would mean building and maintaining a constellation of around six to seven NVS-series satellites to ensure the long-term stability of a regional navigation system like NavIC.

For NavIC’s core services to function effectively, at least four satellites are theoretically required. However, information shared by the Indian government indicates that only three of the constellation’s 11 satellites are currently capable of performing their primary functions.

These include first-generation satellites IRNSS-1B and IRNSS-1I, along with second-generation satellite NVS-01. IRNSS-1B has already exceeded its designed 10-year lifespan, making its continued operation uncertain, while IRNSS-1I could remain functional until around 2028. NVS-01, if it performs as intended, has at least another decade of service ahead. Meanwhile, NVS-02, launched in January 2025, was unable to raise its orbit after its onboard engines failed to fire, severely limiting its utility. As a result, NVS-01 is currently the only satellite that can be considered reliably operational over the long term.

ISRO’s NVS-03 launch could restore NavIC’s functionality, upgrading indigenous clocks and improving regional navigation amid recent launch setbacks.

articles.title: NVS-03 satellite launch successful: ISRO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The 2250 kg NVS-03 is the third satellite in the next-generation navigation satellite system envisaged for providing continuity of navigation services for the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System series

The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-F18) on Friday (October 30, 2026) successfully launched the NVS-03 satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, according to the ISRO.
The GSLV-F18 with the NVS-03 satellite lifted off from the second launch pad of the spaceport and, 18 minutes later placed the satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit.

“The GSLV-F18 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the NVS-03 satellite weighing 2250 kg in the intended elliptical orbit. Let me congratulate each and every team member of ISRO, industrial partners, academia for this outstanding accomplishment,” ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan said.
He added that the vehicle systems have performed as predicted and as expected.

The 2250 kg NVS-03 is the third satellite in the next-generation navigation satellite system envisaged for providing continuity of navigation services for the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS) series or the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC).
According to the ISRO, the satellite carries an indigenous atomic clock, along with procured atomic clocks.
“It also includes L1 signal in addition to existing L5/S signals with coverage over India landmass and a region extending 1,500 km around Indian geopolitical boundary,” the ISRO said.

NavIC is India’s independent regional navigation satellite system designed to provide accurate position, navigation, and Timing (PNT) services to users in India as well as the region extending about 1,500 km beyond the Indian landmass, which is its primary service area.

The successful launch of the NVS-03, which will have a mission life of 12 years, is expected to restore the functioning of the NavIC constellation, which has been weakened due to repeated failures of atomic clocks and the ISRO’s inability to place its previous replacement satellite, NVS-02, in its intended orbit.
It can be recalled that earlier this year, on March 13, the last functioning atomic clock aboard IRNSS-1F had stopped working.
The ISRO Chairman said that with the success of the mission, the NavIC constellation is restored to the minimum operational configuration with four satellites.

“Already three satellites are successfully working in orbit, with this satellite we will have four satellites and restore the PNT services of the country. As you know, the NavIC constellation is a strategic national asset that provides the nation independent access to PNT services. It is also used for civilian applications like real-time tracking of trains along with tracking of vehicles and shipping vessels. It is an important component of the One Nation One Time Project,” the ISRO Chairman said.

articles.title: KTR questions proposed sale of IDBI Bank, asks if its valuable real estate assets were factored in valuation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: BRS working president sought to know why the concerns raised by IDBI Bank employees over the proposed disinvestment were not being addressed

Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president K.T. Rama Rao has questioned the Union government’s proposed sale of IDBI Bank to a private player , raising concerns over the bank’s valuation, changes in bidding norms and the treatment of its real estate assets.

In a post on X, KTR said public sector undertakings (PSUs) and public sector banks were national assets that needed to be safeguarded. He said reports about the alleged undervaluation of IDBI Bank were a matter of concern and sought to know why the rules and valuation methodology were changed after bids fell below the reserve price.
He also questioned whether the bank’s valuable real estate assets, including prime land in Hyderabad, were adequately factored into the valuation.
KTR sought to know why the concerns raised by IDBI Bank employees over the proposed disinvestment were not being addressed.

Before selling a reputed public sector bank to a private entity, the Union government owed the country clear answers on the valuation and the process being followed, he said. Questioning the urgency behind the proposed sale, the BRS leader asked: “What’s the hurry?”.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Congress, VCK mobilise cadres for Nov. 1 INDIA bloc protest in New Delhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “We expect more than five lakh Congress cadres to participate. From Tamil Nadu, we are expecting at least 100 party workers to reach New Delhi from each district,” says MP R. Sudha

Demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) have activated their respective party machineries to mobilise cadres for the INDIA bloc protest to be held on November 1, 2026, in New Delhi.

While the bulk of the heavy lifting would be done by the Indian National Congress, which is much stronger in and around New Delhi, the TNCC leaders, on their part, are expected to mobilise at least 150 people from every district in Tamil Nadu.
Mayiladuthurai MP R. Sudha said that the party’s rank and file are enthusiastic and have heeded the call of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, who is expected to lead the protest.

“We expect more than five lakh Congress cadres to participate. From Tamil Nadu, we are expecting at least 100 party workers to reach New Delhi from each district. Apart from them, the office-bearers of the Mahila Congress, Youth Congress, and other party wings will also participate,” she said.

While the Congress party is mobilising people from across the country, Ms. Sudha alleged that the BJP-led Centre was trying to curtail the privileges of Members of Parliament by not allowing Emergency Quotas in trains and not providing accommodation to their guests.

“EQ is not being released. Family members are not being given accommodation, which we are usually allotted. Congress MPs, in particular, are being singled out. They are curtailing our privileges and our movement. This is an undeclared emergency,” she said.

A senior VCK leader said that the party has asked its organs in Tamil Nadu and across southern States such as Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Keralam to mobilise a modest number of party cadres for the protest in New Delhi.

articles.title: Operation underway to recover bodies from remote chopper crash site in Uttarakhand
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A team from the forest department, Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau officials, a DGCA team have all been dispatched to the crash site
Operations to recover the bodies of the six victims of the helicopter crash in Uttarakhand resumed on Saturday (October 31, 2026) morning, officials said.

Rescue work started at 5 a.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026) but the recovery from the remote area would be difficult, they said. The operation had been halted on Friday (October 30, 2026) due to darkness, the presence of wild bears and other animals and difficult terrain.

A privately run helicopter carrying pilgrims from Badrinath crashed into a hillside in Joshimath in Uttarakhand, killing all six of its occupants. The helicopter, operated by Trans Bharat Aviation, was returning from the Badrinath shrine to Dehradun.
The bodies of the pilot and the five pilgrims from Karnataka were found in the vicinity of the wreckage in Chai village.
The district administration said that on Saturday (October 31, 2026) morning a team from the forest department was also dispatched to the site to recover the bodies.
A team from the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), which is probing the crash, will also be reaching the site on the day.
Speaking to reporters, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said that orders have been issued to investigate and determine the exact cause of the accident.

"We pray to God to grant the departed souls a place at his divine feet and give strength to their families and loved ones, who are going through immense grief and trauma during this difficult time," Mr. Dhami said.

Prateek Jain, CEO, Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) told PTI , "The bodies were found but the recovery is difficult due to the terrain. The mortal remains will be brought to Chamoli district headquarters via a trek and after post-mortem examination, it will be brought to Dehradun."
When asked about permission for flying despite an alert issued by IMD, Mr. Jain said, "We had also issued an advisory but that is in the scope of investigation now."
On Friday (October 30, 2026), officials had informed that after recovery, the bodies will be brought to Joshimath town where post-mortem will be conducted on Saturday (October 31, 2026).
The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has also said that its team has been dispatched to Dehradun to conduct a preliminary and regulatory assessment of the accident.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 31 Oct 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Operation underway to recover bodies from remote chopper crash site in Uttarakhand

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

A team from the forest department, Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau officials, a DGCA team have all been dispatched to the crash site

Operations to recover the bodies of the six victims of the helicopter crash in Uttarakhand resumed on Saturday (October 31, 2026) morning, officials said.

Rescue work started at 5 a.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026) but the recovery from the remote area would be difficult, they said. The operation had been halted on Friday (October 30, 2026) due to darkness, the presence of wild bears and other animals and difficult terrain.

A privately run helicopter carrying pilgrims from Badrinath crashed into a hillside in Joshimath in Uttarakhand, killing all six of its occupants. The helicopter, operated by Trans Bharat Aviation, was returning from the Badrinath shrine to Dehradun.

The bodies of the pilot and the five pilgrims from Karnataka were found in the vicinity of the wreckage in Chai village.

The district administration said that on Saturday (October 31, 2026) morning a team from the forest department was also dispatched to the site to recover the bodies.

A team from the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), which is probing the crash, will also be reaching the site on the day.

Speaking to reporters, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said that orders have been issued to investigate and determine the exact cause of the accident.

"We pray to God to grant the departed souls a place at his divine feet and give strength to their families and loved ones, who are going through immense grief and trauma during this difficult time," Mr. Dhami said.

Prateek Jain, CEO, Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) told PTI , "The bodies were found but the recovery is difficult due to the terrain. The mortal remains will be brought to Chamoli district headquarters via a trek and after post-mortem examination, it will be brought to Dehradun."

When asked about permission for flying despite an alert issued by IMD, Mr. Jain said, "We had also issued an advisory but that is in the scope of investigation now."

On Friday (October 30, 2026), officials had informed that after recovery, the bodies will be brought to Joshimath town where post-mortem will be conducted on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has also said that its team has been dispatched to Dehradun to conduct a preliminary and regulatory assessment of the accident.

articles.title: ABVP holds ‘Save Democracy’ march in Patna amid SIR row
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ABVP National Secretary Abhay Pratap Singh said that in a democracy, governments change through ballots, not mob rule. He added that attempts to pressurise constitutional institutions are unacceptable

Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) members on Friday (October 30, 2026) took out a protest march in Bihar’s Patna under the campaign ‘ Loktantra Bachao Arajakta Hatao’ (Save Democracy, End Anarchy).

Hitting out at the Congress party, the ABVP members gathered at Kargil Chowk to convey the message of unity against alleged attempts to weaken democracy and democratic institutions. Despite continuous rainfall, a large number of students and activists from various districts of north Bihar and south Bihar participated in the programme.

Holding the national flag and ABVP flag, the protesters crossed the police barricades and marched towards Dak Bungalow Chauraha, where the rally concluded. ABVP National Secretary Abhay Pratap Singh and newly elected Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) President Yash Dabas were leading the march.
The protesters also broke the police barricading near JP Golambar before reaching Dak Bungalow and attempted to stand on the barricading.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Singh said, “India is a democratic country where governments are formed and changed through the people’s votes, not through demonstrations of strength on the streets. Anarchy aimed at changing governments in India, inspired by political developments in Bangladesh and Nepal, is unacceptable.”

“Amid questions surrounding the role of external forces, it is clear that India’s political direction will be determined by Indian citizens. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is a regular administrative process, and allegations of irregularities in it should be raised before constitutional forums with supporting evidence,” he added.

Mr. Singh pointed out that raising questions about the credibility of institutions like the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the Supreme Court for political interests, and attempting to bring them under pressure, goes against democratic principles.

“Those who are dreaming to bring a change of Government in India through anarchy, must understand that India’s democracy is strong and the future of Governments here is decided by the people,”Mr. Singh said.

ABVP called upon the youth of the country to remain vigilant in protecting the dignity of constitutional institutions, democratic values and national interest, and to oppose the politics of anarchy and mobocracy through democratic means.

“The roots of India’s youth lie in its rich cultural heritage, civilisational consciousness and sense of duty towards the nation. India’s youth take pride in their cultural identity and believe in positive, constructive and democratic approaches to resolve the country’s challenges,’ Mr. Dabas said.

He also said that through the student march in Patna, students have made it clear that the energy of Indian youth will be channelled towards nation-building, social harmony and strengthening the country’s cultural heritage.

articles.title: Two militants held for 'involvement' in kidnapping of woman in Manipur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: "They have been suspected of being involved in the kidnapping of a woman from Top Awang Leikai in Imphal East district on September 3," says police
Two members of a proscribed outfit were arrested for allegedly being involved in the kidnapping of a woman in Manipur's Imphal East district, police said on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

A joint team of police commandos and 31st Assam Rifles personnel apprehended the two militants, who belong to the banned Kangleipak Communist Party (Nongdrenkhomba), on Thursday (October 29), a police statement said.
"They have been suspected of being involved in the kidnapping of a woman from Top Awang Leikai in Imphal East district on September 3," police said.
A firearm along with ammunition and a car were seized from their possession, it said.
Security forces have been conducting search operations in Manipur since ethnic violence broke out in the State three years ago.

The ethnic conflict that erupted in May 2023 between the valley-based Meitei and hill-based Kuki communities has claimed at least 306 lives, while 49 people remain missing and thousands have been left homeless. In recent months, clashes between Kuki and Naga communities have also been reported.

articles.title: Jadu, lone rhino at Thiruvananthapuram zoo, dead
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The rhino, affectionately called Shambhu by zoo staff, was 39
Jadu, the lone one-horned rhinoceros at the Thiruvananthapuram zoo in Keralam and one of the main attractions of the facility for some three decades, died on Friday night.
The rhino, affectionately called Shambhu by the zoo staff, was 39. He was under treatment for old-age related ailments. The average lifespan of rhinoceros is around 35-40 years.
A ‘veteran’ of the zoo, Jadu was transported from the State Zoological Park, Guwahati, Assam, on May 19, 1993, by incurring an expenditure of ₹6.5 lakh. He was five then.
It was a lonely life for him though since Rita, a female rhino, was gored to death by Ramu, a male rhino, in 2004. Ramu too died of illness later.
A post-mortem examination is set to be conducted under the leadership of zoo veterinary surgeon Nikesh Kiran and State Institute for Animal Diseases, Palode, pathologist Harish.

articles.title: G20 foreign ministers to end Atlanta meeting without consensus on key issues
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Divisions over Russia’s war with Ukraine overshadowed the talks, with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio set to release a chairman’s statement instead of a joint communique

Top diplomats from the Group of 20 (G20) largest world economies will wrap up two days of talks in Atlanta on Saturday (October 31, 2026) without reaching consensus on several critical global security issues, after divisions, notably over Russia’s war with Ukraine, overshadowed the start of the meeting.

As a result, the group will not release a joint communique, but will rely on a chairman’s statement summarising the talks, which U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will release at the conclusion, according to diplomats who attended.

Mr. Rubio, who opened the talks with an appeal for unity, cancelled the traditional group photograph of the foreign ministers on Friday (October 30, 2026), after European diplomats objected to the inclusion of Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and threatened to boycott or walk out of the photograph that often kicks off such gatherings.

Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, who was representing his country for the first time as a guest at a G20 meeting, said on Friday he was not surprised by the failure to reach consensus. “We have wars going on, and we have participants in those wars around the table, so it’s very difficult to agree on a common line,” he told reporters.

Other participants, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the closed-door talks, said all had agreed to try to overcome their differences despite the long odds, and to work to make next month’s G20 leaders’ summit, hosted by President Donald Trump in Florida, a success.

These diplomats said a chairman’s statement had long been the plan, given the deep differences among the attendees, including over the Russia-Ukraine conflict, the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, U.S. tariffs and Chinese actions in the South China Sea.

All have contributed to spikes in the global cost of fuel, as well as uncertainty about trade. They described the opening session as cordial, but said Russia’s position on Ukraine is unyielding — as is its opposition to Poland’s membership in the G20. The disagreements also include the Trump administration’s decision not to invite G20 member South Africa, over the objections of others.

Some G20 countries had already expressed concern that the U.S. invited Russia during its heightened attacks on Ukraine, especially after Mr. Trump pushed ties with Ukraine to new lows by waiving fresh sanctions on Moscow and temporarily limiting logistical and intelligence assistance. However, the State Department announced on Friday that it had approved a proposed $2.1 billion sale of Patriot air defence interceptors for Ukraine.
Mr. Lavrov said Moscow would not allow a situation in which Ukraine poses a “military threat to legitimate security interests of the Russian Federation.”

He has travelled only infrequently to NATO member countries since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and severe sanctions were imposed on Moscow, and it is unclear if Russian President Vladimir Putin will accept Mr. Trump’s invitation to attend the leaders’ summit at his Miami golf club in December 2026.

The U.S. has said a top priority for the meeting is resolving differences over issues related to freedom of navigation, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, the Black Sea and the South China Sea. The topic will include discussions on Iran, Russia-Ukraine and China and its smaller neighbours.

But hanging over the meeting is the prospect of new U.S. military intervention in Iran, which has put the region, including G20 member Saudi Arabia, on edge. Mr. Rubio met on the sidelines with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan, as well as Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, whose country has been a key mediator.

articles.title: Trump backtracks on rallies in turbulent end to midterms campaign
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The U.S. President reinstated two rallies in Kansas and Iowa a day after cancelling them, saying Republicans “have a shot” in the midterms as a record 47.9 million Americans have already voted

U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday (October 30, 2026) insisted Republicans “have a shot” at success in the U.S. midterms, despite a feverish end to the campaign for elections that will decide control of Congress.
Mr. Trump reversed course and reinstated two rallies in Kansas and Iowa a day after cancelling them, a move that had raised questions about his health and about the state of the race.

“There’s such love in these all over the country,” he said of his rallies, before rattling off a series of insults against Democratic candidates vying for House and Senate seats in the elections on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

Speaking late on Friday to a crowd in Daytona, Florida, Mr. Trump said the rallies were being held “for one very simple reason: to stop America-hating communists from taking over the United States Congress.”

He reiterated his promise to give every adult American citizen $5,000 if Republicans retain control of both chambers of Congress. Experts have questioned whether he has the legal authority to do that.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Trump acknowledged to reporters that a sitting President’s party often suffers in midterm elections. “I think we have a shot at doing well. Maybe very well, but you know, pretty well,” he said.

Republicans are defending their 53-47 majority in the Senate, while Democrats are seeking to capture at least one chamber of Congress and curb Mr. Trump’s legislative agenda during his final two years in office.

Mr. Trump has put himself at the centre of the Republicans’ midterm strategy, hoping it will fire up his MAGA (Make America Great Again) base. But his dismal approval ratings and public anger over the Iran war and the cost of living may be a drag on Republican chances.
Mr. Trump, who complained of losing his voice earlier this week, had lashed out on Thursday (October 29, 2026) when asked if he was scrapping the Kansas trip because he was “sick of traveling.”
“I feel perfect,” he snapped, saying he no longer needed to visit Kansas because Republican Senator Roger Marshall was “doing very well.”
But the about-face was likely the result of questions over the energy levels of America’s oldest-ever elected President, political strategist Mike Fahey told AFP .

“My suspicion is that Trump didn’t particularly like that narrative, and putting the events back on the calendar was the fastest way to kill it,” said Mr. Fahey, a veteran of multiple election campaigns. Both Kansas and Iowa voted comfortably for Mr. Trump in 2024, but have emerged as unexpected battlegrounds for Republicans.

articles.title: Jaishankar, Anita Anand agree that Modi’s Canada visit in December will be ‘another building block’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: External Affairs Minister Jaishankar met Canadian counterpart Anita Anand in Atlanta on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met his Canadian counterpart Anita Anand and agreed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Canada in December will be another “building block” in ties between the two countries.

Mr. Jaishankar met Ms. Anand in Atlanta on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting on Friday (October 30, 2026). Both the leaders also assessed the “steady growth” in India-Canada cooperation.
“Delighted to meet FM @AnitaAnandMP of Canada today. Assessed the steady growth of our cooperation,” Jaishankar said in a post on X on Friday (October 30, 2026).

According to an official statement, “the ministers agreed that Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Canada in December will be another building block in the two countries’ ambitious relationship.” They also “agreed” to stay in close contact ahead of the visit, it said.

Earlier this month, during her visit to India, Canadian Foreign Minister Anand met Prime Minister Modi, and she said they had a productive discussion on further strengthening India-Canada ties in trade, technology and energy.
On October 16, the Indian High Commission in Ottawa said Mr. Modi will visit Canada on December 11 and 12. The date of the visit was also confirmed by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.
Mr. Carney had said he spoke to Modi and the visit will take place in Toronto and Ottawa. “We’ll see if we can broaden it out,” he said earlier this month.
ALSO WATCH Falling short on Marco Rubio’s second visit to India | The Hindu Editorial
Mr. Jaishankar also met foreign ministers of Argentina, Mexico, Brazil, and Germany. “Glad to meet FM Pablo Quirno of Argentina on the sidelines of G20,” he said.
Mr. Jaishankar said he discussed trade, critical minerals, defence and nuclear cooperation, and multilateral issues with Quirno.
The Minister said his meeting with Mexico’s Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco Alvarez was focused on giving a new impetus to bilateral relations.
“A pleasure to sit down with FM Mauro Vieira of Brazil. Our conversation covered bilateral and global issues,” Mr. Jaishankar said.

articles.title: Oman rescues 25 from burning ship, Iran halts tankers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Tehran has restricted maritime traffic through the strait since the West Asia war erupted on February 28 with U.S.-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic
Oman said Friday (October 30, 2026) it had rescued 25 sailors from a merchant ship set ablaze in an attack, as Iran reported three oil tankers were halted while crossing the Strait of Hormuz.
Tehran has restricted maritime traffic through the strait since the West Asia war erupted on February 28 with U.S.-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic.
The narrow waterway, which normally carries about a fifth of global oil, has become a focal point of the conflict, with ships regularly coming under Iranian fire.

Muscat's navy "carried out an evacuation operation for 25 crew members of the merchant ship RITI, flying the Panamanian flag, after it was targeted, which led to a fire breaking out on board," Oman's Maritime Security Centre said in a statement.
The crew members were provided with medical care, the Omani statement said, without giving details.
The Marine Traffic ship-tracking website described the RITI as a crude oil tanker.

U.S. Central Command chief Brad Cooper said in a video released on Friday (October 30) that U.S. forces had "successfully cleared the strait's internationally recognised primary transit routes of Iranian sea mines".
U.S. forces remain "present to ensure that all primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear," he added.

Mr. Cooper said he visited some of the more than 50,000 U.S. service members in the region, repeating earlier statements that Washington has helped Gulf countries export more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude via the strait since summer.

British maritime security agency UKMTO said that a ship 40 nautical miles (74 kilometres) south of Lavan Island in Iran was struck on Friday (October 30) by an unknown projectile, which caused a fire onboard.
"The crew of the vessel have been reported as safe and there is no reported environmental impact at this time," the UKMTO said on X.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said earlier that three oil tankers had been halted after encountering unspecified "incidents" or hitting mines.

articles.title: Fears of violence as France braces for Halloween protests
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Around 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday (October 31, 2026), matching the number mobilised a week ago, as authorities seek to avert a repeat of the October 17 unrest

France on Saturday (October 31, 2026) braced for a third weekend of protests coinciding with Halloween, as shops boarded up and authorities scrambled to prevent a repeat of the street violence that swept the country two weeks ago.
The demonstrations come in an increasingly febrile political climate, with presidential elections six months away and far-right leader Marine Le Pen leading opinion polls.
President Emmanuel Macron this week said it was "not normal" for France to be in such a state of "turmoil" so close to a presidential election.
Around 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday (October 31, 2026), matching the number mobilised a week ago, as authorities seek to avert a repeat of the October 17 unrest.
More than 40 metro stations will be closed in the capital and tram services will also be disrupted.

An aide to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said they expected street violence on a scale "comparable" to the unrest two weeks ago, when images of clashes, looted shops and public buildings set ablaze were broadcast around the world.

The protest movement brings together Yellow Vest activists, trade unions, and high school and university students. It initially focused on the rising cost of living, inequality, and deteriorating learning conditions.
But following a security clampdown and serious injuries to some protesters, the movement broadened its demands to include greater protection of civil liberties and the right to protest.
A police source pointed to "considerable nervousness" among the authorities. "There is no reason to think this will go smoothly," the source said.
Alain Di Crescenzo, president of France's chamber of commerce, said business owners were worried.

"Shopkeepers can't wait for Saturday (October 31, 2026) to be over," Mr. Di Crescenzo told broadcaster France Inter . "The information we have is that Halloween is not helping matters, because we're going to have people wearing masks."
Ahead of the protests, some shops and other businesses across France boarded up their storefronts.

articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro says he left Brazil because he is the victim of 'persecution'
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: "The persecution began even sooner than I imagined," Mr. Bolsonaro said during an Instagram livestream in which he discussed his decision to flee after his Brazilian passports were cancelled as part of a money laundering investigation
Former conservative presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said Friday (October 30, 2026) that he fled Brazil to the United States because he was a victim of "persecution" in his country.

Mr. Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's (October 25) election runoff to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, secretly left Brazil on Tuesday (October 27) and arrived in Florida aboard a private jet on Wednesday (October 28) after travelling through Argentina and Ecuador.

"The persecution began even sooner than I imagined," the senator said during an Instagram livestream in which he discussed his decision to flee after his Brazilian passports were cancelled as part of a money laundering investigation.
In the video, he recounted how police informed him on Monday that his passports were being revoked as he left a visit to his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest.
"With tears in his eyes, he told me: 'You know where they're going with this, don't you?'" he said of his father.
"I told him: 'Dad, I know... Now I know what I have to do,'" he recounted.
Although he gave no details of how he left the country, he said he and his wife made the decision "without anyone knowing" and urged people not to "point the finger at anyone."
U.S. President Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei are under pressure to explain the involvement of the United States and Argentina in the senator's escape.
"I didn't leave Brazil; I left for Brazil," Flavio Bolsonaro said, alleging that Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes had made false accusations against him.
He also suggested there had been irregularities in the runoff, comparing them to "handball goals" that were not disallowed by VAR, without detailing what those irregularities might have been.
He also predicted that the economy would "go bust" under Lula and said he was willing to run for president again: "I'm not talking about 2030, I'm talking about before then."

In the video, he recounted how police informed him on Monday that his passports were being revoked as he left a visit to his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest.

"With tears in his eyes, he told me: 'You know where they're going with this, don't you?'" he said of his father.

"I told him: 'Dad, I know... Now I know what I have to do,'" he recounted.

Although he gave no details of how he left the country, he said he and his wife made the decision "without anyone knowing" and urged people not to "point the finger at anyone."

U.S. President Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei are under pressure to explain the involvement of the United States and Argentina in the senator's escape.

"I didn't leave Brazil; I left for Brazil," Flavio Bolsonaro said, alleging that Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes had made false accusations against him.

He also suggested there had been irregularities in the runoff, comparing them to "handball goals" that were not disallowed by VAR, without detailing what those irregularities might have been.

He also predicted that the economy would "go bust" under Lula and said he was willing to run for president again: "I'm not talking about 2030, I'm talking about before then."

articles.title: To overcome technical hurdles, ISRO flew NVS-03 satellite with pyro valves open: Narayanan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Pyro valves are crucial in spacecraft propulsion, and it may be recalled that the NVS-02 (launched in 2025), the second spacecraft in the NVS series, was a failure

ISRO chief V. Narayanan on Saturday (October 31, 2026) said that in order to ensure mission reliability and bypass previous technical hurdles, the NVS-03 satellite was operated with "three pyro valves open".

Addressing the media at a post-launch press conference, Mr. Narayanan revealed that this bold technical decision was validated after rigorous vibration and shock testing by a national-level committee chaired by former ISRO chief Kiran Kumar.
Pyro valves are crucial in spacecraft propulsion, and it may be recalled that the NVS-02 (launched in 2025), the second spacecraft in the NVS series, was a failure.
A high-level panel, after thorough analysis, concluded that "the drive signal did not reach the pyro valve of the oxidiser line of the engine meant for orbit raising."
In February 2026, ISRO, quoting the panel, announced that the most likely cause was the disengagement of at least one contact (in each of the main and redundant paths) of the connector.

Against this background, Mr. Narayanan said that with four satellites, including NVS-01 now active in India's navigation satellite system, ISRO plans to launch NVS-04 in five months, and NVS-05 in 10 months to further bolster the constellation.

Mr. Narayanan highlighted the exceptional accuracy of the flight. "Against [the planned] perigee [point when it is closest to the Earth] of 170.36 km; we have got 170.31 kilometres," Mr. Narayanan said.

"Against [the planned] Apogee [point farthest away from the Earth] of 37,247 kilometres, we achieved 38,080 kilometres," he noted. "This is one of the best accuracy of any of the launch vehicles in the world we can think of," he added.

The successful deployment has restored India's NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) to its minimum operating configuration of four satellites, bolstering both strategic and civilian location services across the subcontinent.

Executing its fastest-ever turnaround for a heavy-lift rocket, the ISRO successfully placed the next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 into a highly precise orbit using the GSLV-F18 launch vehicle early on Saturday (October 31).

He said: "To ensure mission reliability and bypass previous technical hurdles, ISRO flew the satellite with three pyro valves already open. Narayanan revealed that this bold technical decision was validated after rigorous vibration and shock testing by a national-level committee chaired by former ISRO chief Kiran Kumar."

Elaborating on NavIC's civilian applications, the ISRO chief said 10,400 locomotives and 64,000 fishing vessels are currently tracked in real-time. Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, the agency aims to expand this to 1 lakh fishing vessels within the next six months. In total, 15 lakh tracking devices have been fitted across vehicles. When asked when NavIC would be available on civilian mobile phones, Mr. Narayanan stated this would happen once the full seven-satellite constellation is completed.

articles.title: Meta settles, leaving Snap sole defendant in new social media trial
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Jury selection began on Wednesday, and opening statements are scheduled for November 4

Meta reached a settlement in a landmark case over the alleged harms of social media, the plaintiffs' lawyers said Friday, leaving Snap as the only defendant in a trial set to open in Los Angeles next week.

"We remain committed to improving safety for kids on social media apps and holding tech companies accountable, and we are pleased to have brought this matter to a just resolution on behalf of our client," Emily Jeffcott, a lawyer representing one of the young women suing both companies, said in a statement.
Jury selection began on Wednesday, and opening statements are scheduled for November 4.
The terms of the agreement are confidential, but sources close to Meta told AFP the company decided to settle for business reasons.

"Trials, dismissals and settlements are all common in the bellwether process, and this litigation is no exception," a Meta spokesperson said, referring to the series of test cases against the company being tried in Los Angeles.
If Snap does not settle, the trial will go ahead next week.
Snap did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
TikTok and YouTube were also named as defendants in the case, but both had already reached settlements with the plaintiffs, known by their initials SJ and KDB, their lawyers said.
A California state judge consolidated the two cases into a single trial.
Snap, which makes Snapchat, will defend itself against the claims of both SJ and KDB.

Lawyers for SJ and KDB will argue that their clients were exposed to "addictive and problematic" social media apps when they started using them at ages 13 and 15, respectively, according to court documents.

"We believe the evidence will support that we have put our community first, and that these allegations fundamentally misrepresent the plaintiffs' experiences on Snapchat and how our platform was designed," a Snap spokesperson said in a statement earlier this week.

articles.title: OpenAI to limit weapons information for teens on ChatGPT in violence-prevention push
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: OpenAI will restrict practical ‌information on weapons and security systems that ‌could ⁠be misused

OpenAI said on Friday it is tightening limits on the weapons-related information ChatGPT provides ​to teens, even when a question appears ‌harmless, as part of new safeguards aimed at ​preventing real-world violence.
The move comes ⁠as AI companies face growing scrutiny over the risks chatbots pose to young users and the companies’ ‌role in detecting threats of harm.
OpenAI will restrict practical ‌information on weapons and security systems that ‌could ⁠be misused , with the limits applying to ⁠teens even when there is no sign of violent intent
For all users, ChatGPT will be able to ​automatically end chats where ‌someone appears to be fixating on violence, and OpenAI may temporarily pause accounts after multiple such chats

The company also said ‌it strengthened its age prediction system to move ​users it estimates are under 18 into the teen experience, and it ⁠plans to notify parents if their teen’s account is paused for repeatedly discussing violence
For all ‌users, OpenAI is limiting detail on past mass attacks, including the weapons used and how they were obtained
The company said the new safeguards will begin rolling out in the next few weeks, and it will ‌continue to refine them
OpenAI said earlier this month ​that teens spend under 15 minutes a day on average on ChatGPT, in ⁠its first report on teen use

A report by ⁠non-profit Common Sense Media earlier this month found that ChatGPT’s teen version often ‌alerted parents late or not at all when teen accounts held conversations about suicide, self-harm ​or eating disorders

articles.title: A ferocious El Niño is brewing thanks to record Pacific heat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Since the modern era of instrumental records began, there have only been three very strong El Niño events, in 2015-16, 1997-98, and 1982-83, with the three-month averages of the temperature anomaly being 2.6°, 2.4°, and 2.1°C, respectively. The 2026-27 El Niño is projected to peak with an anomaly of 3.8°C

For most of this year, climate scientists have been closely monitoring the Niño 3.4 region in the central-equatorial Pacific — the primary index area to define the phases of the El Niño Southern Oscillation and the alarming amount of ocean heat closely tracking an El Niño. The world’s oceans beyond the poles reached a record-high average surface temperature of 21.18°C on August 22, and daily sea surface temperatures in the Niño 3.4 region have been consistently shattering records.

According to the U.S. NOAA’s Climate Prediction Center, a ‘strong to very strong’ El Niño is 83% likely, with a high chance of a historic event exceeding the strength of any previous El Niño since 1950.

The El Niño is a natural climate pattern that emerges every two to seven years and affects global weather and heightens the risk of extreme heatwaves and altered rainfall worldwide. But this year’s event has put the world more on edge.

articles.title: Hungry customers won’t be able to distinguish between ‘Sangeetha’ and ‘Sangetha’: Madras High Court in trademark case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice P.B. Balaji quotes Tamil poetess Avvaiyar’s statement, ‘Pasi Vandhal Pathum Paranthu Pogum’, and the Tamil idiom, ‘Pasi Kanna Kattuthu’

The Madras High Court has restrained a restaurant located opposite the Thanjavur Brihadeeswarar Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, from using the name ‘HOTEL SANGETHAS PURE VEG RESTAURANT’ after observing that hungry customers are likely to be deceived into believing that it belongs to the popular Sangeetha chain of restaurants spread across the world.

Justice P.B. Balaji quoted Tamil poetess Avvaiyar’s statement, ‘Pasi Vandhal Pathum Paranthu Pogum ’ (hunger could make one forget even the 10 virtues that he/she is supposed to follow), and the Tamil idiom, ‘Pasi Kanna Kattuthu’ (hunger could make your vision go blurry), to reject the argument that customers would be able to note the difference between ‘Sangeetha’ and ‘Sangetha.’

Passing interim orders in a trademark infringement suit filed by Sangeetha Caterers and Consultants LLP, the judge wrote: “A hungry person is the most potential customer for the respondent (Hotel Sangethas Pure Veg owned by Narayanan Chandrasekaran). He is not going to see or notice the colour scheme or the device marks used, but will easily get carried away by the name.”

The judge went on to state that though the respondent had dropped an ‘e’ from the name of his restaurant in English, he had still chosen to write the name as Sangeetha in Tamil. “It is not as if in Tamil language, there is no equivalent word or manner to replicate the English name Sangethas. It is very much possible to exactly convey the same spelling and even a different pronunciation, if really intended,” he added.

“In fact, applying the quote and the idiom that I have discussed above, a customer would easily be deceived by the name of the respondent and would be blind to the colour scheme, spelling, viz., omission of an ‘e’, use of ‘Hotel’ as a prefix or even the device marks (wheel and conch as against a veena used by the plaintiff) and is very likely to be carried away by the name and only associate it with the plaintiff,” the judge said.

Justice Balaji also rejected the argument that the plaintiff does not have any branches in Thanjavur and hence, there was no cause for confusion among customers. “Given the rich cultural heritage of this place, it is an undeniable fact that there is a huge floating population visiting this city, especially to see the Big temple... Given the number of visitors or travellers from various parts of the world to the city of Thanjavur, it is highly possible that they may only see the respondent’s hotel as that of the plaintiff’s,” he concluded.

articles.title: Theni jailbreak: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay orders suspension of Theni district jail superintendent in-charge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: R. Krishnaraj, Superintendent of Madurai Central Prison, has been transferred and posted as Superintendent of Salem Central Prison

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has suspended Deputy Jail Superintendent N. Nageswaran, who had been holding additional charge as Superintendent of the Theni District Jail since August 6, 2024, in view of the jailbreak incident earlier this week.

A total of 17 inmates lodged at the Theni District Jail escaped from the prison on the night of October 26, 2026, after attacking the prison guard on duty. All of them were apprehended within a span of 40 hours.

Following the incident, Mr. Vijay on Saturday (October 31) ordered stringent action over the security lapses in prison administration, negligence in surveillance, and lack of diligence in the discharge of duties.

The officer was placed under suspension with effect from October 30, as per the Tamil Nadu Civil Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, for failing to pay adequate attention to the supervision and control of inmates and prison staff.

The Tamil Nadu government also transferred R. Krishnaraj, Superintendent of Madurai Central Prison, to Salem Central Prison to strengthen prison administration, accountability, and monitoring, a release stated.

The Chief Minister has also stated that Prison Department officials must discharge their responsibilities with utmost care and vigilance to ensure that there are no lapses in security and surveillance in prisons. He warned that stringent action would be taken against officials found to be negligent or careless while discharging their duties.

articles.title: PM Modi inaugurates tourism, infrastructure projects worth ₹307 crore in Gujarat's Ekta Nagar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones for eight development projects worth ₹118.88 crore, taking the total outlay for the 31 projects to ₹426.71 crore

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (October 31, 2026) inaugurated 23 development projects worth ₹307.83 crore to boost tourism and civic infrastructure at Ekta Nagar in Gujarat's Narmada district.
The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones for eight development projects worth ₹118.88 crore, taking the total outlay for the 31 projects to ₹426.71 crore.
Earlier in the day, Mr. Modi paid floral tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel at the Statue of Unity to mark his birth anniversary, which is observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas.
The newly launched projects aim to upgrade visitor facilities and civic infrastructure around the world's tallest statue, which has developed into a major tourism hub.

The major tourism attractions inaugurated by the Prime Minister include an Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) hotel built at a cost of ₹50 crore, the Ekta Cruise (₹16 crore), a Rain Forest attraction (₹14.30 crore), and an Eco-Trail costing ₹3.67 crore.

On the infrastructure front, the Prime Minister inaugurated a sewage treatment plant built for ₹45.53 crore, a water treatment plant worth ₹21.40 crore, and a parade track and associated works costing ₹23.81 crore.

To improve connectivity and convenience, the government has introduced travelators worth ₹28.22 crore, a 24-metre colony road costing ₹23 crore to ease traffic congestion, staff quarters valued at ₹14.25 crore, and two nine-metre-long air-conditioned electric buses.

Other new facilities include a terminal building and a jetty near Mokhadi village, water stations at various locations, an extension of the walkway connecting Ekta Nagar railway station to the Visitor Centre, and fountains at different sites.
Mr. Modi also launched new visual features, including facade lighting within the Statue of Unity campus, the 'Ekta Prakash Parv' heritage display, and an upgraded Unity Glow Garden.

He laid the foundation stones for eight upcoming projects, including the Gora-Bhanadra Road estimated at ₹59.32 crore, and a Smart Zero Waste integrated solid waste management facility costing ₹36.58 crore.

Other upcoming initiatives include the development of the Khalwani Bridge (₹7.72 crore), a cactus and butterfly garden (₹ 5.79 crore), Khalwani Eco-Tourism development (₹5.15 crore), widening of Vaghadia Road, and construction of a disaster control room for the Sardar Sarovar Dam.

The projects form part of the Gujarat government's efforts to develop Ekta Nagar and the Statue of Unity area into a world-class tourist destination, with a focus on new attractions, improved connectivity and better civic amenities.

The West Bengal government is planning to bring back a tigress that was released in the Buxa Tiger Reserve and later strayed into Assam.

The three-year-old tigress, BTR-TF-1 (T-138), was released in Buxa on October 2 from Bihar’s Valmiki Tiger Reserve as part of the State’s first tiger relocation project. However, the tigress crossed into Assam on Sunday (October 25, 2026) in search of a suitable habitat.
West Bengal Forest Minister Manoj Oraon said that he and officers of the department will visit Assam on Saturday (October 31, 2026) to inspect the tigress’s movement and health condition.

“Our team has already been coordinating with Assam’s Forest Department to monitor the tigress. However, I am personally visiting Raimona tomorrow and will finalise the necessary plan to tranquilise and bring her back to Buxa,” he said.

According to the officials, the tigress crossed the Sankosh River and a road in Gosaigaon in Assam to enter Raimona on Sunday (October 25, 2026), mostly in search of suitable habitat. So far, her movement area has been traced 25 km away from the Bengal border.

Forest officials from Assam and West Bengal, along with a team from the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), initially decided to let her explore the surroundings and choose a suitable habitat. However, efforts are now underway to bring her back to Bengal’s territory.
Mr. Oraon said that the tigress is healthy and is also hunting animals.

On October 2, the tigress was translocated from Bihar’s Valmiki Tiger Reserve and released in the presence of Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. Mr. Adhikari said three more tigers would be released in Buxa in the next two months, and the initiative would not only help in conservation of wildlife but also in boosting tourism in the region.

Buxa was declared a tiger reserve in 1983, and over the past few years there have been no reports of tiger presence in the region. According to an official statement by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), the recovery of Buxa has been a sustained, science-based effort, and the Tiger Augmentation and Recovery Project, initiated by the Government of West Bengal with support from the NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India (WII), has been implemented collaboratively since 2018.

Forest officials say this new tigress from Bihar will be subjected to intensive post-release monitoring using a combination of telemetry, camera trapping and field-based monitoring to assess her movement, adaptation, health and behaviour.

articles.title: DMK women cadre protest across Tamil Nadu over price rise, law and order
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: DMK MP Kanimozhi accused CM Vijay of seeking children’s support to mobilise votes without ensuring their safety

The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) Women’s Wing on Saturday (October 31, 2026) staged protests at district headquarters across Tamil Nadu, accusing the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government of failing to maintain law and order, protect women and children, and control the rising cost of essential commodities in the State.

In north Chennai, the protest was led by DMK deputy general secretary and MP Kanimozhi Karunanidhi near the Collectorate. The protesters raised slogans against the government over price rise and the alleged deterioration in law and order. They carried sacks of rice, cans of cooking oil, and other essential commodities to highlight the increase in prices. They also held placards bearing slogans such as “Law and order has become a laughing stock” and “Wake up from your sleep, Chief Minister!”

Addressing the gathering, Ms. Kanimozhi referred to incidents of child abduction and alleged trafficking, accusing the government of failing to ensure children’s safety even within their homes. She also alleged that members of the ruling party were involved in “abducting and selling children.”

Questioning Chief Minister Vijay’s appeal to his supporters, whom he referred to as “ Nanbaas ” and “ Nanbees ” (friends), to persuade their families to vote for him during the election campaign, she accused him of seeking children’s support to mobilise votes without ensuring their safety.

Ms. Kanimozhi said reports of child trafficking had heightened parents’ fears about their children’s safety. She urged people to bring the government to an end, warning that Tamil Nadu risked being pushed into a dark period if the situation continued.

She also alleged that investments were not coming into the State, law and order had deteriorated, women were unsafe, and children faced an uncertain future. The administration had become so ineffective that questions arose about whether the government was functioning properly, she said.

The DMK leader also criticised the government over the rising cost of essential commodities, saying many families were struggling to afford even their daily meals. The increase in the prices of onions, tomatoes, rice, pulses, and cooking oil had made it difficult for ordinary households to prepare food, let alone celebrate Deepavali, she said.

She said rice and pulses had become twice as expensive. She also questioned the government’s claim that better-quality rice would be distributed through ration shops, alleging that the existing rice was merely being polished and presented differently.

Contrasting the situation with the DMK’s tenure in power, Ms. Kanimozhi said Tamil Nadu had previously been at the forefront of investment, economic growth, education, and healthcare. The State was now lagging in several sectors while witnessing rising crime and prices, she alleged.
Taking a swipe at Mr. Vijay’s references to gifts for children and women, she urged him to prioritise their safety instead of distributing presents.

“Please give every woman in Tamil Nadu a can of pepper spray,” she said, alleging that the police and government machinery were failing to protect women. She suggested that pepper spray be distributed through ration shops to help women defend themselves.
Former Ministers P.K. Sekarbabu and Poongothai Aladi Aruna, along with district-level functionaries, participated in the protest.

articles.title: Violence in Punganur: High Court hears Midhun Reddy’s plea to quash FIRs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Midhun Reddy's counsel argued that the cases were foisted on frivolous grounds

Justice Y. Lakshmana Rao of the Andhra Pradesh High Court heard the petitions filed by Rajampet MP P.V. Midhun Reddy for quashing four FIRs registered against him by Punganur urban police for alleged involvement in violence over filing of nominations for the local body election.
Appearing for Mr. Midhun Reddy, Senior Counsel O. Manohar Reddy argued that the cases were foisted on frivolous grounds for vexatious reasons.
Public Prosecutor M. Lakshminarayana appeared for the State. He presented videos to establish the involvement of the MP in the incident.

Senior Advocate Posani Venkateshwarlu appeared for one of the complainants and argued that the presence of the MP and his followers at the nomination centre was unwarranted and that he has no right to seek any relief when sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita invoked against him disclosed the commission of a cognizable offences.
Representing another complainant, advocate P.V.G. Umesh Chandra pointed out that the MP was neither a contestant nor a proposer and he disregarded caution by police.

He added that Mr. Midhun Reddy could not make out a prima facie case for granting stay, as there was evidence of a reasonable nexus. Moreover, Mr. Midhun Reddy's counsel submitted a medical report which revealed injuries to him. The matter was adjourned for a later date.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia says intercepted ‘hostile drone’ in Riyadh region
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: No information yet on who launched the drone
Saudi air defences intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region on Saturday (October 31, 2026), according to the spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis.
"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone in the Riyadh region," Turki al-Malki wrote on X, adding that "debris from the interception fell without causing injuries".

In recent weeks, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis have ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, including by launching deadly strikes on Riyadh airport that forced its closure for two weeks and the cancellation of flagship events — threatening the kingdom's economic diversification plans.
On Friday (October 30, 2026), Mr. Malki said the Houthis had targeted the Medina region, home to Islam's second holiest city, but the group later denied the claim.

The Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure, airports and ships come after hostilities resumed in Yemen over the summer between the Houthis and the country's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Riyadh.
More than 1,600 people have been killed and over 275,000 displaced since the fighting reignited, according to United Nations figures.
In July, a fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen's capital Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.
Later, the Houthis declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before seizing Yemen's entire Red Sea coast in a lightning campaign.
The Houthis have reported frequent Saudi airstrikes in areas they control as Riyadh retaliates.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Houthis have reported frequent Saudi airstrikes in areas they control as Riyadh retaliates.

articles.title: Nations commit to get nature goals back on track at UN nature summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The United Nations had warned that progress was insufficient to meet the goals of the 2030 target including protecting 30% of Earth’s land and oceans, tackling pollution and invasive species, and boosting money for conservation

Nearly 200 nations struck hard-fought agreements on Friday (October 30, 2026) at a UN biodiversity summit, but the outcome was accompanied by disappointment over missed opportunities to address humanity’s destructive toll on nature.
Delegates cheered as crucial texts were approved in overtime but the celebrations were tempered by acrimonious debates and regret over limited progress on some of the most contentious issues.
The COP17 summit in Armenia sought to revive a landmark commitment to halt and reverse the destruction of nature by 2030 after global efforts to meet that goal fell short.
Over two bruising weeks in Yerevan, nations were urged to correct course to keep the pact alive and protect the plants, animals and ecosystems that sustain life on Earth.

The United Nations had warned that progress was insufficient to meet the goals of the 2030 target including protecting 30% of Earth’s land and oceans, tackling pollution and invasive species, and boosting money for conservation.

“And that’s it. Perfect,” said COP17 president Hambardzum Matevosyan in Armenia as he brought down the gavel on two major texts, the final versions of which were still not available early on Saturday (October 31).

But the outcome was “not commensurate” with the crisis engulfing the natural world, said French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut early on Saturday (October 31) as the summit drew to a close.

“The progress we failed to achieve here is a series of missed opportunities to speed up our response to the loss of biodiversity,” Ms. Barbut said in a lengthy statement sent to AFP , stressing that “nature will not wait for the pace of our negotiations.”
The final plenary stretched through Friday (October 30) night and well into the next morning, with negotiations turning sour as the hours dragged on.
Even as some delegates left to catch flights, others stayed behind to argue technical points.

Veteran COP observer Juliette Landry from the IDDRI think tank told AFP “there was a lot of push and pull in every direction” throughout the summit and “in that context, it’s hard to get things accepted”.
In a draft agreement of one closely watched text, nations were urged to “accelerate” their efforts and warned that “increased action” was needed to tackle the forces driving biodiversity loss.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nearly 200 nations struck hard-fought agreements on Friday (October 30, 2026) at a UN biodiversity summit, but the outcome was accompanied by disappointment over missed opportunities to address humanity’s destructive toll on nature.

The United Nations had warned that progress was insufficient to meet the goals of the 2030 target including protecting 30% of Earth’s land and oceans, tackling pollution and invasive species, and boosting money for conservation.

“And that’s it. Perfect,” said COP17 president Hambardzum Matevosyan in Armenia as he brought down the gavel on two major texts, the final versions of which were still not available early on Saturday (October 31).

But the outcome was “not commensurate” with the crisis engulfing the natural world, said French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut early on Saturday (October 31) as the summit drew to a close.

“The progress we failed to achieve here is a series of missed opportunities to speed up our response to the loss of biodiversity,” Ms. Barbut said in a lengthy statement sent to AFP , stressing that “nature will not wait for the pace of our negotiations.”

The final plenary stretched through Friday (October 30) night and well into the next morning, with negotiations turning sour as the hours dragged on.

Even as some delegates left to catch flights, others stayed behind to argue technical points.

Veteran COP observer Juliette Landry from the IDDRI think tank told AFP “there was a lot of push and pull in every direction” throughout the summit and “in that context, it’s hard to get things accepted”.

In a draft agreement of one closely watched text, nations were urged to “accelerate” their efforts and warned that “increased action” was needed to tackle the forces driving biodiversity loss.

articles.title: Launch of NVS-03: PM Modi congratulates scientists, engineers at ISRO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Mr. Modi also said that equipped with enhanced capabilities, NVS-03 will further India’s pursuit of self-reliance in critical technologies and support navigation services that benefit the people

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (October 31, 2026) congratulated scientists and engineers at ISRO on the successful launch of GSLV-F18 carrying NVS-03 and said the mission marks an important step in strengthening NavIC, the country's indigenous satellite navigation system.
Mr. Modi also said that equipped with enhanced capabilities, NVS-03 will further India's pursuit of self-reliance in critical technologies and support navigation services that benefit the people.

"Congratulations to our scientists and engineers at ISRO on the successful launch of GSLV-F18 carrying NVS-03. This mission marks an important step in strengthening NavIC, our indigenous satellite navigation system," he said in a post on X .
The Prime Minister said the dedication and ingenuity of India's space scientists continue to make the nation proud.

India's independent regional navigation satellite system NavIC was restored to its minimum operational configuration of four satellites on Friday (October 30, 2026) as ISRO successfully launched its navigation satellite NVS-03, which was placed into the designated injection orbit by a GSLV rocket.

The second-generation navigation satellite NVS-03, with indigenous and procured atomic clock, has a wide array of applications, including civilian use like real-time tracking of trains, vehicles and shipping vessels.

articles.title: Class 10 student attacked with wood-cutting machine inside classroom in A.P.’s Anantapur; accused yet to be identified
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The girl who was seriously injured in the attack is undergoing treatment in a hospital; two youths who allegedly carried out the attack were not students of the school, fellow students said
A Class 10 student of the Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu of Andhra Pradesh ’s Anantapur district was seriously injured after being attacked inside her classroom on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

The accused allegedly attacked the girl with a wood-cutting machine after entering the classroom in the presence of a teacher while classes were under way, according to preliminary information. The victim was then shifted to a hospital for treatment.
The accused fled the school, leaving the wood-cutting machine behind in the classroom. The police said they are yet to identify the accused or establish the motive for the attack.
According to fellow students, two youths — who were not students of the school — allegedly entered the classroom and attacked the girl.

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu expressed shock over the attack and enquired with officials about the girl’s condition and the treatment being provided to her. He directed the police to apprehend the accused at the earliest and take action against them in accordance with law.

“I am personally tracking her recovery and have directed the medical team to give her the highest priority care. I have ordered the police to hunt down the monster responsible and deliver the harshest legal punishment swiftly,” he wrote in a post on X.

I am deeply shaken and enraged by the barbaric attack on a Class 10 student inside her classroom at Raptadu ZP High School. Attackers who target our young girls inside schools have no place in our society. I am personally tracking her recovery and have directed the medical team to give her the highest priority care. I have ordered the police to hunt down the monster responsible and deliver the harshest legal punishment swiftly.

Nara Lokesh, State Minister for IT, Human Resource Development and Real Time Governance, also expressed shock over the attack on the girl. “I could not hold back tears in my eyes seeing my small sister lying in a pool of blood inside her classroom. We will crush the perpetrators with an iron hand,” he said, adding that any individual who think of harming a girl or a women is dealt with seriously.

చిన్నారి చెల్లిని క్లాస్ రూములో నెత్తుటి మడుగులో చూశాక కన్నీళ్లు ఆగడం లేదు. గుండె బరువెక్కింది. రాప్తాడులో ఉన్మాది ఘాతుకం తీవ్ర దిగ్భ్రాంతికి గురి చేసింది. ఉన్మాదులను ఉక్కు పాదంతో అణిచేస్తాం. ఆడపిల్లలు, మహిళల వైపు కన్నెత్తి చూడాలంటే భయపడేలా చేస్తాం. పిల్లల భద్రత పట్ల నిర్లక్ష్యం వహించేవారు ఎంతటి వారైనా చర్యలు తప్పవు.
BJP Andhra Pradesh State President PVN Madhav said utmost priority should be given to the safety of school children.
