articles.title: Impeachment would have happened in Parliament if those in power had heeded public interest, says AISA’s Neha Bora | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: INDIA Bloc says everyone united in protests, 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar today

Chhattisgarh Congress Legislature Party (CLP) leader Charandas Mahant, in a post on X (translated from Hindi), alleged that the BJP was snatching away fundamental rights and destroying democracy by “stealing votes”.

He said a “mega rally” would be held at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on November 1, 2026, under the leadership of Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi, and appealed to people to reach the venue and raise their voice to save democracy.

All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora said that if those in power had listened to public interest, the impeachment of the Chief Election Commissioner would have been done in Parliament. She was speaking on the INDIA bloc’s ‘public impeachment’ of CEC Gyanesh Kumar today (October 31, 2026).

CPI leader D. Raja, arriving at Mr. Kharge’s residence for the ‘Public Impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar’, said “tomorrow’s rally will send a message to PM Modi that the country cannot be ruled in this way”.

Security was tightened outside the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Rajaji Marg in New Delhi on Saturday (October 31, 2026), ahead of the INDIA bloc’s ‘public impeachment’ programme against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The symbolic exercise, modelled on parliamentary proceedings, is being organised by Opposition parties to highlight their allegations of irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged ‘vote chori’. It does not constitute a formal impeachment or removal process under the law.

JMM MP Mahua Maji said the INDIA bloc’s “public impeachment programme” was part of its push over the SIR of electoral rolls. She said civil society members and people whose names were deleted from the rolls were likely to attend, with an open invitation to MPs and leaders of other parties.

Congress MP Pawan Khera said the INDIA bloc’s exercise was “not a mock parliament” but “a public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. He added that people beyond the INDIA bloc, including members of civil society, were eager to join.
Preparation is in finishing touches for the Congress -INDIA Bloc Maharally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi.

Rajasthan Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra said a “major event” that “will be recorded in golden letters in history” was about to take place, with more than 10 lakh people expected to gather under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge.
He said the rally was aimed at protecting the Constitution, the country and citizens’ voting rights.

The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) on Saturday (October 31) questioned the timing of the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally being held amid Diwali festivities and said that ignoring festivals, social harmony and the country’s economy in the name of politics is not a good sign for political parties.

Impeachment would have happened in Parliament if those in power had heeded public interest, says AISA’s Neha Bora | LIVE

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

INDIA Bloc says everyone united in protests, 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar today

Chhattisgarh Congress Legislature Party (CLP) leader Charandas Mahant, in a post on X (translated from Hindi), alleged that the BJP was snatching away fundamental rights and destroying democracy by “stealing votes”.

He said a “mega rally” would be held at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on November 1, 2026, under the leadership of Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi, and appealed to people to reach the venue and raise their voice to save democracy.

All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora said that if those in power had listened to public interest, the impeachment of the Chief Election Commissioner would have been done in Parliament. She was speaking on the INDIA bloc’s ‘public impeachment’ of CEC Gyanesh Kumar today (October 31, 2026).

CPI leader D. Raja, arriving at Mr. Kharge’s residence for the ‘Public Impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar’, said “tomorrow’s rally will send a message to PM Modi that the country cannot be ruled in this way”.

Security was tightened outside the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Rajaji Marg in New Delhi on Saturday (October 31, 2026), ahead of the INDIA bloc’s ‘public impeachment’ programme against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The symbolic exercise, modelled on parliamentary proceedings, is being organised by Opposition parties to highlight their allegations of irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged ‘vote chori’. It does not constitute a formal impeachment or removal process under the law.

JMM MP Mahua Maji said the INDIA bloc’s “public impeachment programme” was part of its push over the SIR of electoral rolls. She said civil society members and people whose names were deleted from the rolls were likely to attend, with an open invitation to MPs and leaders of other parties.

Congress MP Pawan Khera said the INDIA bloc’s exercise was “not a mock parliament” but “a public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. He added that people beyond the INDIA bloc, including members of civil society, were eager to join.

Preparation is in finishing touches for the Congress -INDIA Bloc Maharally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi.

Rajasthan Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra said a “major event” that “will be recorded in golden letters in history” was about to take place, with more than 10 lakh people expected to gather under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge.

He said the rally was aimed at protecting the Constitution, the country and citizens’ voting rights.

The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) on Saturday (October 31) questioned the timing of the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally being held amid Diwali festivities and said that ignoring festivals, social harmony and the country’s economy in the name of politics is not a good sign for political parties.

1. Core Context & Background: INDIA Bloc says everyone united in protests, 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar today

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chhattisgarh Congress Legislature Party (CLP) leader Charandas Mahant, in a post on X (translated from Hindi), alleged that the BJP was snatching away fundamental rights and destroying democracy by “stealing votes”.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) on Saturday (October 31) questioned the timing of the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally being held amid Diwali festivities and said that ignoring festivals, social harmony and the country’s economy in the name of politics is not a good sign for political parties.

articles.title: Woman rams multiple vehicles, tries to run over cops in Mumbai; booked
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The woman sped away after hitting a stationary car, knocking down a scooter, a motorcycle, and another car during her escape attempt, police official said

A woman allegedly rammed her car into multiple vehicles, tried to run over police officers, and created a ruckus at a traffic signal in the western suburbs of Mumbai, police said on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

The incident occurred near the Sangeet Bharati Chowk signal in Juhu around 8.30 p.m. on Friday (October 30, 2026), when the woman sped away after hitting a stationary car, knocking down a scooter, a motorcycle, and another car during her escape attempt, an official said.
She allegedly also tried to steer her vehicle toward on-duty police personnel, he said.

"When a female police personnel tried to intervene and asked her to stop while recording the scene, the woman took out her mobile phone, started filming the officers, and created a ruckus," the official said.

A constable later instructed the woman to move her car to the side of the road to clear the traffic congestion. Several bystanders at the spot captured the entire episode on their mobile phones, police said.

Following a complaint lodged by the owner of the rear-ended vehicle, the Juhu police registered a case in connection with the accident and rash driving. Further investigation into the matter is underway, officials said.

articles.title: CPCB threatens to shut NCR industries yet to order pollution-control devices
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In an October 30 letter, the Central Pollution Control Board asked authorities in Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan to issue show-cause notices to non-compliant units under the CAQM’s revised emission norms

The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has directed pollution control authorities in Delhi-NCR to shut industrial units that have failed to place orders for installing or upgrading air pollution control devices (APCDs). Though not a new measure, it signals a tightening of enforcement of emission standards ahead of the winter pollution season.

In an October 30 letter, the CPCB has asked the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) and the State Pollution Control Boards of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan to immediately issue show-cause notices to non-compliant units covered under the Commission for Air Quality Management’s (CAQM) revised emission norms. Units that fail to produce evidence of having placed orders for the equipment within five days are to face closure orders and remain shut until they demonstrate compliance with a credible installation timeline, the letter notes.

The direction comes ahead of restrictions scheduled to take effect in Delhi from November 1 under the government’s winter pollution management framework, which includes curbs on vehicles, construction activities and other pollution sources. After peaking in the “poor” category around 222–232 mid-week (October 28–29), continuous rainfall dropped Delhi’s average AQI to 60 on Friday (October 30, 2026) and around 95 on Saturday morning (October 31, 2026), according to the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology-maintained network.

The CAQM prescribed a particulate matter (PM) emission limit of 50 mg/Nm³ for 17 categories of highly polluting industries, as well as specified ‘medium’ and large ‘red-category’ industries, food-processing units, textile industries operating boilers and metal industries with furnaces. The revised standard became applicable from October 1.

The CPCB’s latest direction follows reports that several industrial units have not placed orders for new APCDs or for retrofitting existing equipment, and have also failed to obtain adequacy assessment reports or exemption certificates.

APCDs are filtration and emission-control systems fitted to industrial exhaust stacks to capture particulate matter before gases are released into the atmosphere. They include bag filters, which trap dust using fabric membranes; electrostatic precipitators, which use high-voltage electricity to collect charged particles; cyclone separators, which use centrifugal force to remove coarse particles; and scrubbers, which use liquids to capture dust and certain gases.

The CPCB’s previous attempts at imposing deadlines have only had limited effect. Only around 200 of 2,321 identified industrial units had complied with the installation or retrofitting requirement by July 31, according to reports. Industries had cited delays in equipment procurement, higher costs and shortages of agencies capable of assessing existing systems.
Until the latest tightening, several units operated under an earlier PM emission limit of 80 mg/Nm³, with 50 mg/Nm³ serving as an ‘advisory target’.

articles.title: Gujarat HC Judge strikes down ban on non-veg food sale in Somnath; two-Judge Bench stays her order
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A division Bench stayed the judgment of Justice Nisha Thakore following an urgent appeal moved by the Gujarat Government, and directed that the Collector's notification banning the sale of non-veg food will continue for now

Hours after a single Judge of the Gujarat High Court struck down a ban on the sale of non-vegetarian food in the vicinity of the famous Somnath temple, a two-member High Court Bench stayed her ruling on Friday (October 30, 2026).

A division Bench of Chief Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak and Justice Nirzar Desai stayed the judgment of Justice Nisha Thakore following an urgent appeal moved by the Gujarat Government, and directed that the Collector's notification banning the sale of non-veg food will continue for now.
The division Bench will hear the matter next on December 26.
Earlier in the day, Justice Thakore allowed petitions filed by the owners of hotels and restaurants operating near the Somnath temple in Gir Somnath district and set aside the notification.
The Collector's order prohibits the sale of non-vegetarian food along designated pilgrimage routes.
The Government immediately filed an appeal before the Bench headed by Chief Justice Pathak, which stayed the single Judge's order late in the evening.

The notification dated August 10, 2026, restricting the "preparation, storage and sale" of non-vegetarian food within a 500-metre radius of the Somnath temple along with six specifically identified roads connecting important religious destinations in the area that form part of the sacred Somnath pilgrimage circuit would continue, the Bench said.
Hotel and restaurant owners contended in the petition that the restrictions infringed their fundamental right to carry on lawful business and earn their livelihood.

The State Government submitted that the constitutional freedom to carry on a business did not mean a person can conduct every form of commercial activity at every location, irrespective of the religious, historical and cultural significance of the place.
Somnath is not an ordinary commercial town but has extraordinary spiritual importance for millions of Hindus, the Government said.

articles.title: Congress is using democracy slogan to cover up electoral defeats: R. Ashok
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Leader of Opposition in Karnataka Legislative Assembly R. Ashok accused the Congress of launching its campaign against CEC Gyanesh Kumar out of political desperation

Leader of Opposition in Karnataka Legislative Assembly R. Ashok accused the Congress of launching its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar out of political desperation and to divert public attention from its electoral defeats .

Addressing a press conference in Hubballi on October 31, he said the Congress questioned democratic institutions and the electoral process only when the results went against the party. The party had failed to accept the people’s verdict in several elections, including 59 Assembly constituencies in which it lost, he alleged.

“Why does the Congress have a different stand when it loses an election? It accepts the process when it wins, but questions it when defeated,” he said, referring to the party’s allegations of vote theft and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Mr. Ashok questioned the Congress’s claims about large-scale deletion of voters, including the alleged removal of 24 lakh names on account of death in Karnataka.

On the clean sweep by BJP in recent polls in Karnataka, Mr. Ashok said if the elections were held with EVMs, by this time Congress would have attributed to theft. “Through ballot, Congress has been handed a bullet,” he said.

The Congress is free to organise protests as part of its democratic rights, but threats to create unrest and indulge in violence could not be justified, he said. The campaign was aimed at reviving the Congress politically rather than protecting democracy, he alleged.
“The Congress should accept the people’s verdict and prove its strength through the ballot box,” he said, expressing confidence that the BJP would win 149 seats in the next Assembly election.

On the Karnataka government’s handling of drought relief, Mr. Ashok accused the Congress government of failing to provide the promised assistance to farmers. He said the BJP government, when in power, had released drought relief funds without waiting for assistance from the Centre .
He questioned the government of Karnataka over the delay in distributing the ₹2,500 assistance announced for drought-affected farmers and asked when the promised amount would reach beneficiaries.

He sought details of the funds received by Karnataka under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF). Rejecting allegations by Congress that the Centre had neglected Karnataka, he claimed that the State had received five times more assistance than before, even after accounting for devaluation of the rupee.

Referring to the ongoing protest by sugarcane growers , Mr. Ashok said the issue was serious and required a joint effort by the State and the Centre. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi had held discussions on the matter, and both governments should work together to address the concerns of farmers, he said.

articles.title: Whose sight matters? How gender shapes access to eye care in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Across their lifespans, from childhood to old age, women face disadvantages in access to eye health and care. For many, treatment depends on how their health is prioritised by the men in their household. Late care, or lack of access can leave girls and women with preventable visual impairment and loss

“I remember a patient, a little girl with retinoblastoma,” says Rohit Khanna, a community ophthalmologist and network director from L.V. Prasad Eye Institute, Hyderabad. “We told the family that the child required surgery and that the eyeball would have to be removed for her to survive. We were immediately met with resistance. The father asked, what was the point of her living if she was going to be disfigured. They would not be able to get her married later.”
Retinoblastoma is a rare, fast-growing tumour of the eye and is often seen in early childhood. It is a type of cancer, and can lead to death if not treated.

articles.title: AI giants promise publishers new way to block some
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Publishers currently have to implement multiple blocking commands for every that crawls the web to collect data

OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic pledged on Friday to give media outlets and other websites a single way to prevent their content from being to train artificial intelligence (AI) models, amid growing criticisms and legal battles from news publishers.

Publishers currently have to implement multiple blocking commands for every that crawls the web to collect data , but the new proposed solution will allow them to enter a single, standardized instruction that's recognized and honored by any AI company that adopts the protocol.
The solution will not fully take effect for months, though.

Microsoft will implement it beginning February 1, 2027, and Google sometime in 2027. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it will roll it out "in the coming months," while Claude-maker Anthropic said it has "already started" rolling it out.
The announcement comes as publishers are facing a surge in bots that scrape their articles to feed AI models. Some, like the New York Times, have taken the matter to court.

Meanwhile, internet infrastructure provider Cloudflare has blocked AI bots by default on new customer sites since July 2025, and a standard called Really Simple Licensing already allows publishers to charge bots that visit their pages.

The new setting will apply only to future training of models but does not prevent bots from crawling otherwise, and content will be allowed by default until the setting is changed by a publisher, Microsoft said in a blog post.
Opting out of AI training could reduce the chances that a publisher's content will surface in AI apps and experiences, Microsoft and Google said in separate blog posts.

"We believe creating a common signal that conveys such preferences to multiple providers at once is an important step. And we look forward to working with other AI companies on the standards and their implementation across the industry," Meta spokesperson Andy Stone wrote on X, conveying his support for the effort.

articles.title: How infant deaths in Keralam’s Attappady expose a deep-rooted health, social crisis
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: 12 infants, including 10 tribals, have died in Attappady this year, sparking a political row as the State government orders an expert probe. Tribal activists say the crisis demands action beyond healthcare, addressing malnutrition, anaemia and deep-rooted social issues

The deaths of 12 infants, 10 of them from tribal communities, in Attappady in Keralam in recent months have once again cast a spotlight on a child health crisis that has defied solutions for over a decade. While the State government has set an expert assessment in motion, tribal organisations maintain that the roots of the crisis run deeper than healthcare, demanding sustained action on nutrition, maternal health, landlessness and the wider socio-economic conditions of the community.

Figures cited by tribal activists show that 124 infants have died in the region since 2011. Since 2012, Attappady has also recorded around 300 abortions, 90 intrauterine deaths and two dozen stillbirths. The region came under particular scrutiny in 2013, when 47 tribal infants died. Tribal observers estimate that around 10 children have died annually over the years.

articles.title: Meira Kumar chairs INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of CEC at Kharge's residence | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: INDIA Bloc says everyone united in protests, 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar today

Mallikarjun Kharge said the INDIA bloc was not fighting to protect “infiltrators” but for genuine voters, as he spoke at its symbolic ‘public impeachment’ of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar today (October 31, 2026).

The six charges displayed at the event allege that the CEC conspired to steal elections, deleted 13.2 crore voters, rewrote Form 6 without Parliament, seized the electoral rolls through ECINET, shut out the other two Election Commissioners, and acted at the behest of Narendra Modi and Amit Shah.

Ahead of the planned Congress-led INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, 2026, the Delhi Police have said traffic restrictions will be in place across parts of the national capital from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Sunday.
The traffic police have listed key diversions in Central Delhi, likely regulations on bus movements and suggested alternate routes to reach the New Delhi Railway Station.

Mallikarjun Kharge said the INDIA bloc had no personal enmity with Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and wanted the Election Commission (EC) to work impartially. He was speaking at the bloc’s symbolic ‘public impeachment’ of the CEC today (October 31, 2026).

Mallikarjun Kharge said Article 326 of the Constitution, which guarantees universal adult franchise, was under serious threat, as he spoke at the INDIA bloc’s symbolic ‘public impeachment’ of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

The INDIA bloc’s symbolic ‘public impeachment’ of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar began today (October 31, 2026) at the New Delhi residence of Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge, 10 Rajaji Marg, with former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar opening the proceedings. She said Mr. Kharge would move a motion to “remove” the CEC from office.
Mr. Kharge began his address by invoking Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Indira Gandhi, whose 151st birth anniversary and 42nd death anniversary respectively fall today.

Chhattisgarh Congress Legislature Party (CLP) leader Charandas Mahant, in a post on X (translated from Hindi), alleged that the BJP was snatching away fundamental rights and destroying democracy by “stealing votes”.

He said a “mega rally” would be held at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on November 1, 2026, under the leadership of Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi, and appealed to people to reach the venue and raise their voice to save democracy.

All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora said that if those in power had listened to public interest, the impeachment of the Chief Election Commissioner would have been done in Parliament. She was speaking on the INDIA bloc’s ‘public impeachment’ of CEC Gyanesh Kumar today (October 31, 2026).

CPI leader D. Raja, arriving at Mr. Kharge’s residence for the ‘Public Impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar’, said “tomorrow’s rally will send a message to PM Modi that the country cannot be ruled in this way”.

articles.title: Society that accepts unverified claims and fears questions is vulnerable to authoritarianism: Justice Bhuyan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Speaking at the University of Science and Technology, Meghalaya, the Supreme Court judge said building a scientific temper must extend beyond laboratories to the capacity of youths and students to think rationally, and urged a shift from ‘us’ and ‘they’ to the Preamble’s ‘we’

Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said a society that accepts claims without evidence, fears questions and treats tradition as beyond question becomes vulnerable to misinformation, defenceless in the face of authoritarianism and fails to reform unjust practices.

Justice Bhuyan said building a scientific temper enshrined in Article 51A of the Constitution should not be confined to laboratories but extend to the capacity of youths and students to think rationally as members of a civil and political society.

“All that you need is the capacity to think rationally; what you say or think must be based on reason. It [scientific temper] is an attitude of inquiry and openness to examination. It cannot happen overnight. The germination has to take place in the university,” Justice Bhuyan said in his address at the University of Science and Technology, Meghalaya on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

The speech resonates after the nation saw widespread dissatisfaction among Gen Z over NEET 2026 paper leaks, student unrest in universities and a wave of agitations across premier institutions from IIT Bombay to multiple National Law Schools followed by a demand to restore student union elections at Jamia Millia Islamia.

The judge said society should demand empirical evidence when public discourse relies on emotional resonance and unverified assertions. Students must acquire the habit of inquiry to see through misinformation.

“To inquire is to avoid accepting the very first explanation that comes our way; it tells us to look for reasons; and it trains the mind to search a little deeper than what appears at the surface. This is nothing else but the development of a scientific temper. This will protect the mind from prejudice and empower it to make independent thinking and choice possible,” Justice Bhuyan said.
The judge pointed out how society is willingly or unwillingly getting drawn into a “false narrative; the binary of ‘us’ and ‘they’”. He termed this a destructive tendency.
Justice Bhuyan said the narrative must shift from ‘us’ and ‘they’ to the ‘we’ of the Preamble to the Constitution of India, which starts with the expression ‘We, the People of India’.

“This Constitutional concept of ‘we’ enables diversity to coexist with unity. Its genius lies in the fact that it does not seek to efface the differences; rather, it seeks to restore unity without demanding uniformity. It does not require that our individual identities should get subsumed in the larger whole,” Justice Bhuyan said.

articles.title: Dhruv Rathee defamation case: Delhi Court issues fresh bailable warrants
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Judicial Magistrate Rahul Jain issued the fresh warrants against Dhruv Rathee in a case filed by Vikas Sanskrityayan, who accused the YouTuber of defamation over a video uploaded on his channel
A Delhi Court on Saturday (October 31, 2026) issued fresh bailable warrants against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in a 2018 defamation case.

Judicial Magistrate Rahul Jain issued the fresh warrants against Mr. Rathee in a case filed by Vikas Sanskrityayan alias Vikas Pandey, who accused the YouTuber of defamation over a video uploaded on his channel. The detailed order is awaited.
On October 17, the Court had issued bailable warrants against Mr. Rathee after a process server reported that his house was locked while attempting to serve notice.
The Court had also issued fresh summons to Mr. Rathee at his address in Gurugram, Haryana.
Appearing for Mr. Pandey, advocate Samaksh Sharma had submitted that Mr. Rathee ordinarily resides in Austria and had come to India for the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protests in Delhi.
The Court had noted that Mr. Rathee was initially summoned in July 2019.
The case pertains to a defamation complaint filed by Mr. Pandey in 2018 after Mr. Rathee uploaded a video against him on his YouTube channel.

articles.title: Infosys opens 1.1 million sq.ft. new block at Pocharam campus in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The new facility will add 10,000 seats, enabling the company to aim to support an additional workforce of over 13,000 employees under a hybrid working model, the IT major said after the inauguration by Deputy CM Bhatti, IT Minister Sridhar Babu
IT major Infosys announced expansion of its Pocharam Development Centre in Hyderabad with the inauguration of a 1.1 million sq.ft. software development block on Friday.

Spread across 450 acres, its campus in Pocharam currently houses seven software development blocks with approximately 4.58 million sq.ft. of built-up area. The new block will add 10,000 seats, enabling the company to aim to support an additional workforce of over 13,000 employees under a hybrid working model, Infosys said after the inauguration in which Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, IT and Industries Minister D.Sridhar Babu participated.

Deputy CM Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka with IT and Industries Minister D.Sridhar Babu at the inauguration of the new software development block at Infosys’ Pocharam campus in Hyderabad on Friday. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT

The expansion of the Pocharam campus by Infosys marks another important milestone for Telangana, which has established itself as a global technology destination, supported by world-class infrastructure, skilled talent and a thriving innovation ecosystem, the Deputy CM said.

“Investments of this scale reinforce Hyderabad’s position as a preferred destination for global enterprises and advance our vision of a future-ready, innovation-driven economy,” he was quoted in a release issued by Infosys. The expansion of the facility will create opportunities for the youth to participate in the next wave of technology-led growth, said Mr.Vikramarka, who is also Minister for Finance, Planning and Energy.

The Pocharam Development Centre supports global clients across banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), retail, Life Sciences and manufacturing. The expansion will further strengthen the company’s capabilities in AI, Cloud, cybersecurity, engineering and next-generation digital services, Infosys said, without sharing investment on the new facility.

Chief Financial Officer of Infosys Jayesh Sanghrajka said Hyderabad has played a pivotal role in the company’s growth and the expansion of the Pocharam campus reflects its continued commitment to the region.

“The facility enhances our capacity to scale operations, build specialised talent and deliver complex transformation programmes for global clients. As enterprises accelerate adoption of AI, the campus will serve as a strategic hub bringing together world-class talent, advanced infrastructure and deep capabilities to help clients drive innovation...”, he said.

Deputy CM Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka with IT and Industries Minister D. Sridhar Babu at the inauguration of the new software development block at Infosys’ Pocharam campus in Hyderabad on Friday. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT

On the features of the new facility, Infosys said it incorporates energy-efficient radiant cooling, smart lighting, rainwater harvesting, wastewater reuse and natural daylight-filled spaces. It also features flexible workspaces, collaborative areas and employee wellness facilities to support a modern, hybrid work environment.

articles.title: INDIA bloc Ramlila Maidan rally traffic curbs: Which roads to avoid, timing and more
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: For the INDIA bloc Ramlila Maidan rally on November 1, Delhi Traffic Police will impose restrictions from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., including key diversions and curbs on bus movements

Ahead of the planned Congress-led INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, 2026, the Delhi Police have said traffic restrictions will be in place across parts of the national capital from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Sunday.
The traffic police have listed key diversions in Central Delhi, likely regulations on bus movements and suggested alternate routes to reach the New Delhi Railway Station.

The rally is part of the Opposition bloc’s campaign, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities and cancellation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
As per a PTI report, the Delhi Traffic Police will enforce traffic diversions at key intersections in Central Delhi, depending on the situation

Additional traffic personnel will be deployed across the Central Range to regulate vehicular movement, guide commuters to designated parking areas and prevent congestion around the venue, as per the PTI report.
Bus movement on Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, the Rajghat-JLN Marg stretch, DBG Road and Minto Road may also be regulated, the traffic police said.
The police have advised passengers travelling to New Delhi Railway Station to plan their journeys in advance.
Those approaching the station from the DBG Roadside can take Chelmsford Road, Connaught Place’s Outer Circle, Minto Road and Bhavbhuti Marg.
Commuters coming from east Delhi can use ITO, Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Marg and Bhavbhuti Marg to reach the station.
A separate passage will be provided near Lok Nayak Jai Prakash (LNJP) Hospital for emergency vehicles.
Parking arrangements have been made at the railway parking area opposite the hospital, Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) parking lots and Rajghat, the police have said.

The traffic restrictions will be in place from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on November 1. The police have granted permission for the rally with strict conditions, and have directed the organisers to ensure that the rally remains peaceful and concludes by 5 p.m.

articles.title: Chennai Corporation directs engineers to undertake milling before relaying roads to prevent rise in levels
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Repeatedly adding fresh layers of bitumen and raising road levels must be avoided, Commissioner G.S. Sameeran said

The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has directed its engineers to remove the existing bituminous surface through milling before relaying roads wherever necessary, to prevent road levels from rising with repeated resurfacing as well as to ensure proper drainage.

In a circular dated October 27, 2026, Commissioner G.S. Sameeran said engineers must inspect the condition and levels of roads, their slope, and drainage arrangements, as well as the levels of adjoining properties, before starting work. Repeatedly adding fresh layers of bitumen and raising road levels must be avoided, he said.

articles.title: ISRO NVS-03 launch: 5 things to know about India’s new navigation satellite
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: ISRO successfully launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on October 30, 2026, restoring NavIC to a four-satellite, standalone operational status and advancing India’s push for an indigenous, more precise space-time network

India’s independent regional navigation satellite system NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) was restored to its minimum operational configuration of four satellites on Friday (October 30, 2026) as ISRO successfully launched its 2,250 kg navigation satellite NVS-03 from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota.

The satellite successfully separated from the launch vehicle and was injected into its intended Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO). The satellite is the third in ISRO's next-generation navigation satellite series, envisaged to ensure continuity of navigation services under the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS). This mission aims to revive and modernise NavIC.
Here’s what to know about India’s new navigation satellite, NVS-03, with a mission life of 12 years.

NavIC requires at least 4 active satellites to provide positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) services. Following clock failures on older satellites and failure of NVS-02 to reach its final orbit, the operational fleet shrank to just 3 satellites. Placing NVS-03 into orbit provided the fourth satellite needed to restore standalone navigation services.
Atomic clocks are central to satellite navigation and helps calculate exact distances by measuring signal travel time.

Older IRNSS satellites relied on imported Swiss clocks that repeatedly failed. NVS-03 carries a indigenously developed Rubidium atomic clock (developed by ISRO’s Space Applications Centre) alongside imported ones. This moves India closer to full self reliance in high precision space timing.

NVS-03 transmits on the L1 frequency band in addition to the existing L5 and S bands. The L1 band is widely used in commercial GPS receivers, which will make it easier for everyday mobile chipsets to access Indian Standard Time and NavIC positioning signals. The system is designed to provide coverage over India’s landmass and an area extending 1,500 kilometres beyond its geopolitical boundary.
NavIC offers two main services: an open signal for public navigation, mapping and logistics, and an encrypted restricted service for the military.
The latter provides high-precision data essential for guiding missiles, tracking troop movements and operating defence platforms safely, practically acting as a strategic asset for India.

Elaborating on NavIC’s civilian applications, the ISRO chief V. Narayanan said 10,400 locomotives and 64,000 fishing vessels are currently tracked in real time. Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, the agency aims to expand this to 1 lakh fishing vessels within the next six months. In total, 15 lakh tracking devices have been fitted across vehicles. When asked when NavIC would be available on civilian mobile phones, Narayanan stated this would happen once the full seven-satellite constellation is completed.

India began developing NavIC after Global Positioning System (GPS) access was restricted by the U.S. during the 1999 Kargil War. The first-generation IRNSS satellites were launched between 2013 and 2018, with nine satellites launched during that period. The newly launched NVS-03 brings the total of the entire NavIC programme to 12 satellites.
Operating an independent regional satellite system will ensure India’s positioning and timing capabilities remain secure during geopolitical conflicts.

articles.title: Congress will return to power in 2028, says Shivakumar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Calls for unity among party workers; sets target of winning all seven Assembly seats in Mandya

Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Saturday expressed confidence that the Congress would return to power in Karnataka in 2028 and called upon party workers in Mandya district to begin preparations from now to achieve the target.
He also asked party workers to begin preparations for the forthcoming local body elections, including Zilla Panchayat, Taluk Panchayat, Gram Panchayat and urban local body polls.

Speaking after laying the foundation stone for the Mandya District Congress Committee’s Indira Bhavan near Holalu Circle, he urged party workers to set aside personal differences, strengthen the organisation and work towards winning all seven Assembly constituencies in the district.

He said Indira Bhavan should not remain merely a party office, but should become a symbol of self-respect for every Congress worker. He called upon workers to contribute towards its construction according to their capacity, ranging from ₹100 to ₹10 lakh.
He also announced plans to establish Indira Bhavans in all Assembly constituencies of Mandya district and asked party leaders to take the initiative.

articles.title: Disruption of convocation at Maharaja’s College: Minister Roji says govt. will not yield to unacceptable protests
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Minister says a convocation ceremony carries its own dignity and decorum and that students are assured an opportunity to raise their questions afterwards

There is no ban on anyone protesting peacefully and democratically, but the government has no intention to yield or surrender to protests crossing those limits, said Higher Education Minister Roji M. John.

“I am not someone who views the act of raising a banner or a placard as a problem. Rather, I see such actions as part of the democratic process. However, certain norms and a sense of decorum must be observed when staging a protest,” Mr. John said while addressing the media here on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

The Minister was referring to the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) protest during the convocation ceremony at Maharaja’s College on Friday (October 30, 2026), when SFI activists allegedly disrupted his speech. The protest was reportedly staged to seek answers from the Minister over the suspension of 16 students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady.

The Minister said a convocation ceremony carried its own dignity and decorum. “A convocation ceremony represents a dream for a student as well as for their parents. We fully embrace democratic and peaceful forms of protest. I simply wanted to ensure that the decorum of such an occasion was maintained. That is why I asked the protesting students to wait, assuring them that I would answer their questions afterwards,” the Minister added, recalling the incident.

“Whether student politics should be pursued by disrupting events such as a convocation is a matter for the respective organisations to decide. In any case, we cannot agree with such an approach under any circumstances,” he added.

The Minister further said that the university, not the government, was responsible for taking action on matters concerning student discipline. “The university has the authority to do so. It falls within the university’s mandate to initiate disciplinary action against a student and to review or reconsider such action. It is not the government that makes decisions on these matters,” he added.

Meanwhile, students who could not receive their certificates directly from the Minister during the convocation ceremony have expressed a desire to collect them from him personally, according to a communication from the Minister.
On Saturday, Ajmi Basheer, an MA Islamic History student and first-rank holder, arrived at the venue of an event attended by the Minister and received her certificate from him.

articles.title: All arrangements in place for municipal polls across south A.P.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: All arrangements have been completed for municipal polls across the southern districts of Andhra Pradesh on Sunday. The respective district administrations, police authorities, polling staff and and micro-observers are ready to conduct the elections in a peaceful, free, and fair manner.

Tirupati District Collector S. Venkateswar, along with by Municipal Commissioner M. Jayakrishna, inspected the election materials at the premises of S.V. Arts College on Saturday morning. They reviewed the process of distributing ballot boxes, ballot papers, and other supplies.

“Special facilities have been arranged for pregnant women, nursing mothers, persons with disabilities, the elderly, and female voters. NSS volunteers will assist with queue management. Nearly 2,500 police personnel have been deployed to ensure security,” the Collector said.

In SPSR Nellore district, Superintendent of Police (SP) Ajitha Vejendla said that stringent security arrangements were being implemented to ensure that citizens can exercise their right to vote in a free and peaceful environment.

Following her direction, the police officials conducted on-site inspections of polling stations. They examined the infrastructure and security arrangements available at the polling stations and the surrounding areas.

Similarly, under the directives of Kadapa district Superintendent of Police (SP) Shelke Nachiket Vishwanath, the police officials conducted route march in R.K. Nagar and field inspections of hyper-sensitive and sensitive polling stations within Jammalamadugu and Rajampet municipalities.

The SP warned that strict action will be taken against those engaging in activities that disrupt law and order or lead to untoward incidents. He ensured continuous monitoring and robust barricading at the polling stations.

As polling is set to take place for the Ongole Municipal Corporation, as well as Cheemakurthi and Addanki municipalities, Prakasam District Collector P. Raja Babu, SP V. Harshavardhan Raju and Joint Collector Kalpana Kumari jointly inspected the arrangements for the municipal elections.
Polling staff check the election materials for the municipal elections at RISE Engineering College in Ongole on Saturday. | Photo Credit: KOMMURI SRINIVAS

“Of the 303 polling stations in the district, 100 have been categorised as hyper-sensitive and 107 as sensitive and based on the security scale determined for these respective categories, sufficient personnel have been deployed at all locations,” Mr. Harshavardhan said.

Markapuram district SP Pankaj Kumar Meena said that nearly 800 police personnel were deployed for election security duties to ensure the peaceful conduct of the elections in Markapuram, Giddalur, and Kanigiri municipalities.

Tirupati District Collector S. Venkateswar, along with by Municipal Commissioner M. Jayakrishna, inspected the election materials at the premises of S.V. Arts College on Saturday morning. They reviewed the process of distributing ballot boxes, ballot papers, and other supplies.

Polling staff check the election materials for the municipal elections at RISE Engineering College in Ongole on Saturday. | Photo Credit: KOMMURI SRINIVAS

articles.title: Jowar prices hit an all-time high in Karnataka amidst drought conditions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The price of the Maldandi variety of jowar has increased from ₹5,500 in September to ₹ 8,500 per quintal; Gundu Thene variety is priced at ₹8,200 per quintal, up from ₹5,000

On the heels of a rise in rice and toor dal prices, jowar prices too have surged in Karnataka amid drought conditions. Farmers, traders and agriculture experts say the current price of jowar, a staple in many north Karnataka districts, has hit its highest level in recent times.

According to APMC merchants in Vijayapura and Kalaburagi districts, the price of the famous Maldandi variety of jowar has increased from ₹5,500 per quintal in September to ₹8,500 per quintal at present. The Gundu Thene variety is priced at ₹8,200 per quintal, up from ₹5,000. Last week, the price had gone up to ₹9,200 per quintal for the Maldandi variety and ₹9,000 per quintal for the Gundu Thene variety.

While drought is the major reason behind the increase, department officials and experts from the university pointed out that the mechanisation of almost all other crops in the agriculture sector except jowar, and the fixed Minimum Support Price (MSP) from the Centre, are other reasons why jowar prices have increased compared with previous years.

Data from the Agriculture Department reveal that the sowing achieved in the kharif season was 0.42 lakh hectares against a target of 0.80 lakh hectares, or 53% of the target. Last year, in the same season, sowing was completed on 0.39 lakh hectares against a target of 0.54 lakh hectares.

Speaking to The Hindu , Santosh Budge, Assistant Director, APMC, Kalaburagi, said, “I have seen prices go up and down for more than a decade. But it is the first time that the price has increased to ₹9,000-9,200 per quintal. This week, it has reduced to ₹8,500 per quintal and I believe the price will keep hovering between ₹8,500 and ₹9,500. It might even shoot up to ₹10,000.”

Highlighting previous prices, Mr. Budge said, “In 2022-23, when there was a similar drought situation, the price had increased to ₹8,000 per quintal. Last year, in October, the price was around ₹6,500 per quintal and later decreased to ₹5,000.”

Vijay Hiremath, a jowar trader, said, “Currently, stocks in the market are also low for various reasons. Some farmers sell directly at the APMC, while others sell in the open market to traders of their choice for ₹10-15 more than the APMC price. Whether the prices will rise further or stabilise will be known only in mid-November, when the sowing of jowar for the rabi season will be completed across north Karnataka.”

Prof. Suresh K.B., an expert in post-harvest and engineering technology at the University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru (UAS-B), said, “Jowar is a kharif and rabi crop, but the Maldandi and Gundu Thene varieties are mostly cultivated in the rabi season. The sowing has begun now and will end by the second week of November. As a millet, jowar does not require much water. It is grown in rain-fed regions of Karnataka, including Vijayapura, Ballari, Raichur, Kalaburagi, Belagavi and Dharwad. Instead of depending on rain, many farmers adopt the residual moisture method. This means they sow jowar soon after paddy is harvested. The residual moisture present in the soil helps the cultivation of jowar. In the first 30 days, it does not require water.”

However, he pointed out that paddy cultivation had also reduced during the kharif season because of deficient rainfall and low water levels in major reservoirs. “We have to wait and watch the yield of jowar in the rabi season after the harvest,” he said. He predicted that prices might remain high until new rabi stocks arrive.

Shivanagouda Patil, Joint Director, Agriculture Department, Vijayapura district, said, “Vijayapura has the largest area under jowar cultivation, with 0.12 metric tonnes in kharif and 0.72 metric tonnes in rabi. But over a period of time, farmers have lost interest in cultivation due to the lack of mechanisation.” For instance, in contrast, toor cultivation is completely mechanised and offers better returns. While the Minimum Support Price for jowar is ₹4,073 per quintal, it is ₹8,450 per quintal for toor.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi claims 2024 Lok Sabha elections ‘illegal’ over voter deletions | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge lists six charges against Gyanesh Kumar, including facilitating vote theft, deleting 13.2 crore voter names and changing Form 6 without parliamentary oversight

After the INDIA bloc’s symbolic ‘public impeachment’ programme against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said discussions had been dignified and positive. He expressed confidence that the same spirit would continue at Sunday’s rally, adding that large numbers of people were expected to attend.

In a post on X, Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi alleged that the deletion of one in every seven voters from electoral rolls amounted to an admission that the 2024 Lok Sabha election was illegitimate. He accused Gyanesh Kumar and others of treason and warned of action against them.
Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi claimed the Opposition had enough evidence against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to ensure his removal, warning the BJP against retaining him in office.

BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad criticised Rahul Gandhi for holding a symbolic ‘mock Parliament’ programme, accusing the Congress of ridiculing constitutional institutions. He also alleged that Jawaharlal Nehru became Prime Minister through vote theft and challenged Gandhi to resign.

Speaking at the INDIA bloc’s symbolic public impeachment programme against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi, TMC MP Mahua Moitra accused the Modi government and the Election Commission of undermining voting rights, claiming that 71% of deleted voters in West Bengal were Muslims and 51% were women.

Speaking at the INDIA bloc’s public impeachment programme against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi alleged that the deletion of 13.3 crore voter names had undermined the legitimacy of the 2024 Lok Sabha election. He claimed the number of deleted voters far exceeded the 3% vote margin between the Opposition and the BJP-led alliance.
ormer West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee arrived in the national capital to attend the INDIA bloc rally scheduled for November 1 at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge outlined six allegations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in the INDIA bloc’s public impeachment resolution, accusing him of facilitating alleged vote theft, deleting 13.2 crore voter names, changing Form 6 and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah.

peaking at the INDIA bloc’s symbolic impeachment programme against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi, TMC MP Saugata Roy said the Opposition had followed legal procedure to submit an impeachment notice but was not allowed to raise the issue in Parliament. He also cited concerns over voter names being deleted from electoral rolls.

RJD leader and Bihar Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of orchestrating alleged vote theft at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. He vowed to unite against what he described as an attempt to undermine democracy.

BJP MP Sambit Patra defended the voter registration process amid the SIR row, asserting that only Indian citizens should vote and urging those whose names are missing from electoral rolls to submit Form 6. He said a declaration form had been added, but Form 6 itself remained unchanged.

BJP MP Sambit Patra criticised the Congress’s symbolic ‘mock Parliament’ protest, alleging that the first instance of vote theft took place under Jawaharlal Nehru. He also defended the SIR process, explaining the ‘ASDD’ categories used to identify voters missing from electoral rolls.

articles.title: Petrol export duty cut to nil, diesel levy raised by ₹3 a litre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The government’s fortnightly review raised the export levy on diesel to ₹11.5 per litre from ₹8.5 and on aviation turbine fuel to ₹11 per litre from ₹10.5, while India’s diesel exports touched 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025, according to Kpler

The government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) slashed the export duty on petrol to nil while hiking the levy on export of diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹3 per litre and 50 paise per litre respectively for the next 15-day period.
There was no change in the existing excise duty rates for petrol and diesel for domestic consumption.
Diesel exports would now draw a levy of ₹11.5 for every litre against ₹8.5 per litre it drew in the previous fortnight.
ATF would be subject to an export levy of ₹11 for every litre against ₹10.5 for every litre as mandated for the previous fortnight.
The revised levy on diesel assumes significance as India spiked its exports of the liquid vehicular fuel amid a global supply crunch, particularly in Europe.
According to data from real-time analytics provider Kpler, India’s diesel exports stood at 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025.

Sumit Ritolia, Manager for Modelling and Refining at Kpler, in a social media post on Friday (October 30, 2026) further observed, “India’s diesel exports are expected to ease to 500-550 kbd in Nov–Dec as seasonal domestic demand peaks before recovering to 550–600 kbd in Q1 2027. Higher maintenance in Q2-27 will constrain export, with new capacity contributing meaningfully only later in 2027.”

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

articles.title: Iran’s Supreme Leader warns U.S., Israel against new attacks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Saturday (October 31, 2026) warned the United States and Israel against returning to war, according to a written statement, following threats from the Islamic republic's foes of a possible resumption of strikes.

"If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for ending them," said a statement attributed to Mr. Khamenei posted on his website.

The remarks came during a reported meeting between Mr. Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi. It was the first reported meeting between them.
Mr. Khamenei has not been publicly seen since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's killing in U.S.-Israeli strikes at the start of the war in West Asia in February.
According to the statement, Mr. Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that "any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response".
It also said that Mr. Khamenei ordered the commanders to update Iran's target list to include "all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy".
The war began on February 28 with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran, which swiftly responded with attacks on countries around the region.
The supreme leader's statement came as fresh diplomatic efforts were under way to avert a resumption of fighting.
A Qatari delegation arrived in Tehran on Friday (October 30) for talks with Iranian officials, after Iran reportedly received a letter from U.S. Vice President JD Vance.
According to Iranian media, Tehran had yet to respond to the letter.

articles.title: Britain open to apologising for slavery, says U.K. PM Andy Burnham
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Mr. Burnham pushed back against the notion of financial reparations for victims of slavery saying that the British people could not be held responsible for historical wrongs; Burnham’s omission of colonialism ‘inexcusable’, said Tharoor
U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said his government is open to the idea of formally apologising for Britain’s historical role in the slave trade, although he ruled out financial reparations.

Mr. Burnham set out his position in an opinion piece in The Guardian on Friday (October 30, 2026), ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in Antigua and Barbuda, next week. There have, for long, been calls for Britain to apologise and offer reparations for slavery and its colonial past , including in India.

Some three million Africans were transported as slaves to work on plantations in Britian’s colonies in the Americas. Britain began abolishing the slave trade in its empire in 1807. Slavery was abolished in 1833 though not all slaves were freed until 1838. Britain “compensated” slave owners to a total sum of GBP 20 million or 40% of the government’s annual budget in 1833.
“Manchester’s cotton industry was built on the labour of enslaved people,” wrote Mr. Burnham, the former Mayor of Manchester.
Mr. Burnham acknowledged the calls from affected countries for a dialogue on slavery.

“By sticking our heads in the sand, we have damaged the ability of the Commonwealth to function,” he said, adding that it was necessary to have conversations on slavery to protect the future of the Commonwealth.
Mr. Burnham said the U.K. was “offering structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade”.
“Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process, and I am open to them,” he added.

Calls for Britain to make amends for its past have grown louder in recent days as Britain’s King Charles III tours the Caribbean on his way to the CHOGM. The King is the titular head of the Commonwealth.
In the Bahamas this week, Charles acknowledged the “great suffering and injustices of the past”, stopping short of an apology.
Bucking Palace has said that it was up to the U.K. government to decide whether or not to apologise.

Barbadian Prime Minister Mia Amor Mottley welcomed Mr. Burnham’s statement, even as she acknowledged that “views differ” on reparations. The British Monarch was the titular Head of State of Barbados until 2021, when the country became a republic. It is one of several countries asking Britain to go beyond an apology and make financial reparations for slavery.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Does becoming the Pope automatically mean giving up American citizenship? Can a foreign head of state retain the right to vote in U.S. elections? How does Pope Leo XIV’s dual status as the sovereign of Vatican City and a US citizen affect his voting rights?

articles.title: France heads into third weekend of protests as youth-led rallies sweep Europe
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween

France prepared on Saturday (October 31, 2026) for a third consecutive weekend of protests over living costs and education, deploying 70,000 police and gendarmes and rerouting the Paris march to the capital's edge as youth-led demonstrations spread across Europe.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween.

Paris police banned union and “yellow vest” marches through the city centre, ordering demonstrations to follow a single route along the capital's outer boulevards, from Porte de Bagnolet to Porte de Charenton. Unions and student groups challenged the restrictions in court, but lost.
President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday (October 26, 2026) that marches would stay out of city centres to protect shops.
Police also barred entry to Place de la Republique and Les Halles, both hit by rioting and looting on October 17, from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026) and Sunday (November 1, 2026).

Unaccompanied minors face a separate 9 p.m. curfew around the Champs-Elysees. A Paris court on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) suspended an earlier curfew on minors as a serious and illegal infringement of freedom of movement.
The movement began with high school students protesting school conditions and broadened into anger over living costs.

Authorities counted about 550,000 protesters nationwide on October 17, when rioters looted hundreds of shops, and 410,000 last Saturday (October 31, 2026), when rallies were largely peaceful but police made more than 1,300 arrests.

In Germany, a youth initiative called “Gen Z regelt” — roughly “Gen Z's got this” — urged protests in some 30 cities “for education, health, climate protection and an affordable life,” and against any return of military conscription. Organisers said more than 140,000 people had signed up online.

Berlin police expected about 10,000 people at the Brandenburg Gate. Some shops on the Kurfuerstendamm boulevard boarded up their windows, although authorities said they were unaware of specific threats of violence. Protests were expected to begin in the early afternoon.

In Barcelona, Spain, Catalan police planned to activate their highest-level alert after an anonymous TikTok network called Blocus urged new gatherings. Rioting there last Saturday (October 24, 2026) led to about 130 arrests, mostly of minors.
Italian police were on alert after clashes in Milan, Turin and Bologna, and calls to protest circulated on TikTok in Belgium, the Netherlands, Austria, Switzerland and Portugal.

articles.title: Iran says fishermen found after accusing U.S. of attack in Hormuz

fullParagraphs: Two fishermen from Qeshm, who had gone missing following an attack by the American enemy on their fishing boat this morning, have been found, state television said
Iran said two fishermen it had reported missing on Saturday (October 31, 2026) have now been found, following what it called a U.S. attack on a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz.
"Two fishermen from Qeshm, who had gone missing following an attack by the American enemy on their fishing boat this morning, have been found," state television said.

Earlier, state TV had cited a provincial official as saying that two fishermen had gone missing and two others were wounded in what he called an attack by the United States on their vessel in the crucial Hormuz waterway.
AFP has contacted for comment the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM), which oversees American military operations in the region.

articles.title: India’s first fusion power company takes key steps
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Designs for the first privately built tokamak, a nuclear reactor that uses fusion to produce energy, could be firmed up in 2027 by Bengaluru-based startup Pranos Fusion
If all goes to plan, India may see designs for the first privately built tokamak, a nuclear reactor that uses fusion to produce energy, firmed up in 2027.

Bengaluru-based startup Pranos Fusion has built PRAGYA, a small doughnut shaped tokamak, to test plasma control and superconducting magnets. This is a gateway to building PRANIK, a much larger tokomak that will have plasma heated up to millions of degrees — more than the interior of the Sun — necessary to fuse hydrogen atoms and create energy.

“By 2027, we expect to finalise the blueprint for PRANIK and be on our way to building a practical reactor that can produce energy. To be able to actually produce electricity from fusion is a further step away,” Shaurya Kaushal, co-founder and CEO of Pranos Fusion, said.

The company is currently incubated out of the Institute of Plasma Research, a body affiliated to the Department of Atomic Energy and the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), Bengaluru, an institute with the Department of Science and Technology.

Nuclear plants everywhere employ fission — a chain reaction involving uranium nuclei to produce heat that is used to generate electricity. Fusion, on the other hand, releases energy when light atomic nuclei merge, and usually involves joining two forms of hydrogen — deuterium and tritium — into helium and a fast neutron. However, this requires the fuel to be heated to around 100 million degrees Celsius, far hotter than any solid wall could withstand. In tokamaks, powerful magnets hold this superheated plasma away from the walls, keeping it hot enough for fusion to continue.
Pranos Fusion was one of the deeptech startups showcased at the Emerging Science Technology and Innovation Conclave held here last week.

“Electricity from a fusion reactor is still far away and would be expensive now, however the need for any source of energy is only going to grow,” Roshan George, co-founder and a Computer Science engineer from the Manipal Institute of Technology. “Fusion’s advantage is that while [it’s] nuclear power, it doesn’t need radioactive material like uranium. India already produces plenty of deuterium. Fusion reactions are also not chain reactions, and therefore the risk of a runaway reaction [like in a fission reactor] is almost absent,” Mr. George said.

The largest tokamak under construction is the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor in southern France, a collaboration between China, the European Union, India, Japan, Russia, South Korea, and the U.S. It is designed to produce about 10 times the heating power fed into its plasma. Bogged by delays, a 2024 revision moved the start of research operations to 2034 and full deuterium-tritium operation to 2039, adding about €5 billion to the cost. IPR manages India’s home-grown tokamak reactors, including ADITYA and the Steady State Tokamak (SST-1). It is also the nodal domestic agency to manage India’s contributions to International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor.

The cost of a private tokamak depends on scale, Mr. Kaushal, who holds a Ph.D. from JNCASR, and a mechanical engineering degree from BITS Pilani, said. A compact research machine like PRAGYA is “a comparatively modest investment”, while one designed to reach net energy gain is far larger. Private fusion companies worldwide have raised over $13 billion, he said, and the leading net-gain programmes have each raised hundreds of millions of dollars or more.

Pranos Fusion says compact machines, HTS (high-temperature superconducting) magnets, and India’s manufacturing base can bring costs down substantially. It is backed by Ankur Capital, pi Ventures and Industrial47, and has raised $7.2 million. HTS electromagnets are wound from materials that carry electric current with no resistance when cooled below a critical temperature.

Britain’s JET tokamak produced a record 69 megajoules of fusion energy in 2023, though less than the heating power supplied. In December 2022, the U.S. National Ignition Facility, which uses lasers rather than magnets, achieved ignition, releasing more fusion energy than the laser light delivered to the fuel. This, however, does not count the electricity needed to run the lasers. Magnets made from high-temperature superconductors (HTS) have reached fields of around 20 tesla in tests, making smaller, stronger-field machines feasible.

In an email, Mr. Kaushal said the company is structured in a way its technology generates value before a power plant exists. It has two platforms — JENGA, simulation, design and control software that works as a digital twin of the machine, and MAGGA, its HTS magnet programme.

articles.title: NASA telescope on verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission's chief scientist
An ageing NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower.
The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday (October 30, 2026).

Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission's chief scientist.

Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope's dwindling path.

Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning, yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. Swift blasted off on November 20, 2004, to search for some of the biggest explosions in the universe — gamma ray bursts and supernovas.

“We've known this day would come since before Swift was launched. At least in low-Earth orbit, what goes up must come down. And that end is catastrophic,” said Pennsylvania State University's John Nousek, an astronomer who led the control team.

Intense solar activity over the past few years dragged Swift down faster than usual. NASA hired Katalyst Space a year ago to mount a rush rescue. But the company's three-armed robot named Link ran into trouble after launching in July and got no closer than 7 miles to 9 miles (12 kilometres to 15 kilometres) to the telescope. Link plunged back to Earth in September.

Swift resumed observations once the rescue attempt was called off, discovering even more gamma ray bursts and other ultrahigh-energy events. But by late October, the telescope was too low to remain steady for observations, and its systems were shut down.

Its final tally — more than 2,000 gamma ray bursts and 1,400 exploding stars, not to mention a slew of comets, asteroids, and star-shredding black holes. The telescope's superpower was its ability to swivel swiftly — thus its name — toward erupting celestial events.

NASA considered Swift a first responder for the Hubble and Webb space telescopes and others that would follow its alerts and provide deeper investigations. Scientists are still figuring out how to fill the gap.

“Our fervent hope is that the lessons learned by the successes of Swift can be applied to new generations of space missions to accelerate our discoveries about the universe,” Mr. Nousek said in an email.

articles.title: Shetty Institute of Technology hosts TechNova and NextGen Hackathon in Kalaburagi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Shetty Institute of Technology (SIT), Kalaburagi, hosted TechNova 2026 and the AIC T-Hub NextGen Hackathon 2026 from October 27 to 30, bringing together 89 teams from educational institutions across the country.

TechNova, held on October 27 and 28, featured 26 teams from South India, with Robotics 2.0 among the major attractions. Winners in various categories received cash prizes ranging from ₹5,000 to ₹50,000.
The 36-hour NextGen Hackathon, organised in collaboration with AIC T-Hub on October 29 and 30, saw 63 teams comprising 220 students develop innovative solutions to real-world problems.
Pardha Saradhi of CMR College of Engineering and Technology, Hyderabad, won first place, followed by Smartronics of Symbiosis Skills and Professional University, Pune, and Latents of SIT, Kalaburagi.

Three teams – Technora Crews from SIT, Caffeine and Catastrophe from the Central University of Karnataka, Kalaburagi, and Core4 from NK Orchid College of Engineering, Solapur – were selected for further support from T-Hub.

SIT Director Anirudh Shetty said the events aimed to bring industry exposure, innovation opportunities and the start-up ecosystem closer to students in Kalaburagi. Director Shweta Shetty said such initiatives encouraged students to explore their potential, collaborate and develop practical skills beyond academics.
The four-day programme concluded with cultural performances, music, dance and other entertainment activities on October 30.

articles.title: Protesters smear ink on Addanda Cariappa’s face over his play on Gandhiji
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Controversial theatre personality and former Mysuru Rangayana director Addanda C. Cariappa was allegedly attacked and his face smeared with ink by a group of protesters during the staging of a play on Mahatma Gandhi’s assassination at Suchitra Film Academy in Banashankari on Saturday.

The incident occurred during the staging of Gandhi Hatheya Kicchu , organised by Rangabhoomi Trust (R), Kodagu, at Naga Links, Banashankari II Stage. Mr. Cariappa, who wrote and directed the play, was confronted by protesters who objected to its portrayal of Mahatma Gandhi.

The protesters, led by one Kushal Hanumegowda, lodged a complaint with the Banashankari police, accusing Mr. Cariappa of spreading misinformation about Gandhi and portraying him as “anti-national” and a “slave of Muslims” in the play. The complaint was signed by 14 persons.

The complainants alleged that the play sought to blame the Congress and Mahatma Gandhi for the Partition of the country and made misleading references to the “payment of ₹50 crore to Pakistan”. They also objected to members of the audience being made to raise slogans condemning Mahatma Gandhi during the performance.

The complaint further alleged that tickets for the Bengaluru staging had been sold on the black market in Mysuru. When the complainants questioned the alleged sale, Mr. Cariappa reportedly abused them using vulgar language.
The complainants sought legal action against Mr. Cariappa, the actors who performed in the play, and others associated with its staging.
