articles.title: First import container arrives at Vizhinjam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The vessel carrying the first import consignment to Vizhinjam since full-scale export-import (EXIM) cargo operations commenced at Vizhinjam International Seaport in August called at the port here on Saturday, marking the beginning of a new chapter in the State’s maritime trade.

The first import container to Vizhinjam was booked from Ningbo in China and arrived aboard the vessel MSC Sabrina III. It was booked by BP2G Logistics and Ship Chandlers Private Limited, a Thiruvananthapuram-based start-up, on behalf of the city’s business enterprise, M/s Alteir Group.
The consignment comprises a full container load (FCL) of engineered building boards used in the construction sector as an alternative to conventional plywood.

With import operations now under way at Vizhinjam, containers can be unloaded, cleared and transported directly to markets across Keralam. This will reduce local entrepreneurs’ dependence on distant ports, helping them cut transportation costs and delivery times. The revenue generated through cargo handling and logistics activities will also remain within the State.

The development is expected to create employment opportunities for customs brokers, freight forwarders, transport operators, warehouse operators and port workers, while strengthening Keralam’s position as a maritime trade destination, authorities said.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge lists six charges against Gyanesh Kumar, including facilitating vote theft, deleting 13.2 crore voter names and changing Form 6 without parliamentary oversight
BJP ridicules INDIA bloc’s mock Parliament, defends SIR, political double standards, and highlights alleged vote protection amid poverty claims.

articles.title: 43 women rescued in illegal human egg harvesting racket in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police examine alleged recruitment of women across States, suspected use of rented premises and links with fertility centres and ART banks in Hyderabad

Eight people were arrested and 43 women from West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and other States were rescued during simultaneous raids at four premises in Hyderabad as police busted an alleged illegal human egg harvesting and commercial sale racket involving recruitment, transportation and accommodation of women for oocyte donation procedures.

The raids were conducted by Begumpet and Saroornagar police along with the Special Operations Team of the Malkajgiri Commissionerate at premises in Prakash Nagar, Begumpet, Erragadda, Saroornagar and Gopalapuram. Police seized documents, mobile phones and other material, while the identities, recruitment circumstances and medical histories of the rescued women are being verified.

Malkajgiri Police Commissioner B. Sumathi said the investigation was examining how women were recruited from different States and brought to Hyderabad after being offered ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 for each egg donation cycle. “We are examining the recruitment, transportation, accommodation and medical procedures, including whether the required legal and safety protocols were followed,” she said.

During the investigation, the women reportedly told police that hormonal injections and medicines were being administered to them in connection with the proposed procedures. Police seized five vials of Humog HP 150 I.U. injections, a syringe, two needles, Primolut and Meprate tablets and other material.

Police said inspections of the premises also raised concerns about the absence of authorised medical supervision and biomedical waste disposal arrangements. The investigation is also examining medical records, informed consent, donor frequency, insurance and safety protocols, as well as the statutory compliance of fertility centres and ART banks under the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, 2021.

Among those arrested in connection with the Begumpet and Saroornagar cases are Amit Sharma, 44, described as the alleged main organiser, Nikkat Parveen, 31, an alleged co-organiser and recruiter, Reshma Khatoon, 26, an IVF agent or sub-agent, Meghavath Srinivas alias Sonu, 23, Jepray Pradeep, 27, Sk. Parveen, 42, Vijay Bhagwah Rao Salunke, 46, and Pankaj Soni, 52. Emirisheetty Durga Prasad, 42, a businessman from Saroornagar, was also arrested in connection with one of the Saroornagar cases.

Police said Amit Sharma had been operating from a rented premises at Prakash Nagar, Begumpet, for about two years, paying ₹50,000 a month. Nikkat Parveen allegedly recruited women, particularly from West Bengal, through agents and coordinated their transportation to Hyderabad.

The preliminary investigation indicates that organisers, recruiters, agents and intermediaries allegedly identified women in different States by offering monetary incentives, transported them to Hyderabad, accommodated them in rented premises and referred them to fertility-related service providers for ovarian stimulation and oocyte retrieval procedures.

The investigation is also focusing on identifying recruitment agents, tracing the transportation of the women, verifying suspected forged Aadhaar cards, affidavits and other documents, and tracing financial transactions and commissions. Police are examining whether there were instances of coercion, deception, exploitation or human trafficking and whether fertility centres and ART banks complied with statutory requirements.

The cases were registered under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Sections 29 and 33 of the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, 2021. Further investigation is under way.

articles.title: CM to open women’s policy summit on November 2
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will inaugurate a two-day women’s policy summit in the State capital on November 2.
The event ‘Her Summit 2026’ will be organised as part of the Makalkoppam scheme.

Minister for Women and Child Development Bindhu Krishna said the government aimed at announcing the new women’s policy on March 8, International Women’s Day, next year. The new policy was intended for women’s social, financial, and political empowerment for an equitable, safe, and progressive Keralam.

Employment-financial empowerment and entrepreneurship; political representation and leadership; education-health-psychological welfare; women safety and laws; and cyber safety are the five main areas of discussion at the summit.

articles.title: IOC says crude Q2 price volatile as procurement swings between discounts and premiums
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Anuj Jain, Director (Finance) at Indian Oil also stated under-recoveries on LPG is projected at ₹309/cylinder in November and ₹370/cylinder in December.

Crude oil procurement remained volatile during the September quarter, with Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) sourcing supplies at discounts of up to $5 per barrel and premiums of as much as $12, Anuj Jain, Director (Finance), told investors during a post-results call on Saturday.

The Delhi-headquartered refiner’s net profit more than doubled year-on-year to ₹21,630 crore in the second quarter, supported by improved refining margins and a brief decline in benchmark crude oil prices.
Mr. Jain said LPG under-recoveries stood at ₹184 per cylinder in September before rising to ₹229 in October. These are projected to increase further to ₹309 in November and ₹370 in December.

Explaining the volatility in procurement costs, he said crude purchases during the quarter ranged from a discount of $5 per barrel to a premium of $12 against prevailing benchmark prices. In the first quarter, the range was from zero discount or premium to a premium of $18 per barrel.
Effective procurement prices depend on several factors, including whether supplies are contracted on a free-on-board (FOB) or delivered-at-place (DAP) basis, freight costs and the grade of crude.

Russian crude accounted for around 55% of IOC’s crude basket during the first half of the fiscal, followed by supplies from the Middle East, primarily Saudi Arabia and Dubai, at 24%. Africa, including Angola and Nigeria, contributed about 10%, while Brazil accounted for 7%. Supplies from the U.S. and Venezuela made up the remaining 2-5% and 3-4%, respectively.
Around 87% of the company’s crude procurement during the period came through spot sourcing. Mr. Jain said.
Responding to a question on whether spot purchases entailed higher costs, he said such sourcing did not necessarily mean paying a premium, as prices varied across region/geography.
“Now, within spot you have Russian crude. Sometimes, we are getting a high discount, sometimes we are paying a premium as well,” Mr. Jain said.

“In the few months, we have seen huge, discounted crude coming in from Iraq. So, the moment it is available, we are buying huge quantities from Iraq also. That used to be our staple diet before the [West Asia] crisis as well.”
He added that procurement economics were also influenced by effective negotiations, which played an important role in determining the final price.

articles.title: Towards recognising women farmers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Maharashtra’s passage of the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, brings into focus the structural bias against the female agricultural workforce, highlights the need for a database of women farmers and using it to ensure access to welfare schemes

Picture a farmer. The image that comes to mind is of a man. But when one looks at who is actually farming, she is increasingly likely to be a woman. This perception-reality mismatch is caused by age-old practices of collecting data, designing policies and defining who a farmer is. It makes millions of women who work on farms, make agricultural decisions and contribute to production nearly invisible. That may, however, finally be beginning to change.

In July 2026, Maharashtra passed the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, through a Woman Farmer Certificate. This is the first Indian State legislation to give enforceable legal form to the activity-based, land-delinked definition of ‘farmer’ that the National Policy for Farmers set out in 2007 but never operationalised. The Bill arrives nearly two decades after that policy, and 15 years after a comparable law was first proposed at the national level (a lapsed bill introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 2011). It is, in effect, the culmination of three decades of women farmers’ movements backed by civil society organisations.

Maharashtra’s passage of the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, brings into focus the structural bias against the female agricultural workforce, highlights the need for a database of women farmers and using it to ensure access to welfare schemes

Picture a farmer. The image that comes to mind is of a man. But when one looks at who is actually farming, she is increasingly likely to be a woman. This perception-reality mismatch is caused by age-old practices of collecting data, designing policies and defining who a farmer is. It makes millions of women who work on farms, make agricultural decisions and contribute to production nearly invisible. That may, however, finally be beginning to change.

In July 2026, Maharashtra passed the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, through a Woman Farmer Certificate. This is the first Indian State legislation to give enforceable legal form to the activity-based, land-delinked definition of ‘farmer’ that the National Policy for Farmers set out in 2007 but never operationalised. The Bill arrives nearly two decades after that policy, and 15 years after a comparable law was first proposed at the national level (a lapsed bill introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 2011). It is, in effect, the culmination of three decades of women farmers’ movements backed by civil society organisations.

articles.title: Clashes break out between police and protesters in Paris
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween
The French government estimated that 320,000 people protested nationwide on Saturday (October 31, 2026) in demonstrations focused on high living costs, fewer than in previous demonstrations.

Mass protests on October 17 drew more than 500,000 people around France, and demonstrations on October 24 drew 410,000, according to government estimates. Organisers’ turnout estimates are much higher.

The Interior Ministry told reporters that of the 320,000 protesting on Saturday (October 31, 2026), 70,000 people are estimated to have turned out for the main protest in Paris, which police moved outside the city centre to reduce the risk of unrest around government buildings and tourist sites after a last-minute court battle.

This is the third consecutive weekend of protests over living costs and education, deploying 70,000 police and gendarmes and rerouting the Paris march to the capital's edge as youth-led demonstrations spread across Europe.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez had warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween.

Paris police had banned union and “yellow vest” marches through the city centre, ordering demonstrations to follow a single route along the capital's outer boulevards, from Porte de Bagnolet to Porte de Charenton. Unions and student groups challenged the restrictions in court, but lost.
President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday (October 26, 2026) that marches would stay out of city centres to protect shops.
Police also barred entry to Place de la Republique and Les Halles, both hit by rioting and looting on October 17, from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026) and Sunday (November 1, 2026).

Unaccompanied minors face a separate 9 p.m. curfew around the Champs-Elysees. A Paris court on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) suspended an earlier curfew on minors as a serious and illegal infringement of freedom of movement.
The movement began with high school students protesting school conditions and broadened into anger over living costs.

Authorities counted about 550,000 protesters nationwide on October 17, when rioters looted hundreds of shops, and 410,000 last Saturday (October 31, 2026), when rallies were largely peaceful but police made more than 1,300 arrests.

In Germany, a youth initiative called “Gen Z regelt” — roughly “Gen Z's got this” — urged protests in some 30 cities “for education, health, climate protection and an affordable life,” and against any return of military conscription. Organisers said more than 140,000 people had signed up online.

articles.title: Pakistan PM orders fast-tracking of development projects in Gilgit-Baltistan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The development assumes significance for India as Gilgit-Baltistan is illegally and forcibly occupied by Pakistan
Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has directed officials to accelerate ongoing federal development projects in the controversial Gilgit-Baltistan region and ensure timely release of funds.

Mr. Sharif issued the directions while chairing a meeting in Islamabad on Friday (October 30, 2026) to review the progress of development projects in the region bordering China. Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain also attended the meeting.

The development assumes significance for India as Gilgit-Baltistan is illegally and forcibly occupied by Pakistan. The region is also a key component of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), which passes through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.
India has consistently opposed the CPEC projects passing through territories under Pakistan's illegal occupation, citing concerns over its sovereignty and territorial integrity.

According to state-run broadcaster Radio Pakistan , Mr. Sharif directed the authorities to remove all bottlenecks hindering development projects on a priority basis and ensure effective coordination among the relevant institutions to expedite implementation.

The meeting also reviewed progress on hydropower, infrastructure and solar energy projects in Gilgit-Baltistan. The Prime Minister directed the earliest possible completion of the 100-megawatt solar power project initiated by the federal government for the region.
The meeting also discussed the completion of the China-funded Naltar power project and the installation of digital infrastructure in the region.
The Prime Minister called for regular monitoring of development projects, particularly those related to the energy sector.

A report of a committee constituted in July on the Prime Minister's directives was also presented at the meeting. It reviewed the status of ongoing federal development projects, hurdles in their implementation and measures needed to ensure their timely completion.
Mr. Sharif is likely to visit Gilgit-Baltistan on November 1, the state-run broadcaster reported.

Gilgit-Baltistan, located in northern Pakistan, holds strategic importance because of its geographical proximity to China and its position along the route of the CPEC, a flagship infrastructure and connectivity initiative linking China's Xinjiang region with Pakistan's Gwadar port.
India maintains that the entire Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, including the so-called Gilgit-Baltistan, are integral and inalienable parts of the country.

articles.title: Quad delivering results for people in Indo-Pacific: Rubio
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The group reviewed progress in turning shared priorities into real benefits for the Indo-Pacific region

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, Japan's Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong in Atlanta, U.S., on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting on Saturday (October 31, 2026).
The group reviewed progress in turning shared priorities into real benefits for the Indo-Pacific region amid plans to host a Quad leaders' summit in the Philippines next month.

“I was pleased to meet with my Quad counterparts in Atlanta and discuss the real progress we have made in turning our shared priorities into real benefits for the Indo-Pacific,” Mr. Rubio said in a post on X.

“As our nations continue building reliable and open supply chains, supporting next-generation technologies, increasing maritime cooperation, and securing critical minerals, the United States, Australia, India, and Japan are delivering results for our people and the nations in the region,” Mr. Rubio added.
Mr. Jaishankar said the meeting focused on giving impetus to bilateral relations.
“Appreciated @SecRubio’s hospitality in Atlanta for the @g20org FMM. Took stock of our bilateral cooperation,” Mr. Jaishankar said in a post on X.
This was the third Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting held this year. Earlier, the Ministers met in New Delhi in May and in Manila in July.
Moves are underway to convene a Quad Leaders' Summit, hosted by U.S. President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the ASEAN-East Asian Summits in mid-November.

articles.title: UN ends its Somalia political mission after three decades
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: UNSOM was established by the UN Security Council in 2013 to support Somali authorities in the transition to democracy and the rule of law after more than two decades of conflict involving militias, Islamist groups and criminal gangs

The United Nations political mission in Somalia ended on Saturday (October 30, 2026) after a two-year transition, closing a chapter of more than three decades of UN peacebuilding operations in the east African nation.

UNSOM was established by the UN Security Council in 2013 to support Somali authorities in the transition to democracy and the rule of law after more than two decades of conflict involving militias, Islamist groups and criminal gangs.
It started as UN Political Office for Somalia (UNPOS) in 1995.

In May 2024, Somalia's President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud asked the UN to end the mission ahead of the expiry of its mandate in October that year. He later revised the request, proposing a two-year transition period.
During the transition, UNSOM was renamed the UN Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS).

"Today is not an end to the partnership between the United Nations and Somalia-rather, it marks the conclusion of one chapter and the beginning of another," said Raisedon Zenenga, UNTMIS officer-in-charge and the UN secretary-general's deputy special representative for Somalia in a statement.
"While significant challenges remain, the closure of UNTMIS comes after considerable progress by Somalia since the early years of international efforts to support the country's recovery," he added.
The mission's mandates have been transferred to either Somali institutions or the UN country team.

The transition comes as Al-Qaeda-linked Al-Shabaab, which has fought the Somali government for two decades, continues to control large swathes of central Somalia despite a major international military campaign against it.

The fight against Al-Shabaab is increasingly threatened by international funding cuts, particularly after the United States withdrew all funding for a key UN logistics mission, casting doubt over the future of military operations.
Somalia is due to hold parliamentary and presidential elections next May, with persistent insecurity and opposition disputes threatening the process.

articles.title: Quad ministers express ‘grave concerns’ over economic coercion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Foreign Ministers from the United States, India, Japan and Australia on Saturday (October 31, 2026) jointly raised serious concerns about "economic coercion" like export curbs and practices leading to overproduction, in veiled criticism of China.
"The four ministers expressed grave concerns regarding economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions," said a statement from the Quad alliance in Atlanta, Georgia.

The group, seen as a counterweight to China in the Asia-Pacific region, also took aim at "non-market policies and practices that result in overcapacity," which they said disrupt global supply chains in critical industries.
While their statement did not name countries, these are criticisms often targeting China, which has faced accusations of over-relying on exports to boost growth.
It is also likely a reference to Beijing's stringent export controls on rare earths.
The ministers' gathering early on Saturday (October 31) took place on the sidelines of a G20 meeting hosted by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
China, which views the Quad grouping with suspicion, has pushed back against accusations of overcapacity.

The grouping also recognised the "importance of critical sea lanes, the uninterrupted flow of commerce, energy security, and the unhindered passage and safety of maritime crews and vessels without the imposition of tolls."
It called for "the absolute necessity to protect and preserve navigational rights and freedoms in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait."

🌐 International Affairs 📅 31 Oct 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Quad ministers express ‘grave concerns’ over economic coercion

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics

Foreign Ministers from the United States, India, Japan and Australia on Saturday (October 31, 2026) jointly raised serious concerns about "economic coercion" like export curbs and practices leading to overproduction, in veiled criticism of China.

"The four ministers expressed grave concerns regarding economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions," said a statement from the Quad alliance in Atlanta, Georgia.

The group, seen as a counterweight to China in the Asia-Pacific region, also took aim at "non-market policies and practices that result in overcapacity," which they said disrupt global supply chains in critical industries.

While their statement did not name countries, these are criticisms often targeting China, which has faced accusations of over-relying on exports to boost growth.

It is also likely a reference to Beijing's stringent export controls on rare earths.

The ministers' gathering early on Saturday (October 31) took place on the sidelines of a G20 meeting hosted by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

China, which views the Quad grouping with suspicion, has pushed back against accusations of overcapacity.

The grouping also recognised the "importance of critical sea lanes, the uninterrupted flow of commerce, energy security, and the unhindered passage and safety of maritime crews and vessels without the imposition of tolls."

It called for "the absolute necessity to protect and preserve navigational rights and freedoms in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait."

articles.title: Modi says Opposition has become destructive force; calls for unity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones for eight development projects worth ₹118.88 crore, taking the total outlay for the 31 projects to ₹426.71 crore

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (October 31, 2026) attacked the Opposition, saying it had turned into “ avrodh paksh [obstructive side]” rather than “ virodh paksh [opposing side]”, and underscored that the country needs to stay united.
He was addressing a gathering at the Parade Ground in Gujarat’s Ekta Nagar on the occasion of Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, marking the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
“It is our misfortune that the Opposition has turned into avrodh paksh ,” Mr. Modi said.

In a veiled reference to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s foreign trips, the Prime Minister asked, “Who is secretly meeting whom in foreign countries? Forces opposed to India are extending their support to whom? Who is speaking the language of India’s enemies?”
He said the nation needs to stand united against such forces and alleged that the Opposition wants to divide the people of the country.
“Social media is being used as a weapon, rumours are being spread, and India’s image is being tarnished,” he alleged.

“I said last year that we would not rest until the country was free from Naxalism and Maoism; that promise has been fulfilled. Though we have finished Naxals, the threat of ‘ dimagi (intellectual) Naxals’ remains very high,” Mr. Modi said.
He told the gathering that India’s next big steps include completely securing the country’s borders, stopping infiltration and demographic changes, and moving towards a secular civil code.
“ Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (One India, Best India) and Viksit Bharat are our two goals,” he said, adding that the country is proceeding on the path shown by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, he said.

Meanwhile, the Prime Minister inaugurated 23 development projects worth ₹307.83 crore to boost tourism and civic infrastructure at Ekta Nagar. He also laid the foundation stones for eight development projects worth ₹118.88 crore, taking the total outlay for the 31 projects to ₹426.71 crore.
Earlier in the day, Mr. Modi paid floral tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel at the Statue of Unity to mark his birth anniversary.
Newly launched projects aim to upgrade visitor facilities and civic infrastructure around the world’s tallest statue, which has developed into a major tourism hub.

articles.title: After ‘Arnab’, Andhra Pradesh may face another severe cyclonic storm
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The depression over Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 2; landfall is expected between Narsapur and Nellore on November 3, with maximum wind speed of 120 kmph

Just days after Cyclone Arnab left a trail of destruction in Andhra Pradesh, weather experts warn that the State may face another severe cyclonic storm next week. The weather system developing over the Andaman Sea is expected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 2.
A low-pressure area formed over the south Andaman Sea on October 29, a day after Cyclone Arnab made landfall along the Kakinada-Narsapur coast in the intervening night of October 27 and 28.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, in its 3.30 p.m. bulletin on Saturday, said the low-pressure area intensified into a well-marked low-pressure system over the Southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas of Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Andaman sea at around 5.30 a.m.

The system moved west-northwestwards and concentrated into a depression by 11.30 a.m. By 5.30 p.m., it centered over south-east Bay of Bengal, about 960 km east-southeast of Chennai, 980 km southeast of Vishakhapatnam, and 1,030 km southeast of Machilipatnam and 1,080 km east-southeast of Ongole.

articles.title: Eradicating corruption is collective responsibility: Upa Lokayukta B. Veerappa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “It seems all of us have collectively nurtured the demon of corruption within society. It is impossible to eradicate corruption solely through the Lokayukta or any other institution. Every individual in society must resolve to eliminate it,’’ Upa Lokayukta Justice B. Veerappa said in Belagavi on Friday.
He was speaking after inaugurating a pending cases disposal camp pertaining to the Belagavi and Bailhongal subdivisions, at the Central Hall of the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha.

“In these critical times, when the legislature and the executive appear to be faltering, it seems that the judiciary and the media, often termed the ‘fourth pillar’ of democracy, are also becoming increasingly ineffective. Yet, whenever injustice occurs in society, the judiciary and the press continue to uphold the Constitution by raising their voices,” he said.

“The Karnataka Lokayukta has left a distinct mark in the country through its impartial investigations and operations. Nevertheless, it is not always possible to ensure justice for everyone. Society and families should socially boycott those who engage in corruption,” he said.

“If corruption is eradicated, India will become a powerful nation. Society itself is responsible for the rise in the number of educated fraudsters. Society is heading toward a state of decline because people accept money in exchange for their votes during elections. Things will only improve if society changes. If we set aside selfishness and banish the demon of corruption, India will become the world’s most powerful nation. Corruption has now turned into a competition, and nature itself is sounding an alarm. We must realize this,” he said.

He quoted Rashtrakavi Kuvempu who had advocated Sarvarigu Sama Balu, Sarvarigu Sama Palu (equal share for all, equal life for all) . “This is in accordance with the spirit of the Constitution of India’s assurance of equal rights have been granted to everyone. We should follow this,” he said.

“However, even eight decades of independence, constitutional rights remain a distant mirage for a significant portion of the population. We fight solely for our rights, yet there is a visible lack of interest regarding our duties across all sectors. While we may take a pledge to work without corruption, we simultaneously engage in corrupt practices,” he said.

“As a result of the persistent efforts of the Lokayukta institution, the government has issued an order mandating the allotment of housing sites to all ex-servicemen and their legal heirs in their respective districts or taluks. This government order follows a year and a half of continuous advocacy. The process of identifying and distributing these sites must now be carried out on a war footing,” he said.

The Upa Lokayukta expressed concern that the filing of false cases , often by individuals acting as proxies, was delaying the adjudication of genuine matters and the delivery of justice. He issued a stern warning that complainants who file false cases against government officials could face up to three years in imprisonment. “The Lokayukta has the authority to take strict action against officials found to be negligent in the discharge of their duties. Officials should perform their work with diligence, caution, and integrity,” he said.

articles.title: Govt. sanctions special funds for alternative drinking water sources amid El Nino concerns
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State government has sanctioned special funds to ensure uninterrupted drinking water supply in view of possible scarcity due to El Nino conditions, Panchayat Raj, Rural Development and Rural Water Supply (RWS) Minister Danasari Anasuya Seethakka said on Saturday.

The government has approved ₹120 crore for alternative drinking water arrangements linked to Singur reservoir to cater to Sangareddy, Medak, Kamareddy and Nizamabad districts, while ₹1 crore each has been sanctioned for other districts to meet immediate needs, the Minister said.

During a teleconference with Mission Bhagiratha and Public Health engineers to review the drinking water situation and preparedness, she directed officials to expedite alternative arrangements using the sanctioned funds and ensure there is no disruption in drinking water supply.

She instructed engineers to map villages where Mission Bhagiratha supply is likely to be disrupted and areas where groundwater levels have depleted, and to make local water sources available, including hand pumps, single-phase and three-phase water supply schemes and open wells.
In scarcity-hit habitations, officials were asked to explore hiring private borewells and arranging tankers for water transportation, she said.

Emphasising water conservation, Seethakka called for taking awareness campaigns on judicious use of water and El Nino impact to the village level and for continuous monitoring of reservoir storage levels as per government guidelines.

She also directed officials to take steps for groundwater recharge, especially in areas like Hyderabad, Medchal, Khammam and Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri which received recent rains. Soak pits and magic pits near drinking water sources should be made functional to ensure percolation, and all ongoing recharge works should be completed within two days, she ordered.

articles.title: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit takes charge as 29th Chief of Air Staff
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The IAF accorded a ceremonial guard of honour to the outgoing Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh at the Race Course Air Force Station before he handed over the baton to Ashutosh Dixit

Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit , a seasoned fighter pilot with over 3,500 hours of flying experience on more than 20 types of aircraft, on Saturday (October 31, 2026) assumed charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff, succeeding Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh, who retired after a distinguished career spanning 43 years.
The Indian Air Force (IAF) accorded a ceremonial guard of honour to Air Chief Marshal Singh at the Race Course Air Force Station here before he handed over the baton to his successor.

Air Chief Marshal Dixit, who was serving as the Vice Chief of the Air Staff, played a key role in strategic planning during Operation Sindoor. He has held several key commands, staff and instructional appointments during his nearly four-decade-long career in the IAF.
Born on December 9, 1966, Air Chief Marshal Dixit was commissioned into the fighter stream of the IAF on December 6, 1986.

Before taking over as Vice Chief, he served as the Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee, at Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff. Earlier, he was the Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Central Air Command.
An alumnus of the National Defence Academy, Defence Services Staff College in Bangladesh, and the National Defence College, he is an experimental test pilot and a qualified flying instructor.

His extensive flying experience includes aircraft such as the Mirage-2000, MiG variants, Kiran, Jaguar, IL-78, Hawk and Tejas. During his career, he has been associated with several major operations and exercises, including Operation Safed Sagar, Operation Rakshak and Operation Sindoor.
He has also commanded a frontline fighter air base in the Western sector and a premier fighter training base in the Southern sector.

articles.title: Language skills key to securing nursing jobs abroad, says Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Language proficiency is crucial for Indian nurses and paramedical graduates seeking employment opportunities abroad, particularly in countries such as Germany, Japan, Italy and the United States, said Medical Education Minister Sharan Prakash Patil.
He was speaking after inaugurating an awareness programme on the online services of the Karnataka State Nursing Council (KSNC) here on Saturday.

Dr. Patil said Indian nursing professionals were in high demand overseas and could secure well-paid jobs by acquiring proficiency in English as well as the languages of their prospective destination countries.
He said language was often the only major barrier preventing nursing graduates from taking up employment abroad and urged students to develop the necessary communication skills.

Dr. Patil said the government had taken steps to make nursing registration and renewal services completely online to ensure transparency and convenience. Earlier, nursing students and professionals had to travel to Bengaluru and wait in long queues to complete registration formalities. The new system would enable them to access the services from their homes, he said.

Claiming that Karnataka was among the leading States in medical and paramedical education, he said the State had the highest number of medical colleges and more than 15,000 MBBS and postgraduate seats. The government was taking measures to maintain quality alongside expanding educational opportunities.

articles.title: Aavin to invest proceeds from sale of sweets in welfare of dairy farmers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Aavin will plough back 90% of the proceeds from the sale of sweets this festive season to invest in the welfare of dairy farmers, official sources said. “We have not increased milk prices, despite the procurement prices having gone up. We are balancing the welfare of the farmers’ cooperatives and our loyal consumers with quality goods at affordable prices,” a source said.
People have been supporting Aavin for its quality. Many corporates have booked sweets and savouries in bulk for supply in the run up to Deepavali, the source added.

All of Aavin’s major outlets in the city and elsewhere are already stocking 250 gram packets of ghee badhusha (₹205), nuts halwa (₹200), kaju pista roll (₹340) and kaju katli (₹280). The sweets come in assorted packets too – 250 grams and 500 grams priced at ₹240 and ₹475 each. They also have savouries – 200 gram packets of butter murukku priced at ₹95 each and similar sized packets of special mixture priced at ₹110 each.

Like in the previous years, Aavin is producing sweets using its own ghee, butter, and khoa at its Ambattur dairy. “We are following FSSAI norms and are ensuring that sugar is added in the right proportions. Single use oil is used to fry the eatables. We do not use hydrogenated vegetable oil. Quality check is being done at all stages,” another source said.

articles.title: ED searches premises linked to Mudrex, Instadapp over alleged ₹4,600-crore FEMA violations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Officials of the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) on Thursday conducted searches at three premises in Bengaluru and one in Madhya Pradesh in connection with an investigation into alleged violations of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) involving unauthorised cross-border money transfers through cryptocurrencies, particularly stablecoins.

The searches were conducted by the ED’s Bengaluru Zonal Office on October 27 under Section 37 of FEMA. The investigation concerns entities associated with cryptocurrency platforms Mudrex and Instadapp, which allegedly facilitated cross-border financial transactions by using virtual digital assets (VDAs) to bypass authorised banking channels.

According to an ED press release issued on October 29, the investigation was initiated following complaints alleging large-scale FEMA violations by Bengaluru-based RPAS Technologies Private Limited, which operates the platforms Mudrex and Saber.money.

The agency said its preliminary findings revealed the alleged circumvention of FEMA regulations through an unauthorised cross-border payment system using crypto tokens, particularly USDT/USDC stablecoins. The entities allegedly advertised instant international money transfers through cryptocurrencies without the required authorisation from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
The platforms reportedly offered services to buy, sell, and swap cryptocurrencies, as well as convert fiat currency into crypto assets and back, facilitating international transfers.

The ED said its investigation had identified large-volume over-the-counter (OTC) deals involving shell entities, particularly those incorporated in Canada, Lithuania, the United States and other jurisdictions. These entities allegedly operated foreign-based cryptocurrency trading platforms to facilitate unauthorised cross-border transfers.

The agency also alleged that the entities used foreign-based cryptocurrency platforms to purchase or sell foreign-based crypto assets and settle transactions through Indian bank accounts, in violation of FEMA provisions. It further alleged that expenses in foreign countries were being paid using cryptocurrencies in contravention of the law.
The ED said its preliminary findings indicated that unauthorised cross-border transfers and crypto balances held on foreign platforms amounted to more than ₹4,600 crore. The investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: DVAC searches premises linked to ex-Minister K.N. Nehru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The search at Mr. Nehru’s residence, carried out by a team headed by a Deputy Superintendent of Police, began around 7 a.m.

Multiple teams of the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) conducted searches at the residence of former Minister K.N. Nehru of the DMK in Tiruchi, and four other places in the district on Thursday in connection with the alleged multi-crore cash-for-jobs scam. Searches were also conducted at multiple locations across the State.

Headed by a Deputy Superintendent of Police of the agency, the searches at Mr. Nehru’s residence at Thillai Nagar in Tiruchi commenced around 7 a.m. Several DMK members gathered in front of his residence. The searches came against the backdrop of the Madras High Court clearing the decks for the DVAC to investigate the case filed against the former Minister.
K.N. Nehru cash-for-jobs scam case: Madras High Court clears decks for DVAC probe
What did the ED dossiers against T.N. Minister K.N. Nehru contain | Explained

During the nearly eight-hour operation, investigators seized a tablet computer and a few documents connected with the case, DVAC sources said. Mr. Nehru, who was the Municipal Administration Minister in the DMK government of 2021-2026, was present at the time.

Similar searches were conducted at the residence of DMK town secretary Murali at Thuraiyur in Tiruchi district, and the residence of a person named Mohanraj at Manapparai. Searches were also conducted at the residences of two individuals at Srirangam and Tiruvanaikoil in Tiruchi, police sources said.
DVAC officials also conducted searches on the premises belonging to Mr. Nehru’s brother on Tiruchi Road and at GV Residency in Coimbatore.
DVAC conducts searches at the residence of businessman J. Sekar alias Sekar Reddy at Gandhi Nagar, Katpadi in Vellore on October 29, 2026 | Photo Credit: C. Venkatachalapathy

The DVAC had registered a case against Mr. Nehru and others on the basis of a complaint filed by the Directorate of Enforcement (ED). In a letter to the then Director-General of Police and Head of Police Force, the central agency had levelled serious allegations of corruption in the recruitment of 2,538 Assistant Engineers, Junior Engineers, and Town Planning Officers in the Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department when Mr. Nehru was holding the portfolio.
In Namakkal, the DVAC officials searched the residence of former DMK MLA Ramalingam. They also visited the house of Durai, a relative of Mr. Nehru, but it was locked.

Searches were also conducted at premises linked to former DMK MLA from Vellore’s Anaicut Assembly constituency A.P. Nandakumar, and industrialist and former member of Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) J. Sekar Reddy at Katpadi in Vellore. It is learnt that the searches were part of the ongoing probe against Mr. Nehru.
Mr. Nehru said the searches at his residence could be a diversionary tactic by the TVK-led government in the wake of a spike in crimes in the State and a jailbreak in Theni.

articles.title: NIA takes over probe into alleged arson attack at Kadavumbhagam synagogue in Keralam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police cite suspected cryptocurrency payments, alleged reconnaissance videos and possible international terror links as grounds for a wider probe
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has taken over the investigation into the alleged arson attack on the premises of the 800-year-old Kadavumbhagam Synagogue in Ernakulam.
The move follows a directive issued by the Union Home Ministry.
Last week, the Kochi City police invoked the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) against Ebin Paul, the accused in the case.

He was charged under Sections 15 and 18 of the Act, which deal with offences relating to a terrorist act and conspiracy, respectively. The provisions were invoked in view of the sensitive nature of the site allegedly targeted by the accused.

The police found that instructions had allegedly been passed on to the accused by other individuals. He is also suspected to have received certain payments in cryptocurrency. The police further claimed to have recovered videos showing him conducting reconnaissance of the location and rehearsing the crime.
The accused is suspected to have been involved in three arson incidents in Ernakulam district. Investigators had also found indications that he had identified targets outside the district.

Alleged communications recovered from the accused’s phone, containing references to sensitive targets, including Jewish places of worship, were among the reasons cited for a wider probe by the NIA. Police cite suspected cryptocurrency payments, alleged reconnaissance videos and possible international terror links as grounds for a wider probe

The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has taken over the investigation into the alleged arson attack on the premises of the 800-year-old Kadavumbhagam Synagogue in Ernakulam.

The move follows a directive issued by the Union Home Ministry.

Last week, the Kochi City police invoked the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) against Ebin Paul, the accused in the case.

He was charged under Sections 15 and 18 of the Act, which deal with offences relating to a terrorist act and conspiracy, respectively. The provisions were invoked in view of the sensitive nature of the site allegedly targeted by the accused.

The police found that instructions had allegedly been passed on to the accused by other individuals. He is also suspected to have received certain payments in cryptocurrency. The police further claimed to have recovered videos showing him conducting reconnaissance of the location and rehearsing the crime.

The accused is suspected to have been involved in three arson incidents in Ernakulam district. Investigators had also found indications that he had identified targets outside the district.

Alleged communications recovered from the accused’s phone, containing references to sensitive targets, including Jewish places of worship, were among the reasons cited for a wider probe by the NIA. The police believed that the possibility of international terror links, the identities of individuals suspected of sending messages to the accused, and the financial transactions connected to the case warranted a thorough examination.

articles.title: Foreign Secretary to visit Kathmandu as plans get underway for Nepal PM’s India visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nepal PM Balendra Shah is expected to visit Delhi by the end of the year, in what would be his first bilateral visit abroad, as he has been focused on domestic issues

In a visit to fine-tune the details of Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah ’s planned trip to India, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri is expected to reach Kathmandu on November 4, along with newly designated Indian ambassador Sudhakar Dalela, a Nepali diplomatic source has told The Hindu .

Mr. Shah is expected to visit India by the end of the year, even as his seven-month-old government continues to deal with the aftermath of the devastating floods in the Bhote Koshi River while also planning a slew of administrative and political reforms.

If it materialises, this will be the first bilateral visit abroad by Mr. Shah, who rose to prominence during the September 2025 Gen-Z uprising in Nepal that overthrew the government of former Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli.

The Hindu had earlier reported that Mr. Shah, who belongs to the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) led by former media personality Rabi Lamichhane, had vowed to focus on domestic priorities while deprioritising foreign interlocutors. In fact, Mr. Misri was earlier scheduled to travel to Kathmandu to meet Prime Minister Shah in May but the visit was postponed, ostensibly because of the new leader’s resolve to focus on domestic challenges.

Subsequently, RSP chairman Mr. Lamichhane was hosted in New Delhi and met Prime Minister Narendra Modi on June 3, after which Nepal’s Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal visited Delhi on June 5, in the first Minister-level representation to India from the new government, and met his Indian counterpart S. Jaishankar. This was followed by the visits of Nepal’s Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle in September and Home Minister Sudan Gurung, who participated in the first BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) Home Ministers’ meeting held on October 13. Mr. Gurung also met Mr. Jaishankar before he returned to Kathmandu. Mr. Wagle paid a repeat visit to New Delhi to participate in a private media conclave on October 23, when he also had a courtesy meeting with the Prime Minister.

Despite the flurry of visits, the Embassy of Nepal here has been left without an Ambassador for some months since the previous Ambassador, Shankar Prasad Sharma, returned home. Diplomatic sources said that the appointment of a new Nepali Ambassador to India will feature in the talks with Mr. Misri.

Nepal now has a complex new process to appoint envoys, as the new government announced that top ambassadorial posts would be selected through a public application process. In all, around 4,400 candidates had applied for the vacant ambassadorial positions. Nepali diplomatic sources told The Hindu that Kathmandu is awaiting the agrément (diplomatic permission) from India for Nischal Nath Pandey’s arrival in the Nepali Embassy in Delhi. Of the top ambassadorial posts in 13 Nepali missions, three remain uncertain, while Mr. Pandey’s name, along with nine others, has received the necessary clearance in Kathmandu.

Mr. Misri’s upcoming visit is also expected to review Nepal’s requirements for dealing with the aftermath of the disaster in the Bhote Koshi River, which affected hundreds of Indian families as well, as many individuals remain missing.

The Foreign Secretary is likely to meet Mr. Lamichhane, who earlier this week paid a visit to Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand and the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati. The RSP chairman, who travelled to Uttarakhand by road from western Nepal, had described his visit to these pilgrimage centres as “personal and not political”.

“There are no political meetings planned. Since this is a personal visit, I urge people not to read politics into it,” he said, before starting his pilgrimage in his second visit to India in six months.

Mr. Misri’s conversations in Kathmandu may also include stakeholders from other political parties, though a final outlook on that is yet to be firmed up. It is understood that discussions may include a review of the Balendra Shah-led government, which came to power in March after the RSP’s sweeping electoral victory, defeating the Maoist parties and the Nepali Congress. Since coming to power, Mr. Shah has attempted several new initiatives, the latest of which includes an ordinance that will revise retirement age for government officials, bringing it down to 55 years from 58 years.

articles.title: Deemed ineligible: On the Supreme Court and SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court has pointed to the SIR’s flaws by design

At Wednesday’s hearing of a petition on the Delhi SIR in the Supreme Court, Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked questions that cut to the heart of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s SIR of electoral rolls . If an existing voter was “lax, inert or did not respond” to enumeration forms, was that a ground for the ECI to “forfeit his or her right to vote forever”? The Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the ECI was in “error” to force such voters, struck off for not returning enumeration forms, to reapply on Form 6 as if they were new voters. It asked why voters who had shifted residences could not just disclose details and why deleted voters could not fill enumeration forms belatedly. This is the central design flaw of the SIR as it shifts the burden of enrolment from the state to the elector, including those who have voted before, and treats a mere change of address as ground for deletion. The share of draft deletions recorded as “shifted” or “absent” rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in States/Union Territories in Phase 3. In Karnataka, about 84 lakh electors were deleted, marked as “shifted” or “absent” during enumeration. But only a net of 8.2 lakh, including new electors, were added during the claims phase, with the final roll being 64.5 lakh short of the projected adult population. Requiring moved voters to re-register as fresh applicants defeats the ECI’s historic mandate of widening the franchise, which was inherent in the 2002-03 intensive revision, where enumerators enrolled shifted voters at their new homes and the Chief Electoral Officer reconciled the old entries.

Justice Bagchi also mentioned that the Bihar judgment was not a “binding precedent” and that the legality of “logical discrepancy” checks, allowed only as an “interim arrangement” in West Bengal, had not been finally adjudicated. No statute or rule provides for judging a voter’s eligibility on the basis of family size or the age gap between voters and parents, which were two of the ECI’s ludicrous and algorithm-driven “logical discrepancy” checks. In West Bengal these checks resulted in massive disenfranchisement and The Hindu’s analysis found that in Delhi, Muslims were disproportionately flagged. But the Court should not merely issue managerial fixes such as extended deadlines or displaying printed lists in blocks, as it has in the past. The final SIR rolls are erroneous as deletions flowed from a flawed design rather than just lapses by the ECI. The dead and duplicate entries that the SIR identified should be removed and newly eligible electors added. Voters wrongly removed from draft rolls must be included again. The larger questions over the Commission’s SIR conduct and how its members are appointed must also be settled.

articles.title: Open to investigation: On the challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Public functionaries must not use privacy to seek exemption from scrutiny

The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases.

The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutory protection for their work, freedom of the press is constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a). The Court has also shielded newspapers from arbitrary state restrictions. However, growing mistrust of legacy media and the rise of independent content creators have made it difficult to determine who receives such protection. The Centre has also flagged this concern. Yet, carving out distinct categories is no easy task — a 2026 Reuters Institute report shows that the proportion of 18- to 24-year-olds identifying social media as their primary source of news rose from 21% in 2015 to 39% in 2025. A purely legalistic determination of these competing concerns may perhaps prove too onerous. Stakeholders must build consensus on a mutually acceptable framework where public functionaries and those handling public funds are not insulated from scrutiny under the guise of privacy. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw’s indication that he would meet editors is a welcome step towards consensus.

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary

Public functionaries must not use privacy to seek exemption from scrutiny

The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases.

The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutory protection for their work, freedom of the press is constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a). The Court has also shielded newspapers from arbitrary state restrictions. However, growing mistrust of legacy media and the rise of independent content creators have made it difficult to determine who receives such protection. The Centre has also flagged this concern. Yet, carving out distinct categories is no easy task — a 2026 Reuters Institute report shows that the proportion of 18- to 24-year-olds identifying social media as their primary source of news rose from 21% in 2015 to 39% in 2025. A purely legalistic determination of these competing concerns may perhaps prove too onerous. Stakeholders must build consensus on a mutually acceptable framework where public functionaries and those handling public funds are not insulated from scrutiny under the guise of privacy. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw’s indication that he would meet editors is a welcome step towards consensus.

articles.title: Any plan to restrict sale of liquor in hotel bars and clubs located close to educational institutions? Madas High Court asks Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice N. Ramesh poses the question after expressing shock over a 19-year-old college student having consumed liquor at a bar attached to a hotel reportedly run by the college management

The Madras High Court has directed the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise to spell out whether any norms would be put in place for licensing bars inside hotels/clubs located near educational institutions in order to prevent incidents of underage students being offered liquor and ending up in fisticuffs in an inebriated mood.

Justice N. Ramesh issued the direction after expressing shock over a criminal case registered against a 19-year-old college student for having allegedly indulged in a brawl with fellow students when they were consuming liquor at a bar attached to an adjacent hotel reportedly run by the college management.

The judge suo motu impleaded the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise as one of the respondents to an anticipatory bail petition filed by the college student and called for details regarding the licence issued to El Dorado bar at SRM Hotel in Potheri, near Chennai.

He also wanted the Commissioner to explain whether there were any rules, government orders, circulars or any other guidelines governing the grant and renewal of licence in Form F.L.3, and whether any of them prescribe a minimum distance from an educational institution, a students’ hostel or a place of worship.

The Commissioner was further directed to furnish to the court the distance between the bar and the nearest gate/ building/hostel of the educational institution measured along the path a pedestrian would ordinarily take, and whether the premises lies within a municipal area.

The officer was also ordered to state whether the proximity of the educational institution and the number of students studying there was taken into consideration before granting/renewing the FL3 licence to the bar in the hotel and what action would be taken in future.

Justice Ramesh also impleaded the SRM Institute of Science and Technology as another respondent to the petition and directed its Registrar to disclose whether the college management had any connection whatsoever with SRM Hotel and the steps taken by it to prevent students from consuming alcohol.

Taking note that three students who got injured due to a hit with a beer bottle on September 26, 2026 had been treated at SRM Hospital, the judge ordered that the petitioner should not be arrested until further orders provided he cooperates with the investigation and appears for inquiry whenever required.

articles.title: M.P. wildlife officials highlight Chambal region’s gun culture as probe into cheetah shooting goes on
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Speaking to The Hindu, an official said that the gun culture has emerged as a “crucial segment” in the probe and that the matter had been brought up with senior police officers

The wildlife officials in Madhya Pradesh have raised questions about the prevalent gun culture in the Chambal region even as they continue their investigation into the killing of a 19-month-old cheetah cub who was found with five gunshot injuries on October 25. The cub passed away on the morning of October 27 during treatment in Jabalpur.

Speaking to The Hindu , a high-ranking official said that the gun culture has emerged as a “crucial segment” in the probe and that the matter had been brought up with senior police officers in the region. The probe is yet to make a breakthrough.

“It’s a very complex dynamics there with almost everybody owning a gun so we will have to target this culture too going forward. There is need to review the criteria of issuing a gun license in the region and we hope there is some discussion about this at the government level,” the official said requesting anonymity, while calling for a crackdown on the illegal gun manufacturing in the region.
The conversation on gun culture coming up in the probe was confirmed by State’s Chief Wildlife Warden (CWLW) Sameeta Rajora.
Ms. Rajora said that all possible angles, including poaching, revenge killing or self-defence, were being explored in the probe.

On the evening of October 25, a cheetah monitoring team found the cub, which was wearing a radio collar for tracking, in a still position in compartment no. 748 of the Sheopur Territorial Forest Division on the border of Sheopur and Morena districts, about 50 kilometres from Kuno’s boundaries. During treatment in Jabalpur, five firearm metal pellets were recovered from his body, including one from his lung.

The two districts fall under the Chambal region, which was once infamous for its vast ravines and the dacoits hiding in them. Even though the dacoits are a fear of the past now, rivalries, high crime rates, and the tradition of owning a gun continue to thrive in the region. Morena is often in the news for its illegal arms manufacturing.
Officials from the region say a gun can be found in almost every household there.

The probe is being carried out by a State Government-formed special task force (STF) of forest and police officers, while a high-level team constituted by the Union Government also visited the area on October 28.
Sources in Kuno said that various teams had been mapping the area roamed by the cub for 15-20 days before he was shot for leads.

“Our teams have been mapping the area in which the cub roamed for 15-20 days before being shot and, more importantly, where he made the kills. We have also identified various illegal cattle camps in the area because it is believed that he was killed in revenge after he killed someone’s cattle,” an official said.

“So far we have not found any strong evidence indicating a poaching attempt, but it would be premature to conclusively say anything. We are making progress and should make a breakthrough very soon,” the official added.

articles.title: NHRC flags human rights concerns over parading of three persons in south Kolkata
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Commission took suo motu cognisance of the incident based on media reports and observed that the contents of the news report, if true, “raise serious issues of violation of human rights”

The National Human Rights Commission on Thursday (October 29, 2026) took suo motu cognisance of reports that three accused were paraded in semi-clad condition in the city’s Behala area and issued a notice to the Commissioner of Kolkata Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.

A press release by the Commission stated that, according to media reports, three persons were found in a semi-clad condition with ropes tied around their waists in Kolkata. The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, “raise serious issues of violation of human rights”.

“A day before the incident, an 18-year-old youth and his 19-year-old friend, who were reportedly seen with a minor girl, were beaten and humiliated by the girl’s family members at her house. The youth’s father, whom the girl’s family summoned, was also assaulted. Subsequently, all three were stripped and forced to walk naked on the road at gunpoint,” the release stated. The Kolkata Police on October 27 paraded two men shirtless in their shorts with ropes tied around their waists. The two were held on Monday (October 26, 2026) for parading three naked men, including two teenagers, on the roads of a Kolkata neighbourhood. The police paraded the accused semi-clad on the same stretch on which the accused had forced the family members of the youths to parade a day before.

Civil rights organisations such as the Association for Protection of Democratic Rights (APDR) raised questions about the conduct of the police, saying that police were trying to “normalise revenge” and give punishment which the courts must be doing.

This was not the first time that police in West Bengal have paraded accused semi-clad as part of crime scene reconstruction. Several reports of accused persons being paraded not just with ropes tied to their waists but also in vests and underwear had surfaced earlier from Howrah, Kolkata and other parts of the State. The arrests, mostly of accused against whom several allegations of extortion have been made, have taken place after the Bharatiya Janata Party came to power in the State.

On June 5, 2026, the Calcutta High Court had observed that the State has the authority to arrest and prosecute individuals but cannot subject them to humiliation. “The police... can take action according to the law. If found guilty, they can also hang him. But they cannot deliberately defame the accused in the name of arrest,” the court had observed.

articles.title: Hike to help farmers, says CM; Ashok accuses govt. of placing burden on people
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: While Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar defended milk price hike by ₹8 on Thursday, saying that the decision was taken to support dairy farmers, Leader of Opposition R. Ashok accused the State government of placing an additional financial burden on the people.

After the Cabinet meeting that approved the hike, the Chief Minister said, “The hike has been made to prevent losses to farmers.” He pointed out that input costs, price of packaging of milk, transportation have all increased in the past one year. “There was a demand to increase the price by ₹12 to ₹15. articles.title: ‘Show me one Muslim minister at Centre, BJP-ruled States’: J&K Deputy CM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: J&K witnessed a Cabinet expansion on October 27, with four new faces joining the Omar Abdullah Cabinet

As the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) launched a meme war at the ruling National Conference (NC) over recent Cabinet expansion and protests within the party, J&K Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary on Thursday (October 29, 2026) said the BJP, “which has no Muslim minister in the Centre or BJP-ruled States, has no right to criticise the NC”.

The BJP’s official handle on Instagram, with 338K followers, in J&K released a series of memes, showing J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah fighting own MLAs like Mubarak Gul and Abdul Majeed Bhat Larmi by editing the shots from gory Bobby Deol-starrer movie ‘Animal’. In another meme, the BJP edited characters from the comedy drama ‘Panchayat’ to show the heartburn the Cabinet expansion caused within the NC legislators, saying “endgame of the NC begins now”.

Countering the criticism and BJP spokesman Sunil Sethi’s description of “National Conference as Muslim Conference” over dropping a Hindu minister, Deputy CM Choudhary asked the BJP to identify one Muslim minister in the BJP Cabinet.

“Is there any Muslim who is a minister at the Centre or BJP-ruled States in the country. If it is about ‘Sab Ka Sath, Sab Ka Vikas’, why is there no Muslim minister in the BJP?. The party spokesman has no right point fingers at the NC,” said Mr. Choudhary.

The J&K Deputy CM also objected to BJP criticism over no Hindu representation in the Omar Abdullah cabinet. “I am a Jat from Rajouri’s Nowshera. Am I not a Hindu or Sanathani? Whatever I have become is because of Maa Vaishno and Maa Durga. The BJP needs to clarify if Jatts qualify to be Hindus or not. It should also tell us which ‘baradari’ are Hindus in J&K,” said Mr. Choudhary.

J&K witnessed a Cabinet expansion on October 27, with four new faces joining the Omar Abdullah cabinet. One Minister, Satish Sharma from Jammu, was dropped to accommodate more faces from the Kashmir Valley, where the party swept the 2024 Assembly elections and won 42 seats in the 90-member Assembly.

articles.title: A security deal, but not the end of the Arctic contest
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Greenland agreement strengthens American security while raising sovereignty concerns

The agreement signed between the United States, Denmark and Greenland on September 22, 2026, marks an important moment in the changing geopolitics of the Arctic. Greenland is an autonomous part of the Kingdom of Denmark. Under the 2009 Self-Government Act , it has extensive control over its domestic affairs, while foreign, defence and security policy remain with Denmark. Greenland came into the news this year because of the Trump administration’s repeated interest in gaining control over the island. What began as a territorial controversy gradually became a wider debate about sovereignty, security and the future of the Arctic.

The agreement, signed at the United Nations, expands the American military presence in Greenland while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenland’s right to self-determination. It brings, at least for now, an end to the unusual tensions between Washington and Copenhagen over the future of the strategically important island. The agreement’s entry into force is subject to the completion of the necessary parliamentary procedures in Denmark and Greenland.
