articles.title: Kauvery Hospital treats complex aortic valve disease using HANCHOR technology
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Aortic regurgitation is a condition in which the heart’s aortic valve fails to close properly, causing blood to flow backwards into the heart

Kauvery Hospital, Alwarpet, Chennai, has treated a 63-year-old man with severe leakage in his aortic valve using a minimally invasive procedure called transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), the hospital said at a press conference. The patient had a hole in one of the leaflets of his aortic valve and had previously undergone mitral valve replacement.

Aortic regurgitation occurs when the aortic valve does not close properly, allowing blood to flow backwards into the heart. Treating this condition through a catheter-based procedure can be challenging because the valve may not have enough calcium deposits to help secure the replacement valve. The patient’s previous mitral valve replacement added to the complexity.

The HANCHOR valve has a frame that expands with a balloon and a special anchoring mechanism made of nitinol, a flexible metal alloy. This mechanism is designed to hold the replacement valve securely in place by gripping the existing valve leaflets.

The hospital said checks after the procedure showed no remaining leakage through or around the replacement valve and no abnormal narrowing. No significant problems with the heart’s electrical signals were reported. The patient was discharged three days later.
Rajaram Anantharaman, senior consultant interventional cardiologist said the valve’s anchoring mechanism helped address the challenges of positioning the replacement valve in this case.
Asik Ali, senior consultant and clinical lead, Cardiac Imaging Radiology; Mahesh Kumar K., medical superintendent; and Kamal Kanth, consultant cardiologist, were also present at the press conference.

articles.title: CPI(M) has no links with online attacks against Mammootty, says M.V. Govindan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: SFI and DYFI have won a lot of nationwide approval in the fight against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. In that context, there is no reason to decide not to visit Mammootty, says Govindan
The CPI(M) does not have any links with the online attacks on actor Mammootty, CPI(M) State secretary M.V. Govindan has said, adding that “the party was for a healthy dialogue with everyone.”

At a press conference here on Friday, Mr. Govindan was responding to the attack on the actor from allegedly Left-leaning cyber handles after DYFI, SFI leaders met the actor recently. “The party has never decided to initiate any online attack,” he said.

Mammootty had been targetted earlier this year after a video showed the actor, who was visiting the Wayanad model township built for landslide survivors, telling CPI(M) Wayanad district secretary K. Rafeeq to move aside as people might assume that his visit was organised by the CPI(M).

“The SFI and DYFI have won a lot of nationwide approval in the fight against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. In that context, there is no reason to decide not to visit Mammootty. Not just the SFI and DYFI, CPI(M) leaders are planning to call on writers, scientists, artists, intellectuals and actors in person,” he said.
The CPI(M) State secretary described Mammootty as an internationally-renowned Malayalam actor whose recognition as an artist is of great significance.

“The Left front too has faced criticism on occasions. We see such criticism as constructive criticism. That is how it should be. The CPI(M) is a party that feels that it should have a healthy dialogue with the tens of thousands of people who agree or disagree with it,” he said.

On CPI(M) dissident and UDF-backed Independent MLA G. Sudhakaran’s criticism of the UDF government’s SARAL (Simplified and Accelerated Regulatory Approvals and Licensing) Keralam Bill, 2026, said Mr. Sudhakaran had shared the LDF’s opinion of the Bill.

“SARAL Bill is aimed at destroying our farmlands and major watersheds for the benefit of corporate interests. We don’t have to disagree when individuals in the ruling front, including Mr. Sudhakaran, says it is objectionable,” Mr. Govindan said.
The Bill was passed in the Keralam Assembly on Thursday.

On the UDF government’s decision to order a Vigilance probe into the land acquisition in Kannur initiated through the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB), Mr. Govindan said that Revenue Minister A.P. Anil Kumar had informed the Assembly that the acquisition was legally done.

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab updates: Cyclone wreaks havoc in Odisha, over 55,000 evacuated across 9 districts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu said the very severe cyclonic storm Arnab has inflicted a loss of at least ₹4,600 crore

Village and ward secretariat staff in Andhra Pradesh’s cyclone-hit districts are struggling to charge their phones and biometric devices, which they need to verify pensioners’ thumb impressions during the NTR Bharosa pension distribution on Friday. Many villages in the coastal districts have been without power for two days.
Konaseema district staff try to charge phones in the dark to distribute NTR Bharosa pensions before election duty on October 31.

Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar on Thursday said that Cyclone Arnab caused an estimated ₹500 crore damage to the power sector and that the government has intensified emergency repairs to the damaged infrastructure, with special focus on Palakollu, Bhimavaram and Narsapur, which bore the brunt of the extreme weather event.

Inspecting the cyclone-hit areas in Bhimavaram on Thursday, Mr. Ravi Kumar said a comprehensive assessment would provide a clearer picture of the true extent of the damages, and that around 1,700 personnel were engaged in the restoration works, with an additional 500 employees being mobilised from the three DISCOMs. Another 500 electricity employees from Telangana joined the operations.
Cyclone Arnab caused ₹500 crore in power damage; the government accelerates repairs with 1,700+ personnel, prioritizing Palakollu, Bhimavaram, and Narsapur.

In the wake of the devastation caused by Cyclone Arnab, the Congress on Friday (October 30, 2026) called on the Centre to lead coordinated relief and rehabilitation efforts with state governments, ensuring timely assistance through the PMCARES fund to all the affected families.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also urged party workers to extend all possible help to those in distress.

“Deeply distressed by the loss of lives in Andhra Pradesh and the massive disruption to people’s lives in Odisha caused by Cyclone Arnab. My heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families,” he said on X.

The Union Government must lead coordinated relief and rehabilitation efforts with state governments, ensuring timely assistance through the PMCARES fund to all the affected families, Mr. Kharge said. -- PTI
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to expedite restoration works in areas affected by Cyclone Arnab.

The Chief Minister reviewed relief and restoration operations with the Chief Secretary, senior officials and district collectors following an aerial survey of cyclone-affected areas. Officials briefed him on the ground situation and progress of restoration works.

“Officials should speed up power supply restoration and road repairs in cyclone-hit areas and ensure that all essential services are restored at the earliest,” Naidu said in an official release late on Thursday.

articles.title: Seeman hints at contesting in Ambasamudram bypoll
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The NTK chief says his party will launch its byelection campaign from Palayamkottai on November 26, the birthday of the slain LTTE leader Velupillai Prabhakaran

Even as speculations are rife that the AIADMK and the DMK would refrain from contesting in the Ambasamudram bypoll to facilitate direct tussle between Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) and the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), chief coordinator Seeman has hinted that he would contest in this upcoming byelection.

Mr. Seeman has announced that the NTK’s byelection campaign would start with the birthday celebrations of LTTE supremo Velupillai Prabhakaran in Palayamkottai on November 26 and subsequent public meeting to be organised in Ambasamudram on the next day to mark LTTE’s “Maaveerar Dhinam” (Heroes Day).

The Ambasamduram bypoll has been necessitated with the resignation of AIADMK candidate Esakki Subaya , who joined the ruling TVK. In the last Assembly polls held this year, NTK candidate V. Sivasankaran had polled 14,906 votes while the TVK’s S. Rajagopal bagged 53,611 votes to come third in the race.

Speaking to reporters here on Thursday (October 29, 2026) after appearing before a court in connection with a case pending against him, Mr. Seeman said the NTK, which had contested byelections in the past, would enter the fray in all upcoming five bypolls without waiting for the announcement of a “common candidate.”

The NTK chief attributed the victory of Mr. Vijay and the TVK to “media hype” and said the beleaguered TVK chief had arrested former Minister Anbil Poyyamozhi Mahesh and searching the properties of another former Minister K.N. Nehru in a bid to get rid of them from the Tiruchi East bypoll scene.
He criticised the State government for gifting gold rings to the babies born in government hospitals instead of equipping the hospitals with modern facilities.

articles.title: Stalin slams Vijay govt. over law and order, rising prices; says DMK to hold protest on October 31
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “Isn’t the Chief Minister directly responsible for the Police department? Shouldn’t he hold review meetings with Police officials and issue appropriate directions?” the DMK president asked

DMK president M.K. Stalin on Friday (October 30, 2026) accused the TVK-led government headed by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay of “being incompetent and ruining law and order” in the State. He said criminals have absolutely no fear of the government.

To condemn the deterioration of law and order, the lack of safety for women and children, and the unprecedented rise in prices, the DMK women’s wing would organise protests at district headquarters across Tamil Nadu on Saturday (October 31), he announced.

In a video message on X, Mr. Stalin said whenever he addressed people, he would begin by asking them how they were doing. “But considering the present situation in Tamil Nadu, if I ask how are you, people will ask me whether I am making fun of them.”

Referring to the speeches made by Mr. Vijay as TVK president at public meetings before the 2026 Assembly elections, in which he had accused the DMK government of allowing law and order to deteriorate, failing to ensure the safety of women and children, and allowing crimes under the influence of narcotic substances, Mr. Stalin questioned, “What is the situation now under the government whose leader spoke punch dialogues so loudly?”

Murders, sexual assaults, and the killing of elderly people living alone in their homes to rob them of their jewellery had become routine. Minor girls continued to go missing. Murders were taking place even in some of Chennai’s prominent neighbourhoods, including Mylapore, Adyar, and Taramani, Mr. Stalin said.
Mr. Stalin alleged those who committed murders in broad daylight in the middle of the road were leaving the scene without any panic, boarding motorcycles and autorickshaws.

“We do not know whether the Chief Minister is watching these visuals. There is reason to doubt whether these reports are even reaching him. His actions suggest that nothing of this sort is happening in Tamil Nadu. All political parties issue statements, condemn the incidents, and organise protests. But there has been no response from the Chief Minister,” he said.

“Isn’t the Chief Minister directly responsible for the Police department? Shouldn’t he answer these questions? Shouldn’t he hold review meetings with Police officials and issue appropriate directions? But none of this appears to be happening,” the DMK president charged.

Only a few Ministers were responding on behalf of all departments, and even their responses were “irresponsible”, he said. Despite being in power for nearly six months, whenever issues arose, the government seemed to turn to the DMK and blame it for everything, he alleged.

“What is particularly worrying is that nearly half of the criminal incidents involve members of the TVK. The Chief Minister need not go anywhere to restore law and order. If he simply keeps members of his own party under control, crime could be reduced considerably. Women do not need to be protected by the TVK. Rather, women need to be protected from the TVK,” he said.

Referring to the arrest of TVK functionary Boopalan by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence in Nagapattinam on charges of trafficking methamphetamine, Mr. Stalin said when journalists reported the news, a TVK union secretary threatened them. “Is this what a pure force is?” Mr. Stalin asked.
“Was the money earned by Boopalan through drug trafficking used to finance the party’s election expenditure in Nagapattinam district and other districts?” he asked.

articles.title: Bangladesh police recovers body of ex-Air Force officer from river in Dhaka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Air Force Flight Lieutenant K.M. Tahsif Souri reportedly filmed a video showing deposed P.M. Sheikh Hasina leaving Bangladesh in an Air Force aircraft on August 5, 2024, according to local media

Bangladesh police on Thursday (October 30, 2026) said they have recovered the body of former Air Force Flight Lieutenant K.M. Tahsif Souri from the Turag River in the capital, a day after he went missing.
Mr. Souri, who was in his late 20s, reportedly filmed a video showing deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina leaving Bangladesh in an Air Force aircraft on August 5, 2024, according to local media.

Tongi River Police Outpost officer-in-charge Firoz Uddin said police recovered the body from the Rajabari Ghat area of the Turag River after receiving information on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) afternoon. The deceased was wearing white trousers and a black shirt.
The body was later sent to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital for an autopsy, he said.
He evaded a direct answer when asked if there were any injury marks on the body.
A phone and a wristwatch found with the body helped establish his identity, the Daily Star newspaper reported.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed declined to comment when asked if the incident could have stemmed from any hostility linked to the release of the video of the former Prime Minister's departure.

Bangla-language newspaper Prothom Alo reported that Mr. Souri spent the entire day shopping with his mother on Tuesday (October 27, 2026). He left home in the evening after a friend called him. At night, Mr. Souri sent a message to his mother, saying he was returning home, but never returned.
Mr. Souri was dismissed from service in August 2024 and was reportedly under intelligence surveillance.
In a social media podcast in July, Mr. Souri was asked if he lost his job because of filming the video of Hasina's departure. He briefly replied, “could be”.
In a statement in August last year, the Army said Mr. Souri had been retired in accordance with institutional rules under different circumstances and without any allegations against him.

articles.title: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov arrives in U.S. for G20 meeting
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Moscow has said that Foreign Minister Lavrov would use his speech in the G20 meeting to argue against international sanctions
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov arrived in the United States to attend a meeting of G20 Foreign Ministers in Atlanta, state-owned TASS news agency reported on Friday (October 30, 2026).
The two-day gathering of major economies comes at a time of stalemates on various fronts — from the U.S.-Iran war to fighting in Ukraine — all while oil prices stay high.

The Foreign Ministers' talks in Atlanta, Georgia, also takes place just days before crucial U.S. midterm elections , and will set the stage for the December G20 leaders' summit in Miami at President Donald Trump's Doral resort.

Moscow said Thursday (October 29, 2026) that Mr. Lavrov would use his speech there to argue against international sanctions. It comes ahead of fresh talks between officials from Moscow, Kyiv and Washington on trying to broker an end to the Ukraine war.

articles.title: Glacial lake outburst in Bhutan triggers flood alert in northern West Bengal, Assam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Following reports of flash floods in the river’s upper reaches, water levels in the Sankosh could rise suddenly in Assam’s Dhubri and West Bengal’s Alipurduar districts, says advisory

A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) in Bhutan has triggered a high flood alert in parts of northern West Bengal, prompting evacuations in areas along the Sankosh River and its tributaries amid fears of a sudden rise in water levels, officials said on Friday (October 30, 2026).
Residents of riverbank villages in Alipurduar district were seen leaving their homes with their cattle after the administration issued evacuation instructions.

Water Resources Investigation and Development Minister Nisith Pramanik said a glacial outburst had occurred at Lemthang in Bhutan, with water from the lake flowing through the Mo (Mofu) River towards the Sankosh.

“Everyone living in the catchment areas of the Sankosh River and all its connected tributaries has been asked to move to a safe distance immediately to protect their lives,” Mr. Pramanik said in a video message.
He urged residents living near riverbeds in Tufanganj and adjoining areas in Cooch Behar to evacuate immediately in view of the potential flooding.

He said the administration was prepared to deal with any eventuality, with teams of the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) kept on alert for rescue and relief operations.

A glacier lake outburst flood (GLOF) which has originated from the Sintaphu lake at Mochu subbasin Gasa has been reported. The NCHM is currently monitoring the water level along the Mochu river at Tashithang. India has been informed. https://t.co/ArS7S73wd2
Darjeeling MP Raju Bista urged people in the Darjeeling hills, Terai and Dooars regions to remain vigilant and follow official advisories.

Nearly 7.4 million cubic metres of water had surged out of the breached Shintaphu Lake in Bhutan into the Mo River, raising fears of a sudden increase in the water level of the Sankosh, which flows along the West Bengal-Assam border.

“The administration began evacuation measures late Thursday night (October 29) in villages along the Sankosh. Loudspeaker announcements were made in riverbank settlements under the Rampur-I gram panchayat area, asking residents to leave their homes and move to designated shelters,” officials said.

VIDEO | West Bengal: State authorities have issued high-alert and evacuation warnings for residents living along the Sankosh River following a Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) in neighboring Bhutan. State Forest and Environment Minister Manoj Kumar Oraon said, "Anyone who can is urged to immediately warn others in the affected areas. Special alerts are directed at the forest villages and hamlets bordering the Sankosh River, including the upper Sankosh forest village, the NKC Sankosh Tea Garden, Kumargram CD block, Chengmari, Valka Barabisa, Jharaguri and Pakriguri. If you reside along the banks of the Sankosh River in these vast stretches, please inform everyone around you as quickly as possible. A dam in Bhutan has breached. The floodwaters are expected to surge downstream within the next 1 to 1.5 hours. Please pass the word along without delay and evacuate people from these adjacent low-lying areas to safer ground, as the situation could turn critical. We must act quickly to prevent a disastrous situation like the one seen in Nepal." (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd)
The surge could reach border areas within six to eight hours, potentially inundating vulnerable settlements in West Bengal and Assam, they said.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Israeli media reported that members of Mr. Netanyahu's party were accusing Qatar — a country that many Israelis view as a patron of Hamas, the Gaza-based militant group

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu' s party has amplified unsubstantiated allegations that Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, potentially with foreign assistance, as final results showed his bloc had lost its majority in parliament.

The opposition accused Mr. Netanyahu of demonising the Arab population after a historic showing by Arab-led parties in an attempt to delegitimise the election. If the rest of the opposition teams up with Arab parties, a rare and politically risky move, they could potentially form a majority government in parliament, the Knesset.

Results released by election officials on Thursday (October 29, 2026) showed Mr. Netanyahu's bloc winning 53 seats in the 120-member assembly, well below the 68 seats it had controlled at its peak in the previous parliament. His main opposition won 48 seats and Arab-led parties secured the other 19.
The count is complete, but the results still need to be certified and submitted to the country's president next Wednesday (October 28).

Mr. Netanyahu's party, Likud, has been spreading claims of malfeasance by Arab-led parties since exit polls indicated the Prime Minister had suffered a setback in Tuesday's (October 27) vote. But it ramped up the rhetoric after the head of Israel's election committee, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, said that “serious suspicions” of foreign interference had been brought before him.
In a letter to the Shin Bet security agency, Mr. Sohlberg said he could not verify the claims. But given their serious nature, he asked the agency to investigate.

Mr. Netanyahu's party responded with an inflammatory statement: "The elections in Israel have been stolen!” it said, claiming — without evidence — that the alleged election interference was “aimed at facilitating a foreign takeover of the Knesset, the Islamisation of Israel and toppling of the right wing government.”
Israeli media reported that members of Mr. Netanyahu's party were accusing Qatar — a country that many Israelis view as a patron of Hamas, the Gaza-based militant group.
Qatar issued a quick denial, calling the allegations “ridiculous and dangerous.”

As it announced its results early on Wednesday (October 28), the election commission said the investigation was based on classified intelligence. It did not elaborate but warned of “unfounded” reports surrounding the probe.
“It does not affect the final results that will be submitted to the President, nor does it concern any particular sector of the population,” it said.
Mr. Netanyahu's main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, said Likud was trying to delegitimise the results. “They are doing this because they lost,” he said.

articles.title: North Korea's Kim calls for rapid expansion of drone technology, observes testing of weapons
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: In a speech at the exhibition, Mr. Kim stressed the need to seize “the absolute superiority in the drone technology” and announced unspecified steps needed to “rapidly expand and strengthen the unmanned aeronautical technology,” says Korean Central News Agency

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for rapidly expanding the country's drone technology and observed tests of various weapons, state media reported Friday (October 30, 2026), as his nation remains embroiled in a standoff with rival South Korea along their heavily fortified border.

Acquiring advanced drones is a top priority for Mr. Kim, who now wants to beef up both conventional and nuclear capabilities. Experts say his troops dispatched to Russia to support its war against Ukraine have likely gained valuable expertise in drone warfare from Russian forces and related battlefield experiences.

The North’s official Korean Central News Agency said that Mr. Kim on Thursday (October 29) visited an exhibition of a variety of attack and other drones that show recent achievements in the field of unmanned aeronautical technology.

In a speech at the exhibition, Mr. Kim stressed the need to seize “the absolute superiority in the drone technology” and announced unspecified steps needed to “rapidly expand and strengthen the unmanned aeronautical technology,” KCNA said.

To mark the event, KCNA said that North Korea later conducted test launches of various drones, missiles and weapons from the 600 mm-calibre ultra-precision multiple rocket launchers. KCNA photos showed Mr. Kim watching soaring weapons or him clenching his fist while his teenage daughter was clapping her hands beside him. South Korea's spy agency assesses that the girl, reportedly about 13, is likely Mr. Kim's heir.

South Korea's military earlier said it detected the launches of about 10 short-range ballistic missiles from North Korea's eastern coastal town of Wonsan on Thursday (October 29). They were North Korea's first ballistic weapons firings in 17 days.

Tensions between the two Koreas have been running high since last month's land mine blasts at their border that wounded three South Korean soldiers. Seoul accused North Korea of burying the mines south of the military demarcation line and demanded an apology. But Pyongyang has denied responsibility for the explosions and warned of retaliation if provoked.
Last week, North Korea threatened to resume propaganda loudspeaker broadcasts and place new weapons systems along the border.

North Korea has pulled out of talks with the U.S. and South Korea after Mr. Kim's high-stakes diplomacy with U.S. President Donald Trump collapsed in 2019. In recent weeks, North Korea has dialled up weapons testing activities in a likely attempt to boost its leverage in potential diplomacy with the U.S. after Trump expressed his eagerness to restore talks with Mr. Kim.

On Saturday (October 24), Mr. Kim made a surprise visit to a Chinese border town via a newly opened bridge and vowed to develop bilateral ties. Mr. Kim has recently taken steps to cement ties with China, North Korea's economic pipeline, after years of prioritising ties with Russia, including by supplying thousands of troops and ammunition, likely in return for economic and military assistance.

Meanwhile, Switzerland's Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis arrived in North Korea on Thursday (October 29) to see the reopening of Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang and meet North Korean officials. He is travelling on to South Korea on Friday (October 20).

articles.title: Nvidia's web of AI bets: smart strategy or bubble risk?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: investments have raised a nagging question among some doubters on Wall Street: is Nvidia helping to inflate an AI bubble?

Nvidia's $3 billion investment in Meta's share sale, announced Tuesday, is the latest addition to a portfolio of stakes, loans and guarantees that has made the chip giant what some analysts describe as the central bank of the artificial intelligence boom.
The galaxy of deals has helped keep demand running high for Nvidia's processors, which power vast data centres around the world and are the central ingredient of the AI revolution.
That demand has made Nvidia the world's most valuable company by market capitalisation and turned chief executive Jensen Huang into AI's kingmaker.
But the investments have raised a nagging question among some doubters on Wall Street: is Nvidia helping to inflate an AI bubble?
Nvidia has taken stakes in leading AI developers including OpenAI, Anthropic and Elon Musk's xAI, now part of SpaceX.
It has also invested in "neocloud" companies such as CoreWeave and Nebius, which rent out computing power built on Nvidia chips.

Its bets extend well beyond the United States. In Europe, Nvidia has backed French AI developer Mistral and British self-driving startup Wayve. In Asia, it has teamed up with South Korea's SK Group to build data centers.
Beyond equity, the company has offered financial backstops, acting as a customer of last resort.
In CoreWeave's case, Nvidia committed to buy up to $6.3 billion of unused computing capacity if no other customer takes it.
Nvidia also has around $36 billion in cloud backstops and a guarantee of up to $105 billion linked to an OpenAI data centre, according to US media.
Experts say Nvidia's enormous profits give it few better options.
"They're essentially becoming a bank," said Michael Cusumano, a professor at the MIT Sloan School of Management.

articles.title: Nutritional deficiencies, alcohol intake linked to venous stroke in Karnataka: NIMHANS study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The researchers found that CVT patients were more likely to have diets deficient in protein and folate. Elevated homocysteine levels, anaemia and alcohol consumption were also common among those diagnosed with the condition

articles.title: Tech firms take fresh hit as earnings misses fan AI fears
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The announcements came a day after Google parent Alphabet reported soft growth in revenue from advertising and its search business
Tech firms were again on the back foot Friday after another round of disappointing earnings from Wall Street titans fanned already deep concerns about the AI investment boom.
Traders were also keeping an eye on bitcoin, which tumbled after the world's largest crypto exchange said it had been hit by what analysts warned could be the biggest hack of its kind in the world.

AI-linked tech firms suffered steep losses after Amazon's quarterly report fell short of analyst expectations on profit and revenue, and Intel's expected income missed estimates owing to weak demand for PC processors and supply-chain problems.
The announcements came a day after Google parent Alphabet reported soft growth in revenue from advertising and its search business , while saying it would ramp up capital expenditure.

Alphabet plunged more than 12 percent, while Amazon tanked more than seven percent in after-hours trade, having lost more than four percent before the close, while Intel cratered 23 percent. The Nasdaq finished down more than one percent.
And the selling continued in Asia, where South Korean chipmaker SK hynix dived almost nine percent and rival Samsung lost more than six percent.
Japanese semiconductor firm Kioxia shed more than nine percent, as did Advantest, while SoftBank skidded around seven percent.
"This earnings season has been tough on AI players, with most getting punished against a backdrop of AI bubble and inflation fears," Anna Wu, of Floodlines Research, said.
"The concern isn't that AI demand has already slowed. It's that higher funding costs and credit risk could eventually force hyperscalers to slow their build-out."
The selloff hit most broader markets in the region, with Seoul diving more than five percent, Tokyo shedding more than two percent and Taipei more than three percent.
There were also losses in Shanghai, Singapore and Manila, though Hong Kong, Sydney and Wellington rose.

Friday's retreat was a far cry from the optimism seen earlier in the week, when SK hynix said operating profit soared 632 percent and AI giant Anthropic reported a first-half revenue surge of about 1,300 percent in its IPO filing.

articles.title: Retired IPS officer and former APSRTC chief N. Balasubramanyam dies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu recalls him as an officer of uncompromising integrity

Former IPS officer and former Vice-Chairman and Managing Director of the Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) N. Balasubramanyam died late on Thursday (October 29, 2026) night while undergoing treatment in the United States.

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu condoled Mr. Balasubramanyam’s death. In a post on X, he said: “Deeply saddened by the passing of retired DGP (Rank officer) N. Balasubramanyam garu. An officer of uncompromising integrity, he earned respect for his firm decisions, progressive ideas and unwavering commitment to public service. Throughout his distinguished career in policing, intelligence, transport and public administration, he championed reform, innovation and the use of technology to serve people better. He encouraged out-of-the-box thinking and involved his team in decision-making, fostering a spirit of shared responsibility.

Deeply saddened by the passing of retired DGP Shri N. Balasubramanyam garu. An officer of uncompromising integrity, he earned respect for his firm decisions, progressive ideas and unwavering commitment to public service. Throughout his distinguished career in policing, intelligence, transport and public administration, he championed reform, innovation and the use of technology to serve people better. He encouraged out-of-the-box thinking and involved his team in decision-making, fostering a spirit of shared responsibility. Andhra Pradesh continued to benefit from his experience and dedication until just a few months ago. He fought his illness with extraordinary courage and determination. His passing is a profound loss, but his contributions and the inspiration he gave the police force will endure. My heartfelt condolences to his family, friends and colleagues. Om Shanti.

Expressing grief over his death, APSRTC Chairman Konakalla Narayana Rao said Mr. Balasubramanyam’s death was a great loss to the organisation and to the officers and employees who had worked with him. He recalled his contributions to the corporation during his tenure as its Vice-Chairman and Managing Director, particularly in strengthening administration, improving passenger services and promoting employee welfare.

Describing him as a dedicated and disciplined officer with strong administrative skills, Mr. Konakalla said his services to the public transport sector would remain memorable. He also recalled Mr. Balasubramanyam’s commitment to public service and his humane approach towards employees. He conveyed his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family and prayed for the departed soul to rest in peace.

Education and IT Minister Nara Lokesh also expressed shock over Mr. Balasubramanyam’s death and paid tributes to his memory. Describing him as a straightforward person who discharged his duties with dedication and integrity, Mr. Lokesh said his services would remain memorable. He conveyed his deepest condolences to the family members and prayed for strength to them in this hour of grief.
He was a 1994-batch IPS officer of the Andhra Pradesh cadre and known as a ‘no-nonsense’ officer.
Mr. Balasubramanyam, fondly referred to as Balu by his contemporaries, served as Superintendent of Police for Nalgonda and Mahbubnagar districts, now in Telangana.

He also worked as Inspector-General (Intelligence), Transport Commissioner and Director-General of Police (Organisation) in Andhra Pradesh. He also served as chief executive officer of e-Pragati and the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS). He was appointed Vice-Chairman and Managing Director of the APSRTC in early 2026.

articles.title: Telangana’s minimum temperature between 18℃ and 25℃ on October 30 morning; 22.2℃ in GHMC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Thunderstorms were forecast in 11 Telangana districts between afternoon on Friday and morning on Saturday

Temperatures in Telangana, which dropped under the impact of cyclonic storm Arnab , continue to be relatively low as the minimum temperatures between 18℃ and 25℃ were recorded in various parts of the State on Friday (October 30, 2026) morning.

The minimum temperature — recorded at 8.30 am. — in Medak was 18.8℃, followed by 19.7℃ in Adilabad, 20.2℃ in Dundigal, 20.5℃ in Hanumakonda and 20.6℃ in Khammam, as per India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centre’s weather information.
In Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) limits, the minimum temperature of 22.2℃ was recorded in Patancheru, 22.5℃ in Rajendranagar, 22.6℃ in Hayatnagar and 23.4℃ in Begumpet.
The maximum temperature was 34℃ in Mahabubnagar, and it was 32℃ in Begumpet (GHMC).

The temperatures may continue to be low as 11 districts were forecast to receive thunderstorms between afternoon on Friday and morning on Saturday. India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centre in its seven-day forecast has predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightening and gusty winds as very likely at isolated places in Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Nalgonda, Suryapet, Mahabubabad, Warangal, Hanumakonda, Jangaoan, Siddipet and Yadadri Bhunavanagiri districts.

The Madras High Court on Friday (October 31, 2026) ordered notice to the Centre on a public interest litigation (PIL) petition, which sought a direction to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to probe into the nationality of Saurav Das, co-convenor of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), and cancel his passport and Aadhaar card if he is not found to be an Indian.

The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan also ordered notice to Mr. Das on the PIL petition filed by R. Ganesh Kumar, a businessman from Chennai, who has also sought to block the X and Instagram handles of Mr. Das and prevent him from making derogatory statements against Supreme Court judges.

In an affidavit filed through his counsel B. Jagannath, the PIL petitioner alleged that “the actual name of Mr. Das was Yogesh Sharma” and that he has “roots in Nepal.” The litigant accused the CJP leader of having concealed those details to “fraudulently” obtain an Aadhaar card, passport, and voter ID in India. He claimed that the material facts had been deliberately suppressed.

“The said Respondent No. 06 [Mr. Das] has no genuine work. He is a jobless person self-styled to be a representative of the CJP and has used his social media handle to spread hatred amongst the youth with false and unsubstantiated allegations. One does not know how many passports the said Saurav Das is in possession of. In the interest of the nation, a deeper probe... needs to be undertaken,” the affidavit read.

Listing several social media posts in which Mr. Das had criticised the judiciary, the litigant said that he, “most definitely”, must be receiving funding from abroad and that only an investigation would reveal his sources of funding. The petitioner further accused the CJP leader of having used his social media handles “only for the purpose of creating chaos, anarchy, disenchantment, and hatred against the ruling establishment.”

“The Twitter [now X] handle of the said person along with the Instagram feed is only about abuse of judiciary and has radical communist leaning glorifying the radical leftists which highlight the fact that the said Yogesh Sharma [Mr. Das] is a Communist. Furthermore, he has called during the said Jantar Mantar protest to ‘storm the Parliament’ on the back of a protest called as reform in education,” the litigant added.

articles.title: Balasubrahmanyam takes over as Vice-Chairman and Managing Director of APSRTC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: He emphasises the need to strengthen public transport and enhance the quality of services provided to passengers
Senior IPS officer N. Balasubrahmanyam formally assumed charge as Vice-Chairman and Managing Director of the Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) on Friday.

Executive Director (Administration) K. S. Brahmananda Reddy and others greeted him at the RTC House. Interacting with them, Mr. Balaaubrahmanyam insisted that top priority would be given to passenger safety, punctuality, cleanliness and improvement of services. He emphasised the need to strengthen public transport and enhance the quality of services provided to passengers.

He also highlighted the need to introduce eco-friendly electric buses to improve operational efficiency and ensure financial stability of the APSRTC. Mr. Balasubrahmanyam appealed to the officials and employees to work with dedication and discipline ensuring team work to strengthen APSRTC and to provide better services to the public.

APSRTC Executive Directors A. Appala Raju (Operations) and G. V. Ravi Varma (Engineering), Chief Personnel Manager V.V. Sreedhar, senior officers, supervisors and representatives of various associations were present.

articles.title: CEC row LIVE updates: INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar postponed
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The INDIA bloc was expected to hold a “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s official residence

Inviting people from all walks of life to join the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally, Rahul Gandhi stated that Home Minister Amit Shah is “trying his best” to stop people from other States - U.P., Haryana, Rajasthan, Telangana, Punjab - who want to join the rally in Delhi.
“Now you watch what happens at Ramlila ground,” he asserted. “There is huge anger and emotional pain because large numbers are being disenfranchised,” he added.
The INDIA bloc, led by the Congress, plans to hold a rally at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on Sunday (November 1, 2026) to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The INDIA bloc’s proposed “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar has been postponed to October 31 due to rain, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said.
Addressing a press conference in Delhi, he added that the decision was taken by consensus considering that senior leaders will be uncomfortable in the current weather condition.
Sources said the postponement was due to weather conditions, as the lawns got muddy due to rains in New Delhi
INDIA bloc postpones the public impeachment of CEC Gyanesh Kumar to Oct 31 due to muddy lawns from rain in New Delhi.

Security preparations are under way for the Opposition’s November 1 ‘Chalo Dilli’ event at Ramlila Maidan. Delhi Police will deploy over 3,000 personnel and instal more than 200 CCTV cameras, including AI-enabled surveillance systems, ahead of the protest, said an officer. The venue, which will host its first major demonstration since the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a protest site on October 11, has been divided into 14 zones to manage protesters.

In a letter to Sonia Gandhi, the traders’ body said the proposed rally, which is expected to draw 10 lakh people, could affect business worth ₹10,000-12,000 crore in wholesale and retail markets in central and old Delhi during the peak festive season
CTI urges delaying Congress rally to protect Delhi markets, citing ₹10,000-₹12,000 crore at risk during Diwali peak.

The Congress president’s official residence was decided as the venue after the Opposition bloc’s attempts to organise the event at the Ashok Hotel and Ramlila Maidan allegedly ran into hurdles over permissions.

articles.title: Marco Rubio hosts G20 Foreign Ministers as Iran, Ukraine wars divide members
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: “Conversations in Atlanta will provide an opportunity to discuss energy and supply chain challenges as well as identify ways to collectively address the impact of geopolitical tensions on economic security,” a U.S. State Department official said

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will host his G20 counterparts, including Russia's Sergei Lavrov, for talks on Friday (October 30, 2026) that are expected to be fractious, with wars in Ukraine and Iran and surging energy prices fanning discord.

The Foreign Ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Georgia, taking place just days before crucial U.S. midterm elections, will set the stage for a December G20 leaders' summit in Miami at President Donald Trump's Doral resort.

Few breakthroughs are expected this week from the Group of 20 economies, which include China, India, Russia, Japan, Germany and France, as officials face divisions over Moscow's war on Ukraine and fallout from conflict with Iran.
Russia has been shunned by most of the West after its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, and Mr. Lavrov himself remains under international sanctions.

Mr. Rubio's encounter with Mr. Lavrov , whose presence adds an additional layer of tension, will be closely watched as Washington pursues diplomacy on Ukraine while seeking Moscow's cooperation on reining in fuel prices , a key campaign issue in the midterms.
Donald Trump defends Russia diesel deal as lawmakers from both parties complain
Kremlin says a first tanker of Russian diesel sets sail for U.S. despite Ukraine's protests
"The G20 is no longer really a forum where Foreign Ministers can reach agreement on a statement," a diplomatic source said.

The source added that the U.S. G20 presidency intends for Miami's summit to serve "more as a demonstration of American power, and of U.S. commitments to growth, deregulation, trade and business, rather than as a summit with grand ambitions on substantive issues."
Instead of a final declaration, the source expects a chair summary drafted by the United States to be published from this week's meeting.
The Trump administration, which is set to hand the rotating G20 leadership to Britain, sees the platform as having strayed from its core mission.
Washington has pledged to return the grouping to its goal of driving economic growth, arguing that security and economic prosperity are "inextricably linked."

articles.title: Trump says Russia to immediately supply diesel to U.S. after talks with Putin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The surprise announcement comes against the backdrop of a U.S. law seeking to impose steep tariffs against top purchasers of Russian oil and gas
Russia will immediately supply diesel to the U.S., President Donald Trump announced on Friday (October 9, 2026) after talks with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin.

Trump announced the deal on Friday after a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, a move that drew sharp criticism from Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Democratic leaders and a section of Republicans.
The surprise announcement comes against the backdrop of a U.S. law seeking to impose steep tariffs against top purchasers of Russian oil and gas.

“I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace,” Mr. Trump said in a post on Truth Social.

The announcement comes as the U.S. battles high fuel prices amid the war on Iran, which has become a key issue in the midterm elections on November 3.
Earlier, the U.S. Congress passed a law on September 16 to impose steep tariffs on top purchasers of Russian oil and gas.
Several opinion polls have predicted that it would be tough for the Republican Party to retain control of the U.S. Congress in the midterm elections.
Mr. Trump said the U.S.’ control of the Strait of Hormuz, along with the proposed Russian diesel supplies, would bring down fuel prices sharply.

“Between our total control TOTAL CONTROL of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST,” the U.S. President said.
Mr. Trump said lower prices for Americans, especially farmers, ranchers, and truckers, are his “greatest priority”.
“This is a very big and important announcement,” he said.

articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro reaches U.S., say reports citing sources
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Two media houses, each citing an unnamed source close to the matter, said Flavo Bolsonaro had arrived in the U.S. on October 27

Defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil for the United States despite a court order banning him from exiting the country, U.S. media reported on Tuesday October 27, 2026).
CNN and the Washington Post , each citing an unnamed source close to the matter, said Mr. Bolsonaro had arrived in the U.S. late Tuesday (October 27, 2026). Where he landed remains unknown.
The son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro lost the presidential election Sunday (October 25, 2026) to incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and refused to concede defeat.

The right-wing senator on Monday (October 26, 2026) said a Supreme Court justice had ordered him to hand over his passports. Mr. Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering, and, with his election loss is also set to lose parliamentary immunity.
The U.S. State Department said Tuesday (October 27, 2026) it would issue visas to Mr. Bolsonaro and his family, without confirming his travel plans.
A police source told AFP that the senator’s Brazilian and diplomatic passports had been cancelled, adding that “there is no formal record of Flavio Bolsonaro leaving the country.”
But he has held Italian nationality since 2023, according to an Italian parliamentary document seen by AFP .
Mr. Bolsonaro’s campaign manager Rogerio Marinho expressed shock over reports that the defeated candidate had fled Brazil.
“We still don’t have any news about his whereabouts,” he told reporters Tuesday (October 27, 3036) in Brasilia.
“I received a text message from him this morning, where he said he would let some time pass today and then would talk with us, and that was it,” Mr. Marinho said.
“A person who sneaks out of their country must have something to hide. The act of leaving Brazil is shameful,” he remarked in Brasilia during his 81st birthday celebration.
Mr. Bolsonaro said Monday (October 26, 2026) that the ban on his exit from Brazil amounted to a scare tactic.

articles.title: De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlapping procedures, but will it safeguard standards of medical education?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Under MSMER-2023, there was a defined escalation path; now, action depends on MARB assessments being initiated, completed and acted upon within a reasonable timeframe

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has de-notified and withdrawn the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 (MSMER-2023) where medical colleges were liable to face penalty fines for violations of educational standards and infrastructure requirements at medical colleges.

Earlier reports in The Hindu stated NMC’s withdrawal of MSMER-2023 weakens accountability in medical education by removing provisions to fine individual faculty members and administrators up to ₹5 lakh for submitting false information. Although the Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) can still penalise institutions up to ₹1 crore under separate regulations, institutional penalties may be less effective in deterring individual misconduct. Misleading faculty declarations, inflated patient records, or inadequate clinical training going undetected could ultimately put patients at risk.

articles.title: 12-year-old girl kills four-year-old boy in Madhya Pradesh over chocolate dispute, say police
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police say the girl pushed the child into a water tank after being scolded by his mother over a chocolate

A 12-year-old girl allegedly killed a four-year-old boy by pushing him into a water tank after becoming angry with the child’s mother for scolding her over a chocolate in Madhya Pradesh’s Mandsaur district, police said on Friday (October 30, 2026).
The incident took place on October 26 in Shamgarh town, when the girl allegedly took the boy to the roof of her house, pushed him into a water tank and covered it with a stone slab.
An FIR has been registered in the case, and the girl was sent to a government juvenile home after being produced before a court.
Mandsaur Superintendent of Police Vinod Meena told The Hindu that the boy’s body remained in the tank for about three hours before the girl’s father discovered it.

“The boy’s parents had complained of the boy being missing so as per the usual procedure, we started a search and alerted the neighbours to look for the boy on their roofs and in water bodies. The girl’s father found him in the tank on his roof. He was completely unaware of what his daughter had done,” Mr. Meena said.
The boy’s family lived as tenants in the adjacent house owned by the girl’s uncle.
Mr. Meena said the police spoke to children in the neighbourhood during the search, following which the girl confessed to the crime.

“As per her statement, the girl had taken a chocolate the boy was eating after which his mother had scolded her badly. She had been upset over something the woman may have said and carried the anger for 7-8 days before carrying out the act,” the officer said.

The FIR was registered under the Juvenile Justice Act on October 28, after the post-mortem findings corroborated the girl’s statement, Mr. Meena said, adding that legal action was being taken as per the law.
The post-mortem report stated that the cause of death was ante-mortem drowning.

articles.title: BJP targets Rahul Gandhi over past remarks on Hindutva, questions Congress on ECI appointment process
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The BJP questioned the Congress over its criticism of the process of appointment of chief election commissioners, claiming that during the Congress rule, there was neither a law nor a committee for selecting election commissioners
Posting a video of past remarks by Rahul Gandhi on Hindutva, Hinduism and religious figures, the BJP alleged the Congress leader "pretends" to be a Hindu when elections are near.

This comes days after Mr. Gandhi posted a picture of a 'Tripund Tilak', a sacred mark associated with Lord Shiva, and captioned it 'Satyam Shivam Sundaram', after he was acquitted by the MP-MLA court in Sultanpur in the defamation case related to his remarks against the then BJP president Amit Shah in 2018.

The BJP shared a video on social media that first showed Mr. Gandhi's X post, followed by clips from his speeches on Hindutva and Hinduism as a comparison. The song 'Kya Hua Tera Wada' played in the background.
"If you hate Hindus so much, why pretend to be a Hindu every time elections come around, Rahul ji?" read the caption on X.
In one of the clips, Mr. Gandhi is heard saying, "We have to throw these Hindutvavadis (Hindutva supporters) out once again."
In another, he says, "Those who call themselves Hindus are engaged in violence, violence, violence, 24 hours a day. Hatred, hatred, hatred. Lies, lies, lies."
"People go to temples, bow their heads and worship the goddess. Yet, these very same people harass you on buses. These very same people oppress you," he is heard saying in another clip.
The video also features the Congress leader saying, "All are mythological figures. Lord Ram belonged to that era, right?"

The BJP, in another post on X, questioned the Congress over its criticism of the process of appointment of chief election commissioners, claiming that during the Congress rule, there was neither a law nor a committee for selecting election commissioners and that the Prime Minister and the Cabinet decided the names without consulting the leader of opposition.

articles.title: Chopper with six on board crashes near Uttarakhand’s Joshimath
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rescue operations under way; the helicopter, belonging to a private company, was returning to Dehradun from Badrinath when it crashed around 2.20 p.m., officials said

A helicopter on the way from Badrinath to Dehradun carrying six people, including the pilot, crashed near Joshimath on Friday afternoon (October 30, 2026), Uttarakhand disaster management officials said.
Rescue operations are currently under way and there has been no official confirmation regarding casualties. One pilot and five passengers were on board.

The helicopter, belonging to a private company, was returning to Dehradun from Badrinath when it crashed around 2.20 p.m. near Chai village in Chamoli district’s Joshimath area, officials said. The helicopter that belonged to ‘Trans Bharat Aviation’ crashed into a hillside near the JP Power House, they added.

चाई गांव, जोशीमठ के निकट हेलीकॉप्टर क्रैश होने की दुर्भाग्यपूर्ण सूचना प्राप्त हुई है। जिला प्रशासन, आपदा प्रबंधन विभाग, एसडीआरएफ द्वारा संयुक्त रूप से रेस्क्यू ऑपरेशन चलाया जा रहा है। स्वयं भी पूरे घटनाक्रम की निरंतर निगरानी कर रहा हूं। गंभीर रूप से घायलों को तत्काल एयरलिफ्ट कर बेहतर उपचार हेतु हायर सेंटर पहुंचाने के निर्देश दिए हैं। ईश्वर से यात्रियों के सकुशल होने की कामना करता हूं।

Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, in a post on X, said: “Reports have been received regarding an unfortunate helicopter crash near Chai village, close to Joshimath. A joint rescue operation is being conducted by the district administration, the Disaster Management Department, and the SDRF.

“I am personally monitoring the situation closely. I have issued instructions to ensure that those who are critically injured are immediately airlifted to a higher-level medical facility for better treatment. I pray to God for the safety of the passengers,” he added.

articles.title: Underweight rice bags, uncertified scales among violations at Hyderabad’s 10 rice outlets
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana Civil Supplies Department officials detected violations at 10 rice retail outlets during checks taken up in Hyderabad on Thursday (October 29, 2026). The violations include rice bags having less than stated weight, using uncertified weighing machines and not having necessary trade licenses. The stores are located in Amberpet, Khairatabad, Secunderabad, Mehdipatnam and Nampally circles.

The checks were taken up after two-rounds of meetings between the department’s officials and wholesalers & retail traders on high prices of the food grains. One of the meetings was with millers from Nalgonda, Miryalguda and Nizamabad — districts which are large sources of paddy for the State.

During the checks on Thursday, officials from Hyderabad Chief Ration Officer detected rice bags at a store weighed 1.040 kg less than the stated weight of 26 kgs. A similar issue was found at another store.Three stores did not have required trade licences. Officials said that action was taken up against businesspersons under relevant laws and rules.

articles.title: Maharashtra government releases ₹90.72 lakh for plantation upkeep amid drought in 304 talukas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The funds for the fourth-year upkeep of ‘Panchayat Van’, ‘Bel Van’ and ‘Amrit Van’ plantations are conditional on at least 90% sapling survival.

The Maharashtra government has sanctioned ₹90.72 lakh for the upkeep of tree plantations across the State amid drought affecting 304 of its 358 talukas, with at least 90% sapling survival made a prerequisite for the release of funds.

According to a Government Resolution (GR) issued by the Revenue and Forest Department on Thursday (October 29, 2026), the money has been allocated for the fourth-year maintenance of ‘Panchayat Van’, ‘Bel Van’ and ‘Amrit Van’ plantations under a State scheme for 2026-27.

The funds will cover plantations spread across 227 hectares in various districts. The highest allocation of ₹42.80 lakh has been made to the Pune forest circle, followed by ₹20.80 lakh for Nagpur and ₹20.76 lakh for Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.

The GR says that funding will be available only for plantation sites where at least 90% of saplings remain alive. Local self-help groups and biodiversity management committees will undertake the maintenance, protection and upkeep work.

The allocation comes amid concerns over water availability following poor rainfall this year. The Maharashtra government has declared 304 of the State’s 358 talukas drought-affected, prompting measures to address water scarcity and support affected areas.

The State government on Monday (October 26, 2026) issued an order for soil and water conservation works in 304 talukas where drought-related triggers had been activated during the 2026 Kharif season. The measures included constructing water absorption pits, desilting water bodies and repairing check dams.

The latest GR has asked the Additional Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (Budget, Planning and Development), Maharashtra, to ensure compliance with the prescribed conditions and submit a utilisation certificate for the released funds within seven days.

In 2023, the State launched an afforestation initiative under the ‘Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav’ to mark the 75th anniversary of Independence. The scheme aims to expand green cover and strengthen ecological stability across urban and rural areas as well as religious sites in the State.
The initiative comprises three components — Amrit Van, Panchayat Van and Bel Van — targeting urban centres, villages and prominent pilgrimage sites, respectively.

The Amrit Van component aims to establish dedicated urban forestry gardens in 75 major cities and key urban centres by developing local government or forest department land with indigenous tree species. The Panchayat Van initiative seeks to develop woodland clusters in 25 selected villages in every district, featuring five culturally significant and ecologically suitable tree species to promote biodiversity.

The Bel Van component focuses on plantations at 75 prominent pilgrimage and religious sites across Maharashtra. These plantations include sacred and medicinal species such as bael, Sita Ashok, rudraksha, ber and swastik plants, integrating environmental conservation with the State’s religious and cultural landscape.

articles.title: Drone strikes kill 14, including children, in Ethiopia's Amhara: witnesses
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The strikes at the camp occurred just as the students were coming home from school, recounted Ahmed, one of the two other witnesses

At least 14 people, including children, were killed in several drone strikes on Thursday (October 29, 2026) on a camp for displaced people in Ethiopia's Amhara region, three witnesses told AFP on Friday (October 30).

"Four drone strikes were carried out one after another. We have buried 14 people at the IDP centre. Two more died while receiving medical treatment," said Yasin, who requested anonymity, adding that pregnant women and children were among the victims.
Two other residents of the camp, one of whom said he had buried bodies, reported 14 and 15 deaths respectively, including several children.
The strikes at the camp, 400 kilometres (250 miles) northeast of Addis Ababa, occurred "just as the students were coming home from school," recounted Ahmed, one of the two other witnesses.
"My sister-in-law was killed, and we couldn't even find her body because it was dismembered," he said.
The NGO Acled, which specialises in collecting and analysing data on armed conflicts, said between "16 and 23 people were killed, and an unknown number of people were injured."
It did not provide details as to whether children were among the victims.

Forces from Addis Ababa have carried out numerous drone strikes in Amhara, Ethiopia's second most populous region with more than 20 million inhabitants and where nearly half a million people are displaced, according to figures published by the United Nations in July.
Questioned by AFP , the spokesperson for the Ethiopian federal army has so far not responded.
According to the witnesses, the displaced people are originally from Oromia, the region neighbouring Amhara and the most populous in the country.
The Oromo Liberation Army (OLA), designated a terrorist organisation by Addis Ababa, has been waging an armed struggle in the region against federal forces for more than eight years.

Drone strikes kill 14, including children, in Ethiopia's Amhara: witnesses

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics

The strikes at the camp occurred just as the students were coming home from school, recounted Ahmed, one of the two other witnesses

At least 14 people, including children, were killed in several drone strikes on Thursday (October 29, 2026) on a camp for displaced people in Ethiopia's Amhara region, three witnesses told AFP on Friday (October 30).

"Four drone strikes were carried out one after another. We have buried 14 people at the IDP centre. Two more died while receiving medical treatment," said Yasin, who requested anonymity, adding that pregnant women and children were among the victims.

Two other residents of the camp, one of whom said he had buried bodies, reported 14 and 15 deaths respectively, including several children.

The strikes at the camp, 400 kilometres (250 miles) northeast of Addis Ababa, occurred "just as the students were coming home from school," recounted Ahmed, one of the two other witnesses.

"My sister-in-law was killed, and we couldn't even find her body because it was dismembered," he said.

The NGO Acled, which specialises in collecting and analysing data on armed conflicts, said between "16 and 23 people were killed, and an unknown number of people were injured."

It did not provide details as to whether children were among the victims.

Forces from Addis Ababa have carried out numerous drone strikes in Amhara, Ethiopia's second most populous region with more than 20 million inhabitants and where nearly half a million people are displaced, according to figures published by the United Nations in July.

Questioned by AFP , the spokesperson for the Ethiopian federal army has so far not responded.

According to the witnesses, the displaced people are originally from Oromia, the region neighbouring Amhara and the most populous in the country.

The Oromo Liberation Army (OLA), designated a terrorist organisation by Addis Ababa, has been waging an armed struggle in the region against federal forces for more than eight years.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Oromo Liberation Army (OLA), designated a terrorist organisation by Addis Ababa, has been waging an armed struggle in the region against federal forces for more than eight years.

articles.title: New York restricts AI chatbot interactions with children | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Governor Kathy Hochul signed two laws on October 28 barring AI chatbots from harmful interactions with minors, including simulating romantic relationships and promoting self-harm, and requiring security safeguards in internet-connected baby monitors

The story so far: “As a mother and grandmother, I believe kids deserve to be kids, without dangerous AI chatbots putting their safety and mental health at risk,...Big Tech, you’re on notice,” New York Governor Kathy Hochul wrote on social media after signing two bills on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) aimed at protecting children from the risks associated with artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots and internet-connected baby monitors.

The legislation prohibits AI chatbots from engaging in potentially harmful interactions with minors, including simulating romantic relationships, encouraging emotional dependency, and promoting self-harm. It also requires manufacturers of internet-connected baby monitors to introduce safeguards against unauthorised access to audio and video feeds.

articles.title: Spain train crash: Indian Embassy in Madrid issues helpline after deadly accident
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: After the Spain train crash, the Indian Embassy in Madrid issued the emergency helpline number +34 650 339 008, the email cons.madrid@mea.gov.in, and Renfe: 900 10 10 20, and Iryo: 900 001 403
A high-speed train collision south of Madrid in Spain killed at least 68 people and injured scores of people on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) , with the death toll expected to rise, authorities said.
Indian Embassy in Madrid has opened an emergency helpline for its nationals after the accident — one of Europe’s deadliest rail disasters this century.

The Indian Embassy in Madrid advised Indian nationals who were travelling on the affected trains, as well as their family members, to contact the mission for immediate assistance. In an advisory posted on its official X account, the Embassy urged people to share details of its emergency helpline with anyone requiring support.
The embassy issued the emergency helpline number +34 650 339 008, the email cons.madrid@mea.gov.in, and Renfe: 900 10 10 20, and Iryo: 900 001 403.

The collision occurred in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha on Wednesday (October 29) morning when a train operated by state-owned Renfe crashed into the rear of a stationary train belonging to private operator Iryo.
ALSO WATCH Deadly train collision in Spain: What we know so far

The second major rail accident to hit Spain in 2026 is likely to renew scrutiny of the country’s railway safety systems, with Transport Minister Óscar Puente referring to an “error” and “inexplicable circumstances” that preceded the crash. The accident involved a Renfe AVE service and an Iryo train travelling from Madrid to Seville. The impact caused the rear coaches of the Iryo train to derail and plunge down an embankment near kilometre marker 118.

Mr. Puente said preliminary assessments suggested a possible technical failure at the Atocha control centre involving the LZB safety system, though he stressed that the exact cause remained under investigation.

According to the Minister, an automatic train-control system failed over a 69-kilometre stretch of track, resulting in services being halted. However, the control centre later authorised the resumption of traffic despite the disruption.

“The control centre decided to resume traffic in circumstances that, from our point of view, are inexplicable,” Mr. Puente said, adding that the Renfe train travelled around 25 kilometres before colliding with the stationary Iryo service.
He said the Renfe train had resumed operations about 15 minutes earlier and may have been travelling at speeds of up to 200 kmph at the time of the impact.

Following the collision, several coaches derailed and tumbled down a steep embankment. Debris and twisted metal were strewn across the crash site, and some carriages appeared to have suffered severe structural damage.

articles.title: Hospital review of 578 patients finds 82.5% of breast conditions were cancerous
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A lump does not necessarily indicate cancer, but medical evaluation is needed to establish its cause and determine whether treatment or follow-up is required

A review of 578 patients who presented with breast-related concerns at the Head & Neck Cancer Institute of India (HNCII), Mumbai, over more than three years found that 82.5% had cancerous conditions and 17.5% had non-cancerous conditions. The diagnoses were confirmed through tissue examination.
The findings reveal patients assessed at the institute and cannot be generalised to the wider population or used to estimate the likelihood that a breast lump is cancerous.

Patients diagnosed with breast cancer ranged in age from 23 to 98 years, with an average age of 52.7 years. Tumour sizes varied, with 35.2% measuring up to 2 cm, 43.3% measuring between 2 and 4.9 cm, and 19.3% measuring more than 5 cm.

The institute also reported that 52% of patients had more than four lymph nodes positive for cancer. Lymph node involvement is one of the factors doctors consider when assessing the extent of breast cancer and planning treatment.
Mastectomy, which involves removing the breast, was the most common surgery recorded.
Recognising unusual breast changes and seeking medical advice can help establish a diagnosis and guide appropriate care. Not every lump requires cancer treatment, but changes should be assessed .

articles.title: Indian scientists find new gateway in plants’ alarm system
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Insect pests cause roughly 20% of global annual crop losses, a figure projected to rise with warming, and crop protection still leans heavily on chemical insecticides. Learning how plants sense attack could point to crops that defend themselves better

Researchers at the National Institute of Plant Genome Research (NIPGR) here have identified a previously uncharacterised protein that helps a plant warn undamaged leaves when an insect attacks one of them.
This suggests that plants employ complex defence mechanisms and may have implications for designing crop chemicals under pest attack.

Like other living beings, plants don’t like to be preyed on, by other insects or herbivores. Scientists studying plant defence mechanisms have shown how, when a leaf is chewed, defence systems are activated.

articles.title: Odisha steps up rescue-and-relief operations; four helicopters airdrop food packets in flood-hit Ganjam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “Helicopters of the Indian Navy and Indian Coast Guard are engaged in the operation, where several areas remain cut off due to flooding,” officials said

“The Odisha government on Friday (October 30, 2026) intensified rescue-and-relief operations, deploying four defence helicopters to airdrop food packets in flood-hit Ganjam district, where thousands of people remain marooned for more than 24 hours following heavy rainfall triggered by cyclone Arnab,” officials said.

Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P. Patil said four helicopters had begun dropping food packets at 21 identified locations in the district, with personnel stationed there tasked with distributing them among stranded people.

“Helicopters of the Indian Navy and Indian Coast Guard are engaged in the operation, covering areas including Hinjilicut, Purushottampur, Seragada, Dharakote, Aska, Belaguntha, Bhanjanagar and Chikiti, where several areas remain cut off due to flooding,” officials said.

"The packets carry as much as 4,500 kg of grains, which will be dropped at one place and officials stationed there will later distribute them among the affected people," Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said.
A view of the National Highway No.16 in between Berhampur to Icchapuram in south Odisha’s Ganjam district aftermath of cyclone ‘Arnab”. Photo: Special Arrangement

“Other affected people are being provided cooked food by rescue teams, which are transporting supplies in boats,” he said. Mr. Pujari said more than 23,000 people were staying in relief camps, but the number of those marooned was considerably higher.
He said 40 trained personnel of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) would reach affected areas with cooked food to assist stranded people.
“Movement of boats to several locations had earlier been difficult due to strong water currents, but the situation had improved slightly on Friday (October 30, 2026),” he said.

“Of the 313 rescue teams deployed across the State, more than 100 are engaged in Ganjam and Gajapati districts,” the Minister said. “A central team will visit the State on November 2 to assess the damage caused by floods triggered by cyclone Arnab,” he added.
“Ganjam is the worst-affected district, while Gajapati and Kandhamal have also suffered damage. The government has not received any report of casualties so far,” Mr. Pujari said.
Meanwhile, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, who also holds the Water Resources portfolio, expressed concern over the unexpectedly heavy rainfall in Ganjam and Gajapati districts.
Mr. Majhi, accompanied by Mr. Pujari, left for an aerial assessment of the flood situation in the two districts on Friday afternoon.
